records.excerpt: OpenAI Calls for Another AI Development Pause: Key Industry Implications & Latest Updates English 中文 Deutsch Home Article OpenAI wants to hit the pause button again 36氪的朋友们 2026-11-23 10:59 Players want to be referees. The more capable the model is, the more voices calling for a "pause" in development emerge. On November 22 local time in the United States, Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist of OpenAI, published an article titled "Perplexity and Intelligence", disclosing the pre-training data that the company has tracked for many years, and proposing to establish common standards for the AI industry. Pachocki hopes that all cutting-edge model companies will use a unified metric to measure model capabilities, and will not break the agreed capability threshold before the safety monitoring capabilities meet the requirements. This proposal has also received the support of Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI. A number related to intelligence The core of Pachocki's article is the so-called "Perplexity". Pachocki refers to the mechanism by which the model predicts tokens as training a Compressor — the model extracts patterns from data and uses less information to accurately predict what will happen next. Perplexity measures exactly this predictive capability. The more accurate the model's prediction is, the lower the perplexity will be . What OpenAI actually announced is log perplexity, that is, Cross-Entropy Loss, and the value is also the lower the better. According to the internal data released by Pachocki, the log perplexity of GPT-3.5 is about 0.99, and that of GPT-4 is about 0.91 . The former can already support smooth conversations, while the latter begins to effectively perform reasoning using Chain of Thought (CoT). After the latest GPT-6 version, the perplexity index has dropped below 0.8 . Pachocki said that the model has begun to demonstrate new capabilities in fields such as mathematics and cybersecurity. One of the changes occurs when the log perplexity drops to around 0.76 — researchers found that at this point, the model begins to continuously solve some challenging mathematical problems. Pachocki mentioned that researchers once saw the model in Slack solve problems one after another that they had been thinking about for years. These performances are not specifically trained for a single problem, but results that appear after the underlying capabilities of the model are improved. Pachocki emphasized that this is also the reason why he values perplexity. The key reason is that this value is not directly related to whether the model can complete tasks, but reflects what changes have taken place in its ability to learn information from training data. We used to discuss intelligence emergence very often, the capability evolution brought about by the continuous decrease of perplexity can be understood as a kind of emergence. Boosting pre-training breakthroughs in 2027 In the past, model training methods were mainly proposed by human researchers and then verified through a large number of experiments. After AI began to participate in research, the situation may change: the model not only performs tasks arranged by researchers, but may also help find new algorithms, propose experimental schemes, and even contribute to the training methods themselves. He predicted that as early as 2027, AI may achieve a series of fundamental advances in the field of pre-training. The latest models have already begun to provide substantial design contributions in the R&D process. Pachocki revealed that OpenAI has observed a significant acceleration in the decline rate of pre-training loss this year. However, he also specifically noted that at this stage, this acceleration mainly comes from long-term research and computing power investment, and AI automation currently only contributes a small part. Pachocki also predicted that as the log perplexity further drops to 0.68 to 0.70, the model may demonstrate new capabilities that cannot be foreseen at present. However, taking perplexity as a common standard does not mean that the problem has been solved. Pachocki also admitted that this metric has limitations. First, different companies have different training data, data ratios and evaluation sets, so perplexity cannot be directly used for horizontal comparison. Second, perplexity cannot directly measure the performance of the model in specific tasks. The improvement of a model's predictive capability does not mean that it will make synchronous progress in all mathematics, programming and security tests. In addition, post-training technologies such as chain-of-thought reasoning will also change model capabilities, but they are not necessarily directly reflected in pre-training perplexity. There is another key problem: perplexity has a theoretical lower bound. As the model gets closer and closer to the information entropy contained in the training data, the decline of loss may gradually slow down. But this does not mean that the improvement of capabilities will stop. Even a very small change in the metric may correspond to a new capability breakthrough. Therefore, Pachocki does not advocate using only perplexity to judge whether a model is safe, but hopes to combine it with other metrics to form a set of common standards. To promote this work, OpenAI is willing to disclose more pre-training progress. Pachocki believes that cutting-edge model companies should share necessary transparency information , jointly evaluate model capabilities, and carry out cooperation in red team testing and safety standards. OpenAI and Closed AI After Pachocki published the article, Altman soon publicly expressed his support. "The most important thing released in recent period of time," Altman said. Altman said that OpenAI is improving the transparency of pre-training progress, and hopes to reach an agreement on common restrictions with other companies as partners. In his view, this not only helps to ensure that AI is safe and controllable, but also promotes the establishment of common rules across the entire industry. Altman also agreed with the perplexity limit proposed by Pachocki. He hopes that all labs will establish common constraints around perplexity and other measurement indicators, and will not cross the pre-set capability threshold before researchers truly have the ability to understand and monitor AI behaviors. The example he cited is the development of the next generation of CoT Monitors. In his view, the industry should first clarify the first capability limit, and then agree on what safety work must be completed before breaking through this limit. However, Altman's support has not dispelled the doubts from the outside world. The first thing that was questioned was OpenAI's motivation to promote the industry to set common restrictions. Some netizens believe that whether OpenAI's emphasis on industry restrictions and safety standards at this time is also out of consideration for winning time for the competitiveness of its own models. Some people think that these statements are more like excuses used when model releases lag behind competitors. Others satirized Altman's frequent use of the word "transparency", saying that if OpenAI really wants to improve transparency, it should go open source , instead of continuing to ignore users' demands for model continuity. Criticisms also involve OpenAI's corporate positioning. Some netizens directly suggested renaming OpenAI to ClosedAI, arguing that the company's current level of openness no longer lives up to its name . records.title: OpenAI Introduces 'Standby Discount' for Voice AI, Cutting Fees 60% During Silent Periods on Calls
records.excerpt: OpenAI has added its real-time voice model "GPT-Live-1.1" to its developer API and introduced a "Standby" feature that pauses inference when there is no voice activity during a call. During standby periods, the per-minute rate drops 60%, from $0.05 to $0.02. In a one-hour consultation with 20 minutes of conversation and 40 minutes of standby, the fee falls from $3 to $1.80. The discount applies only to the enterprise and developer API and is unrelated to ChatGPT subscription fees. The new model supports a Korean-language voice option called "noeul" and can handle interruptions. OpenAI has rolled out an enterprise real-time voice AI model along with a pricing system that sharply lowers fees during silent stretches of a call. The move is seen as a signal that the focus of competition in voice AI is shifting from "how naturally it speaks" to "how cheaply it can be operated." On the 19th (local time), OpenAI added the real-time voice model "GPT-Live-1.1" to its developer API. Enterprises and developers can use the model to build AI customer service centers, phone reservation services, and in-vehicle voice assistants. The new model improves the consistency of multilingual pronunciation and intonation over the previous GPT-Live-1 and also enhances speech recognition accuracy. OpenAI says it is particularly useful for tasks that require the accurate exchange of letters and numbers, such as customer names and verification codes. Conversation flow has also become more flexible. If a customer interrupts or asks an additional question while the AI is answering, the AI listens and responds. Complex tasks are handed off to other AI models or the company's internal systems. For example, if a customer inquires about a flight, the AI consults the reservation system for the schedule and relays the result while continuing the conversation. It also supports a Korean-language voice option called "noeul." The centerpiece of the announcement is "Standby." At AI customer service centers, customers frequently stay silent for a while as they look up materials or complete a payment. Previously, normal fees could be charged if the connection was maintained even during such silent periods. Standby temporarily suspends the AI's inference work when no voice activity is detected for a developer-configured period of 5 to 60 seconds. The call connection and conversation record are maintained as-is, and the AI resumes operation immediately when the customer starts speaking again. The price difference is clear. Normal operation costs $0.05 per minute (~67 won), while standby drops to $0.02 per minute (~27 won), 60% lower. This applies not only to the new model but also to the existing GPT-Live-1. In a one-hour consultation with 20 minutes of actual conversation and 40 minutes of standby, the normal rate would come to $3 (~4,000 won), but using Standby reduces it to $1.80 (~2,400 won). That saves $1.20 per hour (~1,600 won), or 40% of the total voice session fee. Category Normal Operation Standby Per-minute rate $0.05 (~67 won) $0.02 (~27 won) One-hour consultation (20 min talk, 40 min standby) $3 (~4,000 won) $1.80 (~2,400 won) Savings - $1.20 (~1,600 won) Note: Based on simple calculation; actual savings vary depending on standby time and service configuration. Additional costs apply when using external AI models or task-processing tools. The discount applies only to API fees used by enterprises and developers. It is unrelated to the ChatGPT voice feature used by general users or to Plus and Pro subscription fees. Enterprises must also meet technical conditions to receive the discount. The $0.02 per-minute rate applies only when the standby feature is enabled on a connection based on WebRTC, a web real-time communication technology. If a developer does not configure this, the discount is not automatically applied even when the customer stops speaking. Some point out that it is too early to adopt the feature purely for cost savings. Because $0.02 per minute is still charged during standby, disconnecting may be more economical when silence runs long. There is also a possibility that the first response may be delayed when operation resumes from standby. Even if the AI announces an order change or reservation completion, it must be verified whether it was actually reflected in the system, and care must be taken to ensure that orders and reservations are not processed twice when a connection drops and recovers. In long conversations, some earlier content may be omitted, so it is safer to record customer consent and payment status separately. The personal information management system—including whether consultation records are stored, the retention period, and access permissions—should also be reviewed. Industry observers expect this pricing approach to change the benchmark for gauging the economics of voice AI adoption. At customer service centers that handle thousands to tens of thousands of calls a day, usage fees matter as much as voice quality. Billing that separates AI operating time from standby time can lower operating costs, making customer service centers with high call volumes and long customer wait times, as well as hospital and restaurant reservation services, emerge as priority demand sources. This is why some assess that the competitive benchmark in the voice AI market is broadening from conversational performance to operational efficiency.

records.title: Microsoft puts OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol in Copilot worldwide as MAI models push in
records.excerpt: Microsoft's admin notice for Copilot says GPT-6.2 Sol ships with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license, while Astra needs usage-based billing and an enabled The newest OpenAI model is now inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint, but the stronger one is fenced off behind a paid tier. Microsoft's own MAI models launched three days earlier, so the company is selling both sides at once. Microsoft said on Friday, November 20, that OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol is rolling out worldwide to eligible users in Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio, and Copilot in Excel, PowerPoint and Word, according to its Copilot blog on the Microsoft Tech Community site. GPT-6.2 Astra, the heavier model, goes to Cowork and Studio for everyone eligible, and reaches Chat and the Office apps only for users in Microsoft's Frontier program. So the line going around in digests, that every Office user got both models at once, isn't quite right. Sol is the one most people will see. Astra is the one you'll have to ask your admin about. Microsoft's own description is thin, but the pricing tells you the split. Per million tokens, Sol costs $2 for input and $10 for output on the API, while Astra costs $8 and $40, according to a Japanese-language summary of the announcement from Taiwan's Newmobilelife. Four times the price is the clue: Sol is the everyday model for drafting a memo or summarizing a thread, and Astra is meant for long, multi-step jobs where you'd pay for fewer wasted tokens. Both models run through Work IQ, which Microsoft says grounds them in a user's files, meetings, chats and business data while respecting existing permissions. Inside an Office tenant, that means the same model gives a different answer to your finance lead than to an intern: it only reads what each of them can already open. Satya Nadella says companies that rent their AI brains are making a strategic mistake they will regret Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has publicly warned enterprises against over-relying on foundation models from OpenAI and Anthropic, arguing that companies must build proprietary AI learning loops or risk ceding their core value to a handful of labs. The argument creates an obvious tension with Microsoft's roughly $13 billion investment in OpenAI, but... - companies building proprietary AI models - why renting AI models fails The admin paperwork is where the friction sits. Microsoft's Message Center notice MC1560916, summarized by MWPro, says both models use usage-based billing in supported services, and that Sol also ships with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user license. Using Astra broadly requires an administrator to switch on the OpenAI subprocessor setting. Microsoft added that OpenAI models operated by Microsoft through Azure OpenAI aren't affected by that setting. The notice rates the admin impact as high and tells IT teams to prepare support staff for usage-limit messages. Availability, Microsoft says, varies by region and organization, and the rollout was still marked in progress. If you run Copilot for a company, expect a ticket queue before expect a productivity jump. The hedge sitting next to the rollout The timing is awkward for anyone who reads Microsoft as OpenAI's loyal distributor. Three days earlier, at Ignite, Microsoft launched MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot. InfoWorld reported the launch as a challenge to OpenAI and Anthropic in AI coding. The Next Web carried Microsoft's own claim that MAI Code 2 matches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol at 40% of the price, and Microsoft said it delivers 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost. Those are Microsoft's benchmarks, run on tests it picked, and the comparison prices include a launch discount that ends in May 2027. The money logic is plain. OpenAI and Microsoft formally ended their exclusive partnership and revenue-sharing arrangement on April 27, 2026, and Microsoft pays OpenAI a share of Azure AI revenue, as reported in coverage of the MAI launch. Every request served by an MAI model is revenue Microsoft keeps whole. Frankly, the two moves aren't a contradiction. Copilot in Word is a place where customers want the best-known name on the label, and Microsoft would be foolish to hold back Sol while rivals sell it. Code is different: developers compare per-task cost on a spreadsheet, and a cheaper in-house model wins there on arithmetic alone. Nadella announced GPT-6.2 for Microsoft Foundry from the same Ignite stage as the MAI Code 2 launch, which shows how deliberately the company is running both. The test for the next quarter is simple and measurable: how many Copilot requests Microsoft routes to its own models instead of OpenAI's, and whether it says so. Microsoft hasn't published that split. records.excerpt: Title: OpenAI Models Improve AMD Flagship GPU Design by Up to 14% in Under Five Months URL Source: http://www.kucoin.com/blog/openai-models-improve-amd-flagship-gpu-design-by-up-to-14-in-under-five-months Final URL: https://www.kucoin.com/blog/openai-models-improve-amd-flagship-gpu-design-by-up-to-14-in-under-five-months Published Time: 2026-11-23T02:43:00.000Z Markdown Content: ![Image 1: Custom Image](https://assets.staticimg.com/cms/media/Fv07MJAAdACohL8N7aDwaU5dnEvqsigcYt2TiDqx2.PNG?w=1024&q=50&format=auto) OpenAI reported that its AI models improved the power, performance, and area (PPA) characteristics of AMD's flagship GPU design by up to 14% in less than five months, according to a November 18, 2026 research announcement. The models identified additional circuit optimizations in designs AMD engineers had already refined over several years, with some changes incorporated into hardware submitted for manufacturing. The development demonstrates a potential role for AI in complex semiconductor engineering, although the reported gains concern GPU intellectual property rather than verified improvements in finished-chip performance. The results also raise questions about how AI-assisted design could influence future processor development. ## Key Takeaways * **AMD GPU design improvement:** OpenAI reported up to 14% improvement in flagship GPU power, performance, and area (PPA) metrics in less than five months. * **AI-assisted circuit optimization:** OpenAI's models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL code, while Synopsys engineering tools checked circuit functionality and evaluated design trade-offs. * **Manufacturing adoption:** AMD incorporated some AI-generated changes into a design submitted for manufacturing and added others to production files for future hardware. * **Additional processor improvements:** OpenAI reported single-digit PPA gains in AMD CPU blocks and silicon-validated area reductions of approximately 13% and 10% in Jalapeño components. * **Future semiconductor development:** OpenAI and Synopsys are developing GPT-Synopsys, a specialized AI model intended to support semiconductor design and verification workflows. * **Important performance limitation:** The reported 14% gain does not establish equivalent whole-GPU speed improvements, and detailed AMD silicon benchmarks remain unavailable. ## What Did OpenAI Improve in AMD's Flagship GPU Design? On November 18, 2026, OpenAI announced that its AI models had helped improve AMD's flagship GPU intellectual property (IP), achieving gains of up to 14% in power, performance, and area (PPA) metrics. The improvements were measured against highly optimized circuit designs that AMD engineers had refined over several years. According to OpenAI, its models identified additional optimization opportunities by rewriting SystemVerilog RTL, the hardware description code that defines how digital circuits operate. The company estimated that the collaboration achieved approximately one year of engineering progress in less than five months. Unlike a conventional software update, these modifications affect the underlying circuit descriptions used to develop future semiconductor hardware. ### What Does the Up-to-14% PPA Improvement Actually Mean? The reported **14% improvement concerns chip-design efficiency, not a 14% increase in overall GPU processing speed**. In semiconductor engineering, PPA measures three important characteristics: power consumption, circuit performance, and the physical area required to implement a design. Improving these characteristics can help engineers develop more efficient processors, although the benefits depend on the specific circuits and design requirements. A smaller circuit, for example, may use fewer logic cells without necessarily completing calculations faster. Engineers must also consider how changes to one design characteristic affect the others, since improvements in speed, power efficiency, and area do not always occur simultaneously. records.title: UC signs $1.2 million-a-year OpenAI deal despite faculty calls for delay
records.excerpt: ChatGPT Edu and Codex will reach students, faculty and staff in the coming weeks. UC says access remains optional; faculty leaders question how the purchase was decided. The University of California is promising broader access and stronger data protections through a $1.2 million-a-year OpenAI agreement covering its 10 campuses. But the purchase is moving forward over faculty leaders’ requests for a delay. ChatGPT Edu and the coding tool Codex are expected to reach students, faculty and staff in the coming weeks. What the annual payment buys The agreement replaces a looser purchasing arrangement dating to 2024, when individual campuses could buy ChatGPT Edu licenses and credits at their own expense. The new purchase covers UC’s academic programs and operations, but not its hospitals or clinics. Access comes with an important price distinction: the university’s annual fee covers basic models, not every model a student or researcher might want to use. More advanced models will still require paid credits purchased by users or campuses. The terms include: Unlimited access to ChatGPT’s base models. A 20% discount on OpenAI credits, according to UC. A waiver of Codex’s $10 monthly per-user fee. Supporters see a way to narrow differences in what students can afford. Miguel Craven, a UC Davis graduate student and student regent, told the Los Angeles Times that some students have long paid for premium subscriptions while others depend on free tools. He said that difference has created an equity gap. Foundational decisions about UC’s educational environment are being made without sufficient involvement of its educators Susannah Scott, UC Academic Senate chair, in an email to the Los Angeles Times A purchase or an academic decision? The Academic Council, an executive body of Academic Senate leaders, said it learned of the pending agreement on October 21. In an October 30 letter, it asked UC President James B. Milliken to delay the purchase. The council said it did not oppose AI but had questions about the deal. Scott told the Times on November 20 that those concerns remained unresolved. Milliken’s response drew a distinction between providing access and setting classroom rules: his letter said the purchase neither requires students or faculty to use the tools nor establishes academic policy . He also said chancellors supported the decision. That distinction is itself contested. UCLA information studies associate professor Greg Leazer called the purchase a significant new academic policy presented as procurement. He argued that ChatGPT undermines learning by replacing the work of reading, discussion and writing. Those are his objections, not findings from an evaluation of this rollout. Data protections and training accompany access UC’s privacy argument concerns what happens to information supplied to the tools. Chief information officer Van Williams said OpenAI will not use UC users’ data to improve its technology. Milliken said the agreement provides stronger privacy protections than personal accounts. Williams also said the contract is intended to give UC legal recourse if OpenAI causes harm. In its November 19 announcement , UC said the partnership also includes AI-literacy workshops and workforce training at no additional cost to the university. Campuses will have access to OpenAI Academy materials explaining how language models work and how to use them. OpenAI will help career centers and student leaders run training sessions. The agreement does not make OpenAI UC’s exclusive AI provider. UC says it will continue supporting multiple vendors, and faculty retain full discretion over whether and how AI tools are used in their courses.

records.title: OpenAI wants AI companies to agree on common limits, Chief Scientist shares plan to keep AI safe
records.excerpt: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed using a metric called perplexity to set common limits on AI growth with CEO Sam Altman urging the industry to agree on shared safety rules Artificial intelligence is getting smarter at a breakneck pace, and even the people building it are now talking openly about putting on the brakes. In a new blog post, OpenAI’s Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki has laid out a way for tech companies to measure AI progress and set sensible limits before the technology becomes too powerful to control.The post quickly got a big push from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who shared it on X (formerly Twitter) and urged rival companies to come together on safety."This is the most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile," Altman wrote. "We are providing a lot of transparency into our pretraining progress and hope we can agree as a field to common limits. I think that would be very wise and help ensure safety and control."Why AI companies are talking about slowing downThe debate over slowing down AI development has heated up in recent weeks. It gained fresh urgency after a former researcher who worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic warned that AI companies were "gambling with our lives." Even Anthropic’s own IPO filing acknowledged that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to society."Following this, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a proposal to "pace the frontier." He called on major AI labs to agree on "common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress." The idea appeared to win support from both Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.However, putting a speed limit on AI comes with a basic problem: before companies can agree to slow down, they have to agree on how to measure speed. That is the gap Pachocki is trying to fill.What is ‘perplexity’ and why does it matter?In his blog post, Pachocki suggested that the AI industry should use a measurement called perplexitynot to be confused with the AI search company of the same name, to track how fast models are advancing.In simple terms, perplexity measures how well an AI model predicts the next word or piece of text (known as a token) on average. The lower the perplexity score, the better the AI is at predicting text, and the more capable the model is.According to Pachocki, most standard tests that check how well an AI performs specific tasks quickly become outdated because models keep getting better too fast. Perplexity, on the other hand, has stayed a reliable and useful way to track an AI system’s underlying growth during pretraining—the massive phase where models learn from huge amounts of data and computing power.How fast OpenAI’s models are improvingTo show how the metric works in practice, Pachocki shared a chart tracking how the perplexity scores of OpenAI’s models have steadily dropped since GPT-3.5.When GPT-4 reached a perplexity score of around 0.91, it became good at "chain-of-thought" reasoning—essentially breaking down complex problems step by step. Pachocki noted that this breakthrough paved the way for today’s modern reasoning models.Now, OpenAI’s models have pushed even further, reaching scores below 0.8. According to Pachocki, crossing that mark has led to "transformative capabilities" in demanding fields like mathematics and cybersecurity.A shared rulebook for the AI industryPachocki believes perplexity can act as a "shared benchmark for general intelligence" across the tech industry. If major AI companies adopt it as a common yardstick, they can agree on clear red lines together.Under this approach, AI labs would commit to not training models past a certain perplexity threshold until their ability to understand, track, and monitor AI behaviour reaches concrete safety milestones.For Altman and OpenAI, the goal is to make sure no single company feels pressured to cut corners in a fiercely competitive race. By sharing its own pretraining progress openly, OpenAI is hoping the rest of the industry will follow suit—and agree on a speed limit before the technology outruns human control.- EndsAlso Read | AI godfather says Dario Amodei has medieval mindset, left OpenAI when things went out of controlAlso Read | OpenAI is building humanoid robots, Sam Altman teases demo timelineAlso Read | OpenAI's AI model finds a way to bypass Apple's Lockdown Mode, report reveals

少数のリポジトリと専任のレビュアーグループから始めます。特にオンボーディングと脆弱性の共有がまだ比較的手作業である間は、最初は対象を絞って展開することをおすすめします。 学びに応じた脅威モデルの改善モデルに小さな更新を加えることで、コンテキストが改善され、時間の経過とともに検出結果の精度が高まります。 現在 GitHub Cloud を使用していない場合は、評価用にリスクの低いリポジトリや本番環境以外のリポジトリから始めることを検討してください。これにより、より広く導入する前に、チームがワークフローへの信頼を高めやすくなります。 生成されたパッチ PR は通常のレビュープロセスでレビューします。修正によってリグレッションが発生しないように、Codex Security PR で Codex Code Review を使用することもおすすめします。 よくある質問 Codex Security はコードを自動的に変更しますか？ いいえ。Codex Security は、人によるレビューのためのパッチを提案します。提案されたパッチは pull request にできますが、コードが自動的に変更されることはありません。 Codex Security はファジングやシグネチャベースのスキャンを利用しますか？ いいえ。Codex Security は、ファジングやシグネチャベースのスキャンではなく、言語モデルの推論、テスト時の計算処理、ツール利用、大規模なコンテキストを活用します。 脅威モデルを確認、編集できますか？ はい。脅威モデルは閲覧・編集できるため、チームは Codex Security がアプリケーションをどう理解しているかを確認し、自らの環境に合わせて前提条件を更新できます。 検証とは何ですか？ 検証とは、Codex Security が潜在的な脆弱性を提示する前に、隔離環境でその再現を試みる工程です。これは、誤検知を減らし、精度の高い検出結果に絞ることを目的としています。 検出結果が検証された後はどうなりますか？ 検証後、Codex Security は根本原因に対処するパッチを提案します。このパッチはレビュー用の pull request にできます。 records.excerpt: ChatGPT Business での広告クレジットの申請 | OpenAI Help Center OpenAI Support このページは機械翻訳されています。 元の英語の記事を表示 。 ChatGPT Business での広告クレジットの申請 ワークスペースが対象となるかを確認し、広告アカウントをリンクして、広告マネージャーでクレジットの利用状況を確認できます。 更新日: 8 hours ago 概要 対象の ChatGPT Business ワークスペースのオーナーは、ChatGPT での広告掲載に使えるクレジットを毎月最大 50 米ドル分受け取れます。本特典の提供期間は 2027 年 1 月 31 日までですが、予定数に達し次第終了します。 登録・受け取り前の確認事項 請求先住所が米国、英国、ドイツ、フランスのいずれかにある有料の Business ワークスペースは、新規・既存を問わず対象となり得ます。 特典 に本特典が表示されるのは、ワークスペースのオーナーのみです。ワークスペースの管理者またはメンバーの場合は、オーナーに受け取りを依頼してください。 各ワークスペースに連携できる広告アカウントは 1 つで、各広告アカウントで本特典を受け取れるのも 1 つのワークスペース分のみです。広告アカウントに新規登録プロモーションが適用されている場合、そのプロモーションが終了するまで、そのアカウントは選択できません。Business への登録をご検討中の場合は、まず広告アカウントのプロモーションをご確認ください。購入手続きの完了後に初めて、お使いのアカウントが対象外だと判明する場合があります。 広告クレジットの受け取り ウェブ版の ChatGPT にサインインし、オーナーとして管理している Business ワークスペースに切り替えます。 ワークスペースの設定を開き、 特典 を選択します。 広告クレジット で、 広告クレジットを受け取る を選択します。 管理している広告アカウントを選択するか、 新しい広告アカウントを作成 を選択します。既存のアカウントを連携する場合も、新しく作成する場合も、Business 特典の適用中は、そのアカウントで通常の新規登録プロモーションを利用できません。 クレジット額、有効期限、特典の利用条件を確認し、 連携して受け取る を選択します。 受け取り後、 広告マネージャーに移動 を選択すると、広告アカウントの請求通貨で残高を確認できます。事前に広告を購入しなくても、クレジットを受け取れます。キャンペーンを開始する前に、広告マネージャーで 請求設定 を完了してください。 受け取れるクレジットの金額 毎月のクレジット額は、割引適用後にお支払いいただいた Business の有料シート料金に相当します。ワークスペースごとに、毎月最大 50 米ドル分、または広告アカウントの請求通貨でそれに相当する金額を受け取れます。税金や従量課金の料金は、クレジット額の算定対象に含まれません。たとえば、丸 1 か月分の対象シート料金として 200 ドルをお支払いいただいた場合、ワークスペースに 50 ドル分の広告クレジットが付与されます。 月払いの場合、初回のクレジットは、お支払い済みの請求月の残り日数に応じて日割り計算されます。次回以降のクレジットは、請求日に支払いが正常に完了した後に付与されます。年払いの場合、有料サブスクリプションと本特典が有効な間、クレジットは毎月分割で付与されます。月額の上限は同じです。 有料シートを追加すると、月額の上限に達するまでクレジット額が増える場合があります。シートを削除またはダウングレードすると、引き下げ後の料金が適用される時点から、今後付与されるクレジット額が減ります。シートを別のユーザーに割り当て直しても、追加のクレジットは付与されません。Business を解約すると、次回の更新日以降、新たなクレジットは付与されません。Enterprise にアップグレードすると、アップグレードが適用された時点で、新たなクレジットの付与が停止します。 クレジットの利用と利用状況の確認 各クレジットの有効期限は、付与から 30 日間です。付与日以降、連携したアカウントで発生する対象の広告費に適用されます。それ以前の料金や既存の請求書の未払い残高は、引き続きお客様にお支払いいただく必要があります。クレジットに現金としての価値はなく、譲渡もできません。 クレジットを使い切った後も、キャンペーンの広告費は引き続き発生する場合があります。たとえば、50 ドル分のクレジットがあり、対象の広告費が 55 ドル発生した場合、50 ドル分はクレジットでまかなわれ、残りの 5 ドルが請求されます。 クレジットの利用額を確認するには、広告マネージャーで 請求 > アクティビティ を開き、 プロモーション を確認してください。料金とクレジットの制限について詳しくは、 請求と支払い および 広告クレジット利用規約 をご覧ください。 この記事は役に立ちましたか？

records.excerpt: OpenAI Daybreak 移行・組織統合ガイド | OpenAI Help Center OpenAI Support このページは機械翻訳されています。 元の英語の記事を表示 。 OpenAI Daybreak 移行・組織統合ガイド Daybreak の移行に向けて準備し、メインの API 組織と ChatGPT または Codex ワークスペースでアクセス制御を設定します。 更新日: 2 days ago Daybreak のアクセス制御のご紹介 OpenAI は、API と Codex に Daybreak（旧称 Trusted Access for Cyber）機能のアクセス制御を導入します。この制御により、管理者は Daybreak を利用できるプロジェクトやユーザーを指定できます。また、許可されたユーザーは、個々の API リクエストや Codex タスクに Daybreak 機能を適用するかどうかを選択できます。 API では、Cyber モデルへのアクセス範囲を プロジェクトレベル で設定できるようになりました。組織管理者は Cyber の作業専用のプロジェクトを作成または選択し、そのプロジェクトで Daybreak を有効化したうえで、アクセスが必要なユーザーだけを追加できます。許可されたユーザーは、任意の `access_programs.cyber` パラメーターを渡すことで、リクエストに Daybreak 機能を適用するかどうかを選択できます（詳細は こちら ）。これにより、Cyber の作業を社外向けのユースケースを含む他の API 利用と分離しながら、メイン組織内で管理できます。 ChatGPT と Codex では、Daybreak Blue と Red の両方に、 ユーザーレベルの Cyber モデルアクセス制御 も導入します。これにより、ワークスペース管理者は、メインワークスペース内のどのユーザーに Daybreak の各ティアへのアクセスを許可するかを選択できます。許可されたユーザーは、詳細モデル選択画面で Daybreak の切り替えをオンにすることで、Daybreak 機能を適用するタイミングを選べます。 これらの制御を組み合わせることで、管理、請求、ガバナンスをメイン組織に集約しながら、Cyber アクセスを適切なプロジェクト、ユーザー、ユースケースに限定できます。なお、Codex の API キー認証は、現時点では同じユーザーレベルの制御に対応していません。ただし、API キーは API のプロジェクトレベルのアクセス制御で引き続き管理できます。 アクセス制御の利用開始 対象となるすべての API 組織および ChatGPT または Codex のワークスペースで、Daybreak のアクセス制御を利用できるようになりました。設定手順は、 OpenAI Daybreak：チームのアクセス設定 をご覧ください。 移行プロセスの概要 メインの API 組織への移行には、以下の手順が必要です。 お客様：移行先の構成の確認 チームが今後 Daybreak 機能を利用するメインの OpenAI API 組織を特定してください。該当する場合は、メインの ChatGPT/Codex ワークスペースも特定してください。 お客様：ユーザーとワークフローの移行完了 対象ユーザーをメインの組織やプロジェクトに追加し、必要なワークフロー、アプリケーション、API キー、運用上の依存関係を Cyber 専用組織から移行してください。以下の 移行チェックリスト をご覧ください。移行を自動化して支援する Admin プラグイン もご参照ください。 お客様：OpenAI への移行リクエストの送信 チームで以下のチェックリストを完了したら、OpenAI が移行処理を実施できる状態になったことを、OpenAI のアカウント担当チーム（または support@openai.com ）にお知らせください。移行リクエストには、アクセス制御を設定する組織の組織 ID と、移行元となるセカンダリ組織の組織 ID を記載してください。 OpenAI：メイン組織の設定 OpenAI が、メイン組織で適切な Cyber モデルへのアクセスとプロジェクトレベルの制御を有効化します。 お客様：最終設定の完了 その後、組織管理者は、メインの API 組織内の対象プロジェクト、または ChatGPT/Codex ワークスペース内の対象ユーザーに対して Cyber アクセスを有効化し、設定を保存できます。必要に応じて、適切なユーザーをそのプロジェクトまたはワークスペースに追加してください。設定手順は、 OpenAI Daybreak：チームのアクセス設定 をご覧ください。 以前、ChatGPT でのログインを使用する Codex のユーザーアクセスを申請した場合は、メインの ChatGPT/Codex ワークスペースで対象ユーザーのアクセスを再設定してください。これにより、手順 7 で専用ワークスペースを無効化する際にアクセスが途切れるのを防げます。 お客様：Cyber 専用組織内のすべての API キーの失効 こちら の組織設定で API キーを確認し、Cyber 専用組織内のすべての API キーが失効済みであることを確かめてください（すべて無効になっている必要があります）。OpenAI が Cyber 専用の組織またはワークスペースを無効化すると、 未失効のキーはすべてアーカイブされますのでご注意ください 。 OpenAI：14 日間の猶予期間後に Cyber 専用の組織またはワークスペースを無効化 メイン組織への移行とワークフローの検証に必要な時間を確保できるよう、OpenAI は 14 日間待ってから、以前プロビジョニングした Cyber 専用の組織またはワークスペースを無効化します。以前、ChatGPT でのログインを使用する Codex のユーザーアクセスを申請し、メインワークスペース内でアクセスをまだ再設定していない場合、対象ユーザーはこの時点でアクセスできなくなります。ユーザーごとに個別にアクセス権が付与されていた場合も、移行時にそのアクセス権は失われます。 移行チェックリスト OpenAI に移行処理を依頼する前に、以下を確認してください。 Daybreak 機能の移行先となる メインの API 組織 ID および ChatGPT/Codex ワークスペース ID を特定しています。 移行後に無効化する Cyber 専用の API 組織 ID および ChatGPT/Codex ワークスペース ID を特定しています。 メインの API 組織 ID と ChatGPT/Codex ワークスペース内で、Cyber モデルへのアクセスが 承認済みの社内ユースケースとユーザー にのみ有効化されることを確認しています。同じ組織やワークスペースで社外向けの利用も可能ですが、社外向けに利用するプロジェクトや外部ユーザーが参加するプロジェクトには、Daybreak 機能へのアクセスを許可できません。 Cyber 専用組織から、 必要なユーザー、ワークフロー、API キー、アプリケーション、運用上の依存関係を移行済み です。移行対象には以下が含まれます。 ユーザーアカウント GPT プロジェクト ワークスペースの管理者設定（SCIM、ユーザーグループ、ワークスペースアイコン、分析と指標） 共有された会話 データ保持期間 Compliance API のログ キャンバス ライブラリのコンテンツ コネクタの設定とデータ Codex のタスク、履歴、設定 ワークスペースのエージェントとスキル Cyber 専用組織内のすべての API キー が適切に失効されていることを確認しています。残っているキーは、14 日間の猶予期間後に OpenAI が Cyber 専用組織を無効化する際にアーカイブされます。 OpenAI によるプロビジョニングの完了後、組織管理者が承認済みプロジェクトで Trusted Access for Cyber を有効化する準備ができています。 OpenAI が Cyber 専用の組織またはワークスペースを無効化 しても問題ない状態になっています。 すべての項目が完了したら、該当する組織 ID またはワークスペース ID を OpenAI のアカウント担当チームに送り、OpenAI が移行処理を実施できる状態になったことをお知らせください。 よくある質問 Cyber の作業を他の API 利用と分離できますか？ はい、できます。組織管理者は Cyber の作業専用のプロジェクトを作成または選択し、そのプロジェクトで Trusted Access for Cyber を有効化したうえで、アクセスが必要なユーザーだけを追加できます。 同じメイン組織を、社内の Cyber 作業と社外向けのユースケースの両方に利用できますか？ はい。ただし、Daybreak 機能は承認済みの社内ユースケースに対してのみ有効化し、サイバーモデルは社内のサイバー関連ユースケース専用のプロジェクト内でのみ使用する必要があります。社外向けのユースケースがあるプロジェクトや、外部ユーザーが参加するプロジェクトには、Daybreak 機能へのアクセスを許可しないでください。 承認済みの社内ユースケースとは何ですか？ Daybreak の利用承認は、承認を受けたお客様に雇用されている人員、またはそのお客様のために業務を行う人員を対象とします。Daybreak のモデルや機能へのアクセスを第三者に付与することはできません。承認されるユースケースには、組織の社内チームが行うセキュリティ研究、レッドチーム評価、脅威分析、脆弱性評価、防御テスト、セキュリティのためのコードレビュー、インシデント調査、その他のセキュリティ業務が含まれます。OpenAI の Daybreak パートナープログラムから明示的な承認を得ていない限り、Daybreak 機能を顧客向け製品、第三者へのアクセス提供、一般公開する自動化処理に使用しないでください。 移行後、専用の統合 API 組織はどうなりますか？ 移行が完了すると、OpenAI は Cyber 専用の組織またはワークスペースを 無効化 し、従来の組織レベルの Cyber アクセス権を削除します。 準備が整う前に OpenAI が Cyber 専用組織を無効化することはありますか？ いいえ、ありません。必要なユーザー、ワークフロー、API キー、アプリケーション、運用上の依存関係をメインの組織またはワークスペースに移した後にのみ、OpenAI に移行処理を依頼してください。 既存の API キーは引き続き使えますか？ Cyber 専用の統合組織で作成した API キーは、メイン組織には引き継がれません。移行前に、メイン組織内の承認済みプロジェクトで新しい API キーを作成し、古いキーに依存しているアプリケーション、スクリプト、ワークフローを更新してください。この移行の一環として、Cyber 専用の API 組織内にある既存の API キーを失効させる必要があります。Cyber 専用組織が無効化されると、その組織のキーは使用できなくなります。 OpenAI にどのような情報を送る必要がありますか？ 移行先となるメインの API 組織 ID と、移行後に無効化する Cyber 専用の API 組織 ID を、OpenAI のアカウント担当チームにお送りください。 この記事は役に立ちましたか？

records.title: China's intelligence arm ran campaign to acquire advanced AI chips: Report
records.excerpt: Title: China's intelligence arm ran campaign to acquire advanced AI chips: Report URL Source: http://www.business-standard.com/world-news/china-s-intelligence-arm-ran-campaign-to-acquire-advanced-ai-chips-report-126112200365_1.html Final URL: https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/china-s-intelligence-arm-ran-campaign-to-acquire-advanced-ai-chips-report-126112200365_1.html Published Time: 2026-11-22T15:37:56+05:30 Markdown Content: China's intelligence agency has made acquiring advanced semiconductor chips and gathering intelligence on the global chip industry a priority, running a campaign to overcome Western export restrictions for at least two years, according to a New York Times (NYT) report. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) set up a working group under its chief Chen Yixin to lead the effort, which includes helping Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into the country, besides collecting intelligence on the semiconductor sector and its supply chains, the report said, citing serving and former security and intelligence officials from Asia, the US and Europe. The revelations come amid US scrutiny of Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom American officials allege was working with the Chinese intelligence agency to spy on Jensen Huang, Nvidia's co-founder and former chief executive. The NYT report, published on Saturday, adds to findings published by the newspaper on November 20, which detailed extensive, albeit largely indirect, links between companies associated with Alice Huang's family and Chinese state-owned defence contractors supplying the People's Liberation Army (PLA). Citing a confidential analysis by independent intelligence firm Strider Technologies and its own review of corporate filings, the November 20 report said around USD 3.6 billion in Chinese government funding had flowed through companies associated with Huang's family or business associates. The money funded technology projects, including data centres that received Nvidia chips. ### Also Read However, the report noted that the available research did not establish whether the Chinese military had actually used computing power from these data centres. China has rejected the espionage allegations as "pure fabrication". According to NYT's Saturday report, the MSS campaign is part of a broader effort by Chinese President Xi Jinping to achieve technological self-reliance and overcome restrictions imposed by the US and its allies. The effort is being coordinated at the party level by the Central Science and Technology Commission, established by Xi in 2023 and led by Ding Xuexiang, a member of the Politburo Standing Committee, the report said. Chen, who became China's state security minister in late 2022, has repeatedly described the campaign against Western technology restrictions as an important responsibility of his agency. In April, he called for intensifying the struggle against technological blockades and advancing artificial intelligence innovation, industrial development and applications, according to a Communist Party journal cited by the report. The November 20 NYT investigation detailed how companies linked to Alice Huang's family were connected to Nvidia partners and businesses with ties to China's defence industry. Alice Huang's sister, Huang Yu, and an investor named Kang Wei, described in the NYT report as Huang's business partner and often introduced as her husband, had links to several companies involved in the data centre business, the report said. One such company, Century Litong, based in Shanghai, was founded in 2023 by Century Longteng, a data centre operator in which an investment firm controlled by Huang's sister held a 27 per cent stake. Kang had been an executive director of Century Longteng since February 2022, according to the report. In 2023, Jiangsu Lettall Electronic bought 90 per cent of Century Litong and owned the entire company by 2024. Lettall also owns 80 per cent of Nanjing Jinning Microwave, a manufacturer of components that Lettall has said are used in Chinese radar and missile systems, it said. Alice Huang ran Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and provided high-end computing capacity to Chinese companies. The company is under investigation by the US Justice Department over suspected illegal shipments of advanced chips to China. The Saturday report said US officials were also examining whether Megaspeed had helped supply Nvidia chips to data centres linked to Chinese military research. It further said the US administration was seeking to close a perceived loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access advanced Nvidia chips through data centres located outside China. The Trump administration announced last week that it would move ahead with a new rule requiring overseas data centres to obtain a government licence before supplying significant volumes of computing power to companies headquartered in countries on a list that includes China, Russia and Iran. The restriction is scheduled to take effect in about 90 days, according to the newspaper. The US officials' assessment of Alice Huang's role in the Chinese intelligence agency's efforts and the extent of her connections to companies linked to the PLA remain under scrutiny, the NYT report added. (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

records.title: SoftBank's Son Calls Anthropic Pass a Mistake as Stock Tumbles 16% and a $1 Trillion SK hynix Idea I
records.excerpt: Masayoshi Son calls missing Anthropic an error after SoftBank backed OpenAI; shares fell 16% Friday amid AI valuation doubts. SoftBanks , Son SoftBank's Son Calls Anthropic Pass a Mistake as Stock Tumbles 16% and a $1 Trillion SK hynix Idea Is Shelved Published on 11/23/2026 at 05:41 | Editorial boerse-global.de Masayoshi Son calls missing Anthropic an error after SoftBank backed OpenAI; shares fell 16% Friday amid AI valuation doubts. SoftBank Group Illustration mit AI erstellt. SoftBank Group founder Masayoshi Son has owned up to one of his costliest regrets: sitting out Anthropic. In comments to the Financial Times on 18 November, Son described the decision to skip an investment in the AI developer as one of his mistakes, a remark that landed after SoftBank had already thrown its weight behind rival OpenAI. The admission came in the wake of Anthropic's stock market debut, which, according to Reuters, did little to dispel doubts about the returns on AI spending. The ensuing sell-off in AI-related names dragged SoftBank shares down 16% on Friday to close at €15.92. CNBC reported that investors were questioning the valuations of AI companies and the payback on large AI bets, with SoftBank particularly exposed because of its OpenAI stake. Capital Commitments in Sarawak Attention is also turning to SoftBank's build-out plans in Southeast Asia. On 10 November, SoftBank Group, Grab Holdings and Petroleum Sarawak unveiled an agreement to develop AI infrastructure in Sarawak, backed by a joint initial capital commitment of US$1 billion. SoftBank's share of that is US$800 million, with the contributions contingent on hitting agreed milestones and satisfying closing conditions. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying SoftBank Group? The same day brought a less welcome development from Astris Advisory, which cut its price target on SoftBank from 6,000 to 4,000 yen while keeping a "Neutral" rating, following the release of the company's earnings figures. A Chinese Hurdle for ABB Robotics SoftBank's planned purchase of ABB's robotics business ran into a regulatory wall on 4 November, when China's investment screening authority blocked the acquisition of the unit's Chinese operations. SoftBank said it remains in close contact with ABB, and both companies are continuing to work constructively on the transaction. A Trillion-Dollar Idea, Quietly Dropped Reuters reported that Son had explored financing options for a potential takeover of SK hynix valued at US$1 trillion. SoftBank has since said the idea is no longer being actively pursued, while SK hynix stated it was unaware of the matter. First-Half Loss The developments cap a difficult reporting period. For the first half of fiscal 2026, covering April through September, SoftBank posted a net loss attributable to shareholders of the parent of ¥768.0 billion. A year earlier, in the first half of fiscal 2025, the group had booked a net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥2.92 trillion. records.title: ABB、54億ドルのソフトバンク取引が北京で停滞する中、ロボティクス事業の分離を検討
records.excerpt: ABBは、ソフトバンクへの54億ドル（約8,600億円）の売却が中国の国家発展改革委員会に阻止されたことを受け、救済できなければロボティクス部門の上場または分離の準備を進めている。阻止の理由は、ソフトバンクとOpenAIなど西側AI開発企業との関係、および機密データが米国に渡るリスクへの懸念だった。両社は中国事業（部門の約30%を占める）を切り離し、現地上場または国内買い手への売却などを通じて取引を再構築しようとしている。解決策は数週間以内にまとまる可能性があるが、来年にずれ込む恐れもある。中国はABBにとって最大のロボティクス市場であり、約30の現地法人で1万5,000人を雇用している。 ABB Ltd（SIX:ABBN）が、ソフトバンクグループ（TYO:9984）への54億ドル（約8,600億円）の売却を復活できなくなった場合の代替策として、ロボティクス部門の上場準備を開始した。ロイターが関係者の話として伝えた。 スイスのエンジニアリング大手は、再構築交渉が決裂した場合に備え、同部門の分離または別の買い手への売却を検討しているという。上場先や目標評価額はまだ確定しておらず、関係者は匿名を条件に語った。 双方は依然として当初合意の維持を望んでいる。ABBとソフトバンクは、北京の規制当局を満足させ得る修正案を協議しており、最有力の選択肢は、ロボティクス部門の約30%を占める中国事業を切り離し、その部門を現地取引所に上場するか国内の買い手に売却するというものだ。数週間以内に合意に達する可能性があるが、ある関係者は交渉が来年に持ち越す可能性があると警告した。 ABBはコメントを拒否し、ソフトバンクも同様だった。スイス企業は以前、ソフトバンクと緊密に連絡を取り合い、取引に向けて建設的に取り組んでいると述べていた。 北京の国家発展改革委員会は、ソフトバンクとOpenAIを含む西側の人工知能開発企業との関係（この日本の投資家はOpenAIに主要な出資を行っている）、および機密データが米国に渡る可能性への懸念から、売却を阻止した。中国当局は、AIをめぐるワシントンとの競争が激化する中、先端技術への外国投資に対する監視を強化している。 今回の介入は、中国がメタ・プラットフォームズ（META）に対し、AIスタートアップManusの買収（20億ドル超相当）を撤回するよう命じた4月の同様の措置に続くものだ。 中国はABBにとって最大のロボティクス市場である。同社は約130都市に約30の現地法人を展開し1万5,000人を雇用しており、ABBエンジニアリング（上海）はロボティクス事業のグローバル本社であると同時に、重要な研究・生産拠点となっている。 ソフトバンクにとって、買収失敗は孫正義最高経営責任者（CEO）がグループのAI投資戦略の中心と位置付けるロボティクス分野への進出を損なうことになる。ある関係者によると、取引が破談となれば日本の複合企業は違約金を負う可能性があるが、金額は開示されていない。 ABBの contingency planning（緊急対応策の策定）は、こう着状態が規制上の遅延から、今年最大級の産業技術取引の一つが解消される可能性へと移行したことを示している。分離となれば、株主には中国へのエクスポージャーが大きい独立したロボティクス事業が渡ることになり、中国事業の切り出し売却となれば、北京が同部門の技術を国内に留める構造を受け入れるかどうかが試されることになる。 投資家にとっての主要な変数は、再構築された取引の形とタイミングである。中国部門の現地上場となれば、ABBにはより小規模だが政治的に持続可能なロボティクス事業が残る。完全分離となれば、中国市場をどれだけ維持できるかで評価額が左右される独立上場企業が誕生することになる。

records.title: SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 Splashdown Completes ISS Solar Upgrade, Returns Canadarm2 Robotic Arm Joint
records.excerpt: SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 splashdown on November 21, 2026 closed out the ISS Roll-Out Solar Array program, with Dragon C211 returning the eighth and final pair of Redwire-designed flexible iROSA solar... SpaceX's Cargo Dragon capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast on Friday, November 21, 2026, at 2:03 p.m. PST, closing out the CRS-35 resupply mission to the International Space Station. The recovery marked the successful end of a cargo run that quietly accomplished two of the most consequential hardware milestones in the station's recent operational history.Dragon Delivers and DepartsDragon C211 — on its fourth flight — launched October 13, 2026, at 6:33 a.m. EDT from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral on a Oct. 13 Falcon 9 launch of Booster B1096, making its eighth flight. Dragon docked to the Harmony module's forward port two days later and remained berthed for more than five weeks before undocking on November 20. The three-day weather delay caused by sustained high winds over the Pacific recovery zone pushed the original November 18 splashdown target to Friday.SpaceX recovery teams aboard the GO Navigator vessel retrieved the capsule and its cargo shortly after splashdown.The Final Pair of Solar ArraysThe headline cargo on the outbound leg of CRS-35 was a pair of ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays — the seventh and eighth iROSAs in the station's power upgrade program, and the last the station will ever receive. Each iROSA is a roll-out solar wing designed by Redwire Space: a flexible photovoltaic blanket that unfurls from a compact stowage cylinder like a roll of carpet and deploys to full span without any hinged rigid panels. The design allows the arrays to be packed tightly enough to fit inside Dragon's unpressurized trunk and still cover a surface area large enough to meaningfully supplement the station's aging original solar arrays.The installation program spread across four Dragon missions — CRS-22, CRS-26, CRS-28, and CRS-35 — beginning in June 2021 and concluding with the final pair installed on the station's 2A and 3B power channels in late October and early November. The completed eight-array suite delivers more than 160 kW supplemental power across all eight arrays, enough to cover the growing electricity demands of research facilities added to the station over the past decade while also providing margin for future expansion. With all eight iROSAs in place, Boeing's solar power system for the station is now operating at its fully upgraded configuration.Canadarm2 Wrist Joint Returns to EarthThe second major hardware story of CRS-35 traveled in the opposite direction: the failed wrist joint from the 17.6-meter robotic arm built by MDA for the Canadian Space Agency, which has been in continuous service since its launch aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis during mission STS-100 in April 2001. The arm is equipped with seven joints and can lift payloads of up to 116,000 kilograms — a capability that makes it indispensable for berthing Dragon capsules, repositioning large station components, and supporting spacewalking astronauts.On May 27, 2026, engineers monitoring the arm's performance telemetry detected that the wrist joint was drawing elevated motor current, a classic indicator of mechanical binding or bearing wear. Ground teams temporarily restricted the joint's range of motion while they developed a repair plan. The arm itself remained functional for essential operations, but the fault limited its full articulation and introduced risk into time-sensitive berthing and assembly tasks.On June 30, 2026, NASA astronauts Chris Williams and Jessica Meir conducted U.S. Spacewalk 95 — lasting 7 hours and 20 minutes — to remove the failed wrist joint assembly and install a spare that had been stored aboard the station. The procedure restored the arm to full articulation, and Canadarm2 returned to unrestricted operations the same day. The repaired arm was used to assist with subsequent payload handling, including support for the iROSA installation spacewalks in October and November.The failed joint, returned to Earth inside Dragon's pressurized cargo bay, will now be examined by MDA engineers. Physical analysis of flight hardware can reveal failure mechanisms that telemetry alone cannot — information that may inform maintenance schedules for Canadarm2's remaining joints, which have no planned replacement on the books as the station targets operations through the 2030s. ISS extension scenarios assume the arm continues to operate without a successor system.Science Cargo Returning to EarthDragon's pressurized cargo hold carried more than 6,300 pounds (2,858 kilograms) of return cargo, the largest portion of which was scientific samples and experiment hardware accumulated during the Expedition 75 crew rotation.Among the science cargo were bioprinted blood vessel constructs developed using the reduced-gravity environment of microgravity, which allows cells to self-organize in three dimensions without the structural support scaffolding that Earth-based printing requires. The samples will be analyzed to assess whether microgravity-printed vascular structures exhibit geometry and mechanical properties comparable to native tissue — a capability that could have implications for pharmaceutical testing and, ultimately, for the bioprinting of transplantable grafts.Also returning: antibiotic-resistant bacterial cultures cultivated during the mission, protein crystal samples grown for a JAXA pharmaceutical structure-determination study, and blood and urine samples from the Expedition 75 crew for long-duration spaceflight health monitoring.Dragon C211's RecordDragon C211 has now completed four cargo missions: CRS-26, CRS-29, CRS-33, and CRS-35. SpaceX's reusable Dragon capsules are refurbished between flights and can carry both pressurized and unpressurized cargo in their trunk section. The trunk — which is not recovered and reenters the atmosphere after splashdown — carried the iROSA hardware on the outbound leg of CRS-35 and was jettisoned before reentry on the return.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhat did SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 deliver to the ISS?CRS-35 delivered the seventh and eighth ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays — the final pair of Redwire-designed flexible solar wings to be installed on the station — along with science experiments, crew provisions, and hardware. The solar arrays were installed on the 2A and 3B power channels in October and November 2026, completing the station's iROSA upgrade program.Why was the CRS-35 Dragon splashdown delayed?The original splashdown target of November 18, 2026 was pushed back three days due to high winds over the Pacific recovery zone. NASA and SpaceX stood down from the November 18 attempt and rescheduled after weather conditions improved. Dragon ultimately splashed down on November 21 at 2:03 p.m. PST.What is Canadarm2 and why was its wrist joint repaired?Canadarm2 is a 17.6-meter robotic arm built by MDA for the Canadian Space Agency, in service on the ISS since April 2001. It is used to berth visiting spacecraft, move large components, and support spacewalking astronauts. In May 2026, its wrist joint began drawing elevated motor current, indicating mechanical wear. NASA astronauts Chris Williams and Jessica Meir replaced the faulty joint during U.S. Spacewalk 95 on June 30, 2026, restoring the arm to full operation. The failed joint returned to Earth aboard CRS-35 for engineering analysis.How many iROSA solar arrays does the ISS now have?Eight. The ISS Roll-Out Solar Array program installed arrays across four SpaceX Dragon cargo missions — CRS-22 (June 2021), CRS-26 (November 2022), CRS-28 (June 2023), and CRS-35 (October–November 2026). Each array sits atop one of the station's existing solar wing masts and supplements its power output. All eight are now installed and operational.

records.excerpt: SoftBank Group Chairman Masayoshi Son reportedly once considered a plan to acquire SK Hynix for approximately $1 trillion, or 1.346 quadrillion won. However, SoftBank states it is not currently actively considering the deal, and no actual acquisition negotiations or official proposals have been confirmed. However, SoftBank stated that it is not currently actively reviewing the deal, and no actual acquisition negotiations or official proposals have been confirmed. Possibility of a $1 trillion deal explored Chairman Son reportedly recently inquired with Wall Street financial institutions about whether it would be possible to raise the funds necessary to acquire SK Hynix. This matter is said to be closer to an idea exploring the feasibility of financing a massive deal rather than a stage where acquisition negotiations are underway in earnest. Specific details regarding the share acquisition method, financing structure, or SK Group’s willingness to sell remain unknown. Masayoshi Son considers a 1.346 quadrillion won acquisition of SK Hynix (Photo: YouTube video capture) SoftBank: “Not currently under active review” A SoftBank Group spokesperson stated that the SK Hynix deal is “no longer under active consideration.” Consequently, the acquisition idea considered by Chairman Son has not proceeded to the implementation stage. It has also not been confirmed that any actual acquisition negotiations have taken place between SK Hynix and SoftBank or that any official acquisition proposal has been delivered. There is no separate official position from SK Hynix. Semiconductor firm mentioned amidst AI investment expansion SK Hynix is a company that produces memory semiconductors, including High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for artificial intelligence. As SoftBank pushes for investment and business expansion related to AI, SK Hynix’s semiconductor competitiveness is cited as the backdrop for it being mentioned as an acquisition target. However, SoftBank has not officially disclosed the reason why it attempted to acquire SK Hynix. No negotiations or proposals for an actual deal have been confirmed in relation to this idea. records.title: Takata airbags prompt Honda and Toyota to recall 1.6 million cars
records.excerpt: Takata airbags prompt Honda and Toyota to recall 1.6 million cars LM DH Lisa Monica, Ramdhani Pratama 22 November 2026, 11:00 WIB LM Lisa Monica Reporter DH Ramdhani Pratama Reporter WhatsApp Channel Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million US vehicles over airbag risks. JAKARTA - Automotive manufacturers Honda and Toyota are recalling approximately 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs in the United States (US) due to the risk of Takata airbag inflators rupturing. Both manufacturers have urged owners of affected vehicles to have the components replaced to prevent potential injuries. As reported by Reuters , Honda and Toyota said they had received no reports of accidents or injuries involving vehicles covered by the latest recall. Both companies also confirmed that no airbag inflator ruptures had occurred in vehicles included in the recall programme. Read Also: Foreign sell state-owned shares as JCI surges 1.59% in first session Nevertheless, they will replace the airbag inflators in affected vehicles as a precautionary measure. The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said that analysis and simulations of inflator degradation conducted by an independent testing group had enabled manufacturers to take action before the risks materialised. "Honda and Toyota have seen early evidence of potential degradation risks in certain vehicles and are currently conducting proactive vehicle recalls," NHTSA said. NHTSA added that other automotive manufacturers were continuing to analyse and test their airbag inflators. The recalls cover 810,592 older Honda cars and SUVs in the US and 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 units in the US. For Toyota, the affected models include the 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 Lexus IS250, 2017 Lexus GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Toyota Tundra, 2005-2007 Toyota Sequoia and 2016-2017 Toyota 4Runner. Meanwhile, Honda's recall covers several models, including the 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Civic, 2012-2013 CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX. Honda's recall programme applies to vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 US states or territories. Airbag Risks Have Caused Fatalities The Takata airbag inflator defect has become one of the biggest automotive safety scandals in US history. Since 2009, at least 28 people have died and more than 400 have been injured in the country due to defective Takata airbag inflators. All the fatalities involved airbag inflators without a desiccant. At least 20 of those killed were travelling in Honda vehicles. Unlike in previous cases, the vehicles covered by the latest recall use airbag inflators containing moisture-absorbing material. Nevertheless, Honda identified signs of degradation in the propellant material of several inflators in certain geographical areas following long-term monitoring and analysis. Toyota also warned that degradation of the propellant material could cause the inflator to rupture when the airbag deploys. Over the past decade, approximately 24 automotive manufacturers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide. Around 67 million of these vehicles were in the US. A defective inflator can cause the airbag canister to explode during deployment, sending metal fragments flying into the vehicle cabin. In several cases, the components have caused fatalities and injuries to drivers and passengers. Similar concerns have also emerged in Australia. Lexus has recalled more than 7,000 vehicles over concerns about the degradation of Takata airbag inflators. The recall covers several Lexus models, including the IS250, IS250C, IS350 and IS-F manufactured between 2005 and 2012. So far, it remains unclear whether other vehicles in Australia are also affected by the latest global recall programme. Owners of vehicles included in the recall can check their vehicle status through the Australian Government's official Vehicle Recalls website or contact the relevant manufacturer. Repairs through authorised dealerships, including the replacement of defective airbags, will be provided free of charge to vehicle owners. records.excerpt: Title: Honda Two-Wheeler Sales October 2026: Activa Crosses 3.86 Lakh, Total Volumes Rise 11% URL Source: http://www.autopunditz.com/post/honda-two-wheeler-sales-october-2026 Final URL: https://www.autopunditz.com/post/honda-two-wheeler-sales-october-2026 Published Time: 2026-11-21T07:45:01.912Z Markdown Content: 2 days ago 3 min read Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) recorded **6,64,831 units in October 2026**, registering 11% year-on-year growth over 5,98,946 units in October 2025. Dispatches also increased 4.4% month-on-month from 6,36,768 units in September 2026. Activa remained Honda's largest volume contributor, crossing 3.86 lakh units and accounting for 58.1% of total dispatches. Shine 125 retained second position, while CB350 and H'ness delivered strong annual growth. However, SP160, Dio 125 and Honda's electric scooters faced pressure across comparison periods. ## Honda October 2026 — Model-wise Sales Model Oct 2026 Oct 2025 YoY Sep 2026 MoM Activa 3,86,029 3,26,551+18%3,52,271+10% Shine 125 1,58,797 1,44,372+10%1,66,132−4% CB Unicorn 43,868 0 N/A 46,468−6% Shine 27,101 30,243−10%23,809+14% Dio 125 15,345 20,428−25%12,710+21% Dio 15,027 15,912−6%16,450−9% CB 125 Hornet 6,347 9,899−36%4,381+45% CB350 5,894 3,395+74%5,984−2% H'ness 3,393 2,056+65%3,568−5% SP160 1,104 5,756−81%1,820−39% QC1 789 0 N/A 1,464−46% Hornet 2.0 572 1,949−71%1,073−47% CB200X 387 1,053−63%400−3% Activa e:172 0 N/A 141+22% CBR1000RR 6 0 N/A 8−25% Other listed models*0 37,332−100%89−100% **Total****6,64,831****5,98,946****+11%****6,36,768****+4%** * **Activa:** Dispatches reached 3,86,029 units, increasing 18% YoY and 10% MoM. Activa contributed 58.1% of Honda's total October volumes and added 59,478 units over October 2025, accounting for approximately 90% of the company's net annual increase. * **Shine 125:** Recorded 1,58,797 units, up 10% YoY. However, volumes declined 4% from September's 1,66,132 units. It remained Honda's second-largest selling model, contributing 23.9% of total dispatches. * **CB Unicorn:** Registered 43,868 units, declining 6% MoM from 46,468 units in September. A direct annual comparison is not meaningful because the October 2025 data lists 32,825 units separately under CB Unicorn 160. * **Shine:** Dispatches stood at 27,101 units, down 10% YoY but up 14% MoM, indicating a sequential recovery despite remaining below last year's levels. * **Dio and Dio 125:** Dio recorded 15,027 units, declining 6% YoY and 9% MoM. Dio 125 posted 15,345 units, down 25% YoY, although monthly dispatches recovered 21%. * **CB125 Hornet:** Recorded 6,347 units, declining 36% YoY but rising 45% MoM from 4,381 units in September. The strong sequential improvement partially offset weaker annual performance. * **CB350 and H'ness:** CB350 sales increased 74% YoY to 5,894 units, while H'ness rose 65% to 3,393 units. Both models registered modest sequential declines of 2% and 5%, respectively. * **SP160:** Dispatches fell sharply to 1,104 units, down 81% YoY and 39% MoM, making it one of the weakest-performing models in Honda's October portfolio. * **Hornet 2.0 and CB200X:** Hornet 2.0 registered 572 units, declining 71% YoY and 47% MoM. CB200X recorded 387 units, falling 63% YoY and 3% MoM. * **QC1 and Activa e:** Honda's electric scooter portfolio recorded combined dispatches of 961 units. QC1 declined 46% MoM to 789 units, while Activa e: increased 22% MoM to 172 units. Electric scooters contributed just 0.14% of Honda's total monthly volumes. * **Premium and other models:** CBR1000RR recorded six units, while CB500, XL750, GL1800 and several other listed models reported zero dispatches during October 2026. ![Image 1: Honda October 2026 sales grew 11% YoY to 6,64,831 units, led by Activa with 3,86,029 units and Shine 125 with 1,58,797 units.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1da610_947e62537f4e4ca2b0d6275a70597d12~mv2.png/v1/crop/x_0,y_0,w_1086,h_1399/fill/w_1086,h_1399,al_c,q_90,enc_auto/1da610_947e62537f4e4ca2b0d6275a70597d12~mv2.png) _Honda October 2026 sales grew 11% YoY to 6,64,831 units, led by Activa with 3,86,029 units and Shine 125 with 1,58,797 units._ ## Auto Punditz Take Honda's October 2026 performance was overwhelmingly driven by Activa, which contributed nearly 90% of the company's net year-on-year volume increase. Together, Activa and Shine 125 accounted for approximately 82% of total dispatches, underlining Honda's continued dominance in mainstream commuter mobility. The encouraging growth of CB350 and H'ness indicates improving annual volumes in Honda's premium motorcycle portfolio, although smaller models such as SP160 and Hornet 2.0 faced significant declines. Meanwhile, the electric scooter business remained at a limited scale compared with Honda's established petrol-powered products. The key trend to watch is whether Honda can sustain Activa's growth while broadening its sales contribution through motorcycles, premium offerings and electric scooters, reducing its reliance on a single high-volume model.

records.title: Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million vehicles over Takata airbag rupture risk
records.excerpt: Honda and Toyota Motor said on Friday they are recalling about 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture. WASHINGTON — Honda and Toyota Motor said on Friday they are recalling about 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture. Honda and Toyota both said there were no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being recalled, and there have been no airbag inflator ruptures. The automakers will replace the airbag inflators in the recalled vehicles. There have, however, been at least 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009, an issue prompting the largest auto recall in U.S. history. All of those deaths involved airbag inflators without a drying agent. At least 20 of those deaths were in Honda vehicles. The vehicles in the current recalls have airbag inflators that contain a moisture-absorbing material — unlike the millions of vehicles recalled previously. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said analysis and inflator degradation simulation models conducted by independent testing groups allowed the automakers to act ahead of potential risks. “Honda and Toyota saw early evidence of degradation risk in certain of their vehicles and are currently conducting proactive recalls of vehicles,” NHTSA said late Friday, adding that other automakers continue to conduct inflator analysis and testing. The recall includes 810,592 older Honda cars and SUVs in the United States and 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the United States. The Toyota recall includes 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 IS250, 2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner models. The Honda recall covers some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles. The Honda recall covers vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperatures, humidity and large temperature fluctuations. Over the past decade, two dozen major automakers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide, including about 67 million vehicles in the United States. Various automakers have also reported hundreds of injuries in vehicles since 2009 from Takata airbag inflators that can explode, unleashing metal shrapnel inside cars and trucks, killing or injuring drivers or other vehicle occupants. Honda said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions. Toyota warned that degraded propellant could cause the inflator to rupture if the airbag deploys and cause serious injuries. The Honda recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, the Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa. Toyota did not specify in which U.S. states the recall applies but said it expects the replacement inflators will be ready by early 2027.

records.title: Honda's Epic S2000 Recalled For Potential Fuel Leaks
records.excerpt: Honda's Epic S2000 Recalled For Potential Fuel Leaks 2008 Honda S2000 finished in silver with red and black interior Honda Add CarBuzz on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Silvian Secara Published Nov 22, 2026, 2:00 PM EST Classic gems, tasteful customs, legendary supercars - for Silvian, they're all fair game. He's been in love with cars and motorcycles for as long as he can remember, so it made perfect sense to eventually turn that passion into a full-time writing career. Around six years and more than 3,000 articles later, he is still going strong and doesn't plan on hitting the brakes anytime soon. Sign in to your CarBuzz account The iconic S2000 sports car was discontinued back in 2009, but it will always be remembered as one of Honda’s all-time greats. Its high-revving character, near-perfect weight distribution, and analog charm make it an absolute blast to drive as you work your way up and down that six-speed manual gearbox. In short, there are plenty of things to love about Honda’s roadster, and we could go on forever about each and every one of them. Add CarBuzz on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover But that’s not what brings us here today. We are instead going to talk about a recall notice issued by Honda a few days ago, involving well over 16,000 vehicles in the United States. They are all S2000s of the AP2 variety, meaning the second generation introduced for the model-year 2004. So, what is this all about? Fuel Flange Joints Are The Main Culprits Here Honda The AP2-gen S2000 is the one powered by Honda’s 2.2-liter F22C1 engine, with the affected model-years being 2004 and 2005. A total of 16,387 vehicles are involved, risking fuel leaks that can lead to engine stalling, loss of acceleration, or the inability to start the engine at all. Besides that, flammable fluids leaking onto hot powertrain components is clearly a big no-no, but why is this even possible in the first place? According to Honda, it is believed that up to 67 replacement fuel flange joints have been improperly manufactured, so “without brazing material at the joint-to-flange connection.” This could lead to the connection coming loose over time, which would ultimately result in the aforementioned leaks and a loss of fuel pressure. Needless to say, that’s not the kind of superficial problem you can simply ignore. What Is Honda Doing To Remedy This? 2004-2009 Honda S2000 Front Angle View Honda The automaker will reach out to registered S2000 owners via snail mail in case their vehicle is among those affected. Then, said cars will have to be taken to authorized dealers who will inspect their flange joints for manufacturing defects and have them replaced if need be. Notification letters will reportedly be sent to owners by January 4, 2027. You can also find the recall notice on the NHTSA’s website, so feel free to search its database with your VIN and see if you should take further action. Honda’s customer service can be contacted for more information, too, with internal code LQD identifying this particular recall . Now, if you happen to own a 2004–2005 S2000, do yourself a favor and put your mind at ease sooner rather than later. CarBuzz Insight – Why This Matters: 2004-2009 Honda S2000 Rear Angle View Honda Sudden power loss, unexpected engine stalls, and even a potential fire hazard – there are many potential issues that could arise from this. And, according to some sources, Honda is thought to have produced just over 20,000 copies of its popular sports car for model-years 2004 and 2005. That means the vast majority of them are affected by this recall campaign, so it should be taken very seriously by everyone involved. Since the NHTSA has already updated its records with all the relevant VINs, we encourage you to go ahead and check if your S2000 is on the list right now. Sources: Honda, NHTSA
