records.excerpt: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援 – 日刊自動車新聞 2026.11.23(月) 管理者 紙面で読む 会社案内 各種申し込み 購読のご案内 ログイン 購読の ご案内 管理者 紙面で 読む ログイン 検索 トップ 自動車流通 開発・生産 行政・輸送 Home 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー お知らせ アーカイブ検索サイトメンテナンス終了のお知らせ アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー , 自動車メーカー , 人事・組織改正 2026年5月29日 11:30 SNSで共有: 井上勝史氏 ホンダと日立が出資する自動車部品メーカーのアステモ（東京都千代田区）は5月29日、ホンダの井上勝史取締役が7月1日付で社長CEO（最高経営責任者）に就任するトップ人事を内定したと発表した。竹内弘平社長CEOは退任する。6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。1963年10月22日生まれ、62歳。福岡県出身。 〈2026/5/29更新〉 SNSで共有: 関連記事 ホンダ、現実路線で四輪事業の収益改善へ 開発費・期間・工数を半減 「開発スピードは世界トップレベルに」 2026年5月15日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー , 企画・解説・オピニオン ホンダ、電動化戦略を見直し EV目標は撤回 2029年度までに次世代HV15モデル投入 新型セダンとアキュラSUVも公開 2026年5月14日 14:10 ｜ 自動車メーカー ホンダ、アステモを子会社化 ソフトやAI開発加速 新規株式公開も視野 2025年12月18日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー , 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー ホンダ系サプライヤー、EV戦略見直しに「補償求める」「量産前の決断歓迎」などの声 2026年3月13日 05:00 ｜ 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー 資本再編進む自動車サプライヤー 親子上場の解消 円安で外資も意欲 経営資源集中でEVやSDVに対応 2026年1月1日 05:00 ｜ 企画・解説・オピニオン , 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー トヨタ、FCトラックベースの地震体験車を公開 災害時の給電車としても 全国自治体に導入見通し 2026年11月21日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー アクセスランキング 直近 昨日 一週間 ランキングを読み込み中です。 ランキングを読み込み中です。 ランキングを読み込み中です。 ワンソクTubeのブログはこちら 【レクサス大丈夫か?!】2026年上半期の新車販売台数ランキングTOP50で異変! 意外な車が上位へ?! レクサスを叱咤激励するオーナーたちの意外な本音とは?! records.title: ナイキがF1のオフィシャルパートナーとして、アパレル＆ユニフォームサプライヤーに。2027年からの長期契約
records.excerpt: ナイキがF1のオフィシャルパートナーとして、アパレル＆ユニフォームサプライヤーに。2027年からの長期契約（オートスポーツweb） F1は、2027年にスポーツ関連ブランド、NIKE／ナイキをオフィシャルパートナーに迎え、長期的なパートナーシップ契約の下、同社… ナイキがF1のオフィシャルパートナーとして、アパレル＆ユニフォームサプライヤーに。2027年からの長期契約 オートスポーツweb 2026年11月21日 11時43分 F1は、2027年にスポーツ関連ブランド、NIKE／ナイキをオフィシャルパートナーに迎え、長期的なパートナーシップ契約の下、同社がF1のオフィシャル・アパレル＆ユニフォームサプライヤーに就任することを発表した。 この契約により、ナイキは、スタイル、パフォーマンス、ライフスタイルに焦点を当てたカプセルコレクションとして、フットウェア、アパレル、アクセサリーを展開するほか、パフォーマンス面の革新や、次世代のアスリートとファンに向けたレースウイークエンドの体験も提供するということだ。 2027年からナイキはF1のオフィシャルパートナー／公式アパレル＆ユニフォームサプライヤーを務め、世界各地で開催されるF1イベントにおいて、スタッフが着用する共同ブランドのユニフォームを製作する。 さらにファンは、『Formula 1 x Nike』のアパレル／スポーツウェアコレクションを入手することができ、第一弾として、ラスベガスGPの週末に、「ラスベガスGP × Nike」カプセルコレクションがF1ハブとナイキ・ラスベガス店で発売される。 なお、ナイキが、女性ドライバーのシリーズ、F1アカデミーのオフィシャルパートナーおよびオフィシャル・スポーツアパレル・パートナーを務めることも、併せて発表された。 [オートスポーツweb 2026年11月21日]

records.excerpt: Commercial Space Transportation | Federal Aviation Administration Skip to main content USA Banner An official website of the United States government Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. United States Department of Transportation Commercial Space Transportation Countdown to launch. The FAA has reached a historic milestone with successful launch and reentry operations. See Stats Here FAA Reaches 1,000 Licensed Space Operations August 14, 2025 marked the FAA’s 1,000th operation of a commercial space vehicle that the agency licensed or permitted. The United States is a leader in space exploration, and this milestone highlights more than 35 years of the FAA successfully fulfilling its mission to protect safety and advance the future of our skies. The commercial space transportation industry emerged in the 1990s and was primarily used to launch commercial satellites and transport cargo to the International Space Station (ISS). In just the last few years, growing interest in commercial space is realizing new possibilities for the industry including providing transportation to the ISS laboratories for research and space tourism. This rapidly growing industry is inspiring scientists, engineers, teachers, and a whole generation, to imagine entirely new possibilities for the future of space. Safety Safety is our North Star. Compliance, Enforcement & Mishap Legislation & Policies Operations We protect the public, property, and U.S. national security interests. Airspace Integration Commercial Space Data Licensing We license all U.S. commercial launches and reentries here and abroad. Environmental Licenses, Permits and Approvals Stakeholder Engagement Vehicle Operator Licenses Industry Outreach We work collaboratively with industry to promote safety. Aerospace Rulemaking Committees: (SpARCs) COMSTAC Standards Development International We work with our international partners to promote safety. International Affairs Spaceports U.S. Spaceports are critical infrastructure for the industry. Office of Spaceports Spaceports by State Commercial Space By The Numbers Spaceports Map Find a U.S. spaceport near you. Map to commercial, government, and active private spaceports around the country. Learn about U.S. Spaceports Jobs What do we do? What careers are in commercial space? Commercial Space Transportation ensures that rocket launches and reentries are safe. We do this by applying a broad range of skillsets to manage licensing and regulatory work, as well as many programs and initiatives. Some examples of the jobs we do include inspecting reusable and expendable launch vehicles, assessing aerospace vehicle systems, developing public safety standards and requirements, assuring engineering quality, and assessing environmental impacts. Why does it matter? Our efforts help facilitate both the U.S. and global commercial space transportation industry’s health and growth. We value the talents, ideas, and insights that will enable us to continue our mission of ensuring and promoting the safest commercial space transportation in the world. Join us in exploring this exciting, meaningful, and innovative field! How can I find out more and apply? We are actively hiring qualified people to help us grow our team to meet the global commercial space community’s increasing demands. If you would like to find out more about being part of an organization where the possibilities are literally limitless, please take a look at Commercial Space Careers and email us at 9-AST-Comm-Space-Careers@faa.gov . Back To Main Menu Membership Become A Member Renew Membership Gift Membership Kids Membership Other Ways to Give Contact Us Our Work Explore Space Take Action About Membership Member Community Account Center Search “Exploration is in our nature.” - Carl Sagan Starship’s triumph and Vulcan’s failure A tale of two rockets Written by Casey Dreier Chief of Space Policy, The Planetary Society November 19, 2026 On Nov. 14, after reaching orbit and deploying a batch of Starlink satellites, SpaceX’s Starship did something no fully reusable second stage had done before: It came home. Amid a din of sonic booms, Starship returned to its launch site and was caught by the “chopsticks” arms of the very tower that helped launch it. SpaceX Starship catch The upper stage of the SpaceX Starship megarocket shortly before being caught by robotic arms on its launch tower. Image: SpaceX The following day, a more conventional rocket, Vulcan, attempted to launch a payload of 40 Amazon Leo communications satellites. Vulcan is the new rocket from the Boeing-Lockheed Martin joint venture United Launch Alliance (ULA). It is a single-use medium-to-heavy-lift vehicle; its primary customer is the U.S. national security market. It was making a return-to-flight effort after a partial failure last year. It failed. The contrast could not be more stark: The world’s largest, most audacious rocket hit a historic milestone while a more conservative approach failed to reach orbit. SpaceX’s ongoing achievements further underscore its dominance over the U.S. launch industry, now so lopsided that both government and commercial space companies are functionally dependent on a single company to place their assets into space. But what happens if SpaceX no longer wants to prioritize launch services to its competitors? The lucre of space-based AI data centers and the company’s Starlink satellite business are so great that the CEO, Elon Musk, has stated the company will be winding down its Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets once Starship is flying reliably. Already, SpaceX has reportedly stopped accepting orders for future rideshare missions and stopped booking new commercial launches on Falcon. SpaceX appears to be more interested in using Starship to deploy space-based AI data centers as rapidly as possible rather than allocate its capacity to other customers. As a consequence, many in the space industry and in federal agencies with space-based assets are growing ever more anxious about the availability of launch vehicles in the coming years . As Vulcan’s recent failure demonstrates, there are no immediate alternatives to the Falcon 9. There are a handful of potential replacements: Rocket Lab’s Neutron, ULA’s Vulcan, Blue Origin’s New Glenn, and Relativity Space’s Terran R are all under development. But all are facing delays. In addition to Vulcan’s failed flight, New Glenn suffered a pad explosion that temporarily derailed its launch capacity, Neutron has been delayed to 2027 , and Terran R has shared no public timeframe for first launch. None of these will immediately replicate the reliability and launch cadence of the Falcon 9. This has major consequences for NASA’s space science missions. Since 2020, seven out of every 10 NASA launches have been on SpaceX rockets. And eight upcoming science missions, including Dragonfly , NEO Surveyor , and the Rosalind Franklin Rover , will launch on SpaceX rockets. NASA orbital launches per year SpaceX has grown to dominate NASA's launches to space since the Falcon was introduced. Image: Casey Dreier/The Planetary Society Starship, while capable of sending large payloads into space, currently has no means to deploy them once there. Its “Pez dispenser”-like deployment system is custom-designed for Starlink satellites, and incompatible with most military and NASA payloads. The company could feasibly make a disposable upper stage with a more standard payload fairing, but there are no indications this is a priority. And even then, some spacecraft going beyond the Moon would need a dedicated kick stage beyond what Starship could provide. At the moment, it appears that SpaceX will preserve some Falcon capacity for U.S. government needs, but exactly how much, and for how long, isn’t clear. It will be winding down the Dragon crew capsule , forcing NASA to rely on Boeing’s troubled Starliner for rides to low Earth orbit after 2030. The Space Launch System and Orion, once considered to be facing an inevitable cancellation in the wake of Starship, are now being put forward by the NASA Administrator as the agency’s primary long-term access to the Moon. At its core, the current conundrum is a function of SpaceX acting like a commercial company rather than a national asset. As Musk stated , it doesn’t make sense to retain limited engineering resources on older rockets such as Falcon when Starship is the company’s top priority. But this attitude is rare for the space industry, where reliability and conservatism have dominated for decades. SpaceX’s self-interested financial decision highlights the novel risks NASA and the nation have accepted with their move toward commercial-led launch: A private company does not have to provide launch services to outside customers, or even to the government. NASA’s goal of nurturing a commercial launch industry, where the space agency was just one of many customers, in effect worked too well: NASA is no longer a big enough customer for SpaceX. SpaceX remains the outlier in the launch industry. No other company has come close to competing on reliability or availability, nor, as recent events demonstrate, will do so anytime soon. The conservative approach does not appear to be a guaranteed path to stability, and NASA and other customers will have to hope that the aggregate capability of the launch industry can provide enough options in the near future to replace the capability SpaceX is now deploying inward for its own purposes. records.label: techtimes.com
records.title: SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 Splashdown Completes ISS Solar Upgrade, Returns Canadarm2 Robotic Arm Joint
records.excerpt: SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 splashdown on November 21, 2026 closed out the ISS Roll-Out Solar Array program, with Dragon C211 returning the eighth and final pair of Redwire-designed flexible iROSA solar... SpaceX's Cargo Dragon capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast on Friday, November 21, 2026, at 2:03 p.m. PST, closing out the CRS-35 resupply mission to the International Space Station. The recovery marked the successful end of a cargo run that quietly accomplished two of the most consequential hardware milestones in the station's recent operational history.Dragon Delivers and DepartsDragon C211 — on its fourth flight — launched October 13, 2026, at 6:33 a.m. EDT from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral on a Oct. 13 Falcon 9 launch of Booster B1096, making its eighth flight. Dragon docked to the Harmony module's forward port two days later and remained berthed for more than five weeks before undocking on November 20. The three-day weather delay caused by sustained high winds over the Pacific recovery zone pushed the original November 18 splashdown target to Friday.SpaceX recovery teams aboard the GO Navigator vessel retrieved the capsule and its cargo shortly after splashdown.The Final Pair of Solar ArraysThe headline cargo on the outbound leg of CRS-35 was a pair of ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays — the seventh and eighth iROSAs in the station's power upgrade program, and the last the station will ever receive. Each iROSA is a roll-out solar wing designed by Redwire Space: a flexible photovoltaic blanket that unfurls from a compact stowage cylinder like a roll of carpet and deploys to full span without any hinged rigid panels. The design allows the arrays to be packed tightly enough to fit inside Dragon's unpressurized trunk and still cover a surface area large enough to meaningfully supplement the station's aging original solar arrays.The installation program spread across four Dragon missions — CRS-22, CRS-26, CRS-28, and CRS-35 — beginning in June 2021 and concluding with the final pair installed on the station's 2A and 3B power channels in late October and early November. The completed eight-array suite delivers more than 160 kW supplemental power across all eight arrays, enough to cover the growing electricity demands of research facilities added to the station over the past decade while also providing margin for future expansion. With all eight iROSAs in place, Boeing's solar power system for the station is now operating at its fully upgraded configuration.Canadarm2 Wrist Joint Returns to EarthThe second major hardware story of CRS-35 traveled in the opposite direction: the failed wrist joint from the 17.6-meter robotic arm built by MDA for the Canadian Space Agency, which has been in continuous service since its launch aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis during mission STS-100 in April 2001. The arm is equipped with seven joints and can lift payloads of up to 116,000 kilograms — a capability that makes it indispensable for berthing Dragon capsules, repositioning large station components, and supporting spacewalking astronauts.On May 27, 2026, engineers monitoring the arm's performance telemetry detected that the wrist joint was drawing elevated motor current, a classic indicator of mechanical binding or bearing wear. Ground teams temporarily restricted the joint's range of motion while they developed a repair plan. The arm itself remained functional for essential operations, but the fault limited its full articulation and introduced risk into time-sensitive berthing and assembly tasks.On June 30, 2026, NASA astronauts Chris Williams and Jessica Meir conducted U.S. Spacewalk 95 — lasting 7 hours and 20 minutes — to remove the failed wrist joint assembly and install a spare that had been stored aboard the station. The procedure restored the arm to full articulation, and Canadarm2 returned to unrestricted operations the same day. The repaired arm was used to assist with subsequent payload handling, including support for the iROSA installation spacewalks in October and November.The failed joint, returned to Earth inside Dragon's pressurized cargo bay, will now be examined by MDA engineers. Physical analysis of flight hardware can reveal failure mechanisms that telemetry alone cannot — information that may inform maintenance schedules for Canadarm2's remaining joints, which have no planned replacement on the books as the station targets operations through the 2030s. ISS extension scenarios assume the arm continues to operate without a successor system.Science Cargo Returning to EarthDragon's pressurized cargo hold carried more than 6,300 pounds (2,858 kilograms) of return cargo, the largest portion of which was scientific samples and experiment hardware accumulated during the Expedition 75 crew rotation.Among the science cargo were bioprinted blood vessel constructs developed using the reduced-gravity environment of microgravity, which allows cells to self-organize in three dimensions without the structural support scaffolding that Earth-based printing requires. The samples will be analyzed to assess whether microgravity-printed vascular structures exhibit geometry and mechanical properties comparable to native tissue — a capability that could have implications for pharmaceutical testing and, ultimately, for the bioprinting of transplantable grafts.Also returning: antibiotic-resistant bacterial cultures cultivated during the mission, protein crystal samples grown for a JAXA pharmaceutical structure-determination study, and blood and urine samples from the Expedition 75 crew for long-duration spaceflight health monitoring.Dragon C211's RecordDragon C211 has now completed four cargo missions: CRS-26, CRS-29, CRS-33, and CRS-35. SpaceX's reusable Dragon capsules are refurbished between flights and can carry both pressurized and unpressurized cargo in their trunk section. The trunk — which is not recovered and reenters the atmosphere after splashdown — carried the iROSA hardware on the outbound leg of CRS-35 and was jettisoned before reentry on the return.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhat did SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 deliver to the ISS?CRS-35 delivered the seventh and eighth ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays — the final pair of Redwire-designed flexible solar wings to be installed on the station — along with science experiments, crew provisions, and hardware. The solar arrays were installed on the 2A and 3B power channels in October and November 2026, completing the station's iROSA upgrade program.Why was the CRS-35 Dragon splashdown delayed?The original splashdown target of November 18, 2026 was pushed back three days due to high winds over the Pacific recovery zone. NASA and SpaceX stood down from the November 18 attempt and rescheduled after weather conditions improved. Dragon ultimately splashed down on November 21 at 2:03 p.m. PST.What is Canadarm2 and why was its wrist joint repaired?Canadarm2 is a 17.6-meter robotic arm built by MDA for the Canadian Space Agency, in service on the ISS since April 2001. It is used to berth visiting spacecraft, move large components, and support spacewalking astronauts. In May 2026, its wrist joint began drawing elevated motor current, indicating mechanical wear. NASA astronauts Chris Williams and Jessica Meir replaced the faulty joint during U.S. Spacewalk 95 on June 30, 2026, restoring the arm to full operation. The failed joint returned to Earth aboard CRS-35 for engineering analysis.How many iROSA solar arrays does the ISS now have?Eight. The ISS Roll-Out Solar Array program installed arrays across four SpaceX Dragon cargo missions — CRS-22 (June 2021), CRS-26 (November 2022), CRS-28 (June 2023), and CRS-35 (October–November 2026). Each array sits atop one of the station's existing solar wing masts and supplements its power output. All eight are now installed and operational.

records.title: SpaceX launches intelligence-gathering satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office
records.excerpt: The NROL-136 mission was the fourth launch of the year supporting the agency’s proliferated architecture satellite constellation in low Earth orbit. Liftoff from pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base happened at 4:23 a.m. PST (7:23 a.m. EST / 1223 UTC). Falcon 9 SpaceX launches intelligence-gathering satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office Will Robinson-Smith November 21, 2026 4:50 p.m. A Falcon 9 rocket stands poised to launch from the Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. File Photo: SpaceX Update Nov. 22, 8 a.m. EST (1300 UTC): SpaceX landed its booster at Landing Zone 4. SpaceX launched a batch of intelligence-gathering satellites to low Earth orbit on behalf of the National Reconnaissance Office on Sunday morning. Its Falcon 9 rocket took off from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, smashing the pad turnaround record at the site by more than 23 hours. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for 4:23 a.m. PST (7:23 a.m. EST / 1223 UTC). It came 32 hours, 3 minutes, and 21 seconds after the launch of the USSF. The previous turnaround was set back in June at 55 hours, 48 minutes, and 21 seconds. Prior to Sunday morning, SpaceX’s overall pad turnaround record was 45 hours, set by back-to-back Starlink flights from Cape Canaveral Space Force Base in Florida in January. The mission, designated NROL-136, will add an undisclosed number of satellites to the NRO’s satellite constellation that it refers to as its proliferated architecture. This was the fourth such launch this year and the 15th to date. Plays from YouTube SpaceX launched the mission using the Falcon 9 first stage booster with the tail number B1097. This was its 14th flight following the launches of NROL-172, USSF-259, Transporter-17, Twilight, Sentinel-6B, and eight batches of Starlink satellites. Roughly 7.5 minutes after liftoff, B1097 touched down at Landing Zone 4, adjacent to the launch pad. This was the 38th landing at this site and the 680th Falcon booster landing to date. records.title: SpaceX's Cursor is exploring phasing out Chinese AI models over geopolitical risk
records.excerpt: SpaceX's Cursor is exploring a phase-out of Chinese AI models Subscribe Politics & Government SpaceX's Cursor is exploring phasing out Chinese AI models over geopolitical risk Cursor told two House committees about the plan as lawmakers examine U.S. firms' adoption of Chinese AI models By Ella Rodrigo · 2 min read · Updated November 20, 2026 Add QZ to Google Samuel Boivin / NurPhoto via Getty Images Cursor, the AI coding platform owned by SpaceX, is exploring a phase-out of Chinese-developed AI models because of geopolitical risk, according to CNBC . The plan appears in a report from the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Select Committee on China that is due for publication Friday, according to CNBC. The document says Cursor "informed the Committees" that it would "explore phasing out PRC [People's Republic of China]-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk." Cursor built its coding model Composer 2 on Kimi K2.5, a model from Chinese lab Moonshot AI, according to CNBC. SpaceX said in June that it had formally agreed to purchase Cursor, and it closed the transaction in August, valuing the equity at an implied $60 billion. SpaceX is building its Grok line of models, and Cursor has contributed to training them. The report comes after an inquiry lasting several months into how Chinese AI models made their way into U.S. technology infrastructure, according to CNBC. Airbnb $ABNB and DoorDash were also involved in the investigation, which asked about how they use Chinese models. The investigation concluded that Chinese models are being adopted largely because they are cheap, customizable and close to frontier-level performance, according to CNBC. The U.S. has yet to produce an open-weight rival that is competitive on "price and performance the market demands," the report says. The report recommends a "national American open-weight initiative" that would pool government-provided computing resources, common infrastructure for evaluating models, and "lawful access" for training purposes on America's frontier models, according to CNBC. It also says the order disclosed in October that barred DeepSeek from federal civilian agency systems should be broadened to bar "PRC-developed AI models" from federal information systems and from work done under federal contracts. Cursor, SpaceX and DoorDash did not respond to a request for comment from CNBC. Airbnb declined to comment. U.S. business leaders have split over the use of Chinese models. OpenAI Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar warned businesses in October that adopting Chinese AI models carries cybersecurity risks and urged them to favor Western alternatives. Nvidia $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang said in July that American companies should be free to use Chinese open-source models , arguing that openness makes AI more secure. records.title: SpaceX Sets 32 Hour Falcon 9 Launch Turnaround Record
records.excerpt: SpaceX launched two Falcon 9 rockets from the same California pad 32 hours apart, setting a new turnaround record while advancing classified satellite missions. Rapid launch operations at California's Vandenberg Space Force Base reached a new milestone on November 22, 2026, when SpaceX sent another Falcon 9 rocket into orbit for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). The mission, designated NROL-136, followed another launch from the same pad just 32 hours earlier, establishing a new turnaround record.The rocket departed Launch Complex-4E at 4:23 a.m. local time, carrying classified satellites toward low Earth orbit. According to Space.com, the interval between the two launches was precisely 32 hours, 3 minutes and 21 seconds.SpaceX's previous record for consecutive launches from a single pad was 45 hours, achieved at Pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The latest achievement brings the company closer to its stated goal of reducing launch preparation time to 24 hours.Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, credited the company's West Coast team for the accomplishment in a November 22 post on X."Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin.Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Dontchev said.The NROL-136 mission also continued the intelligence agency's expansion of its proliferated satellite network. According to the NRO, the architecture is intended to strengthen global surveillance coverage and improve the resilience of U.S. intelligence operations in space.NROL-136 represented the network's 15th dedicated deployment mission and the NRO's sixth launch of 2026. SpaceX and Northrop Grumman developed the satellite architecture in partnership with the agency, which began deploying the constellation in May 2024 through the NROL-146 mission.The NRO has not disclosed how many satellites NROL-136 carried or provided details about their onboard equipment. All six of its launches during 2026 have used Falcon 9 rockets to deliver classified payloads into low Earth orbit, according to Space.com.The rocket's first-stage booster separated approximately two minutes after liftoff before returning to Vandenberg. It landed at Landing Zone 4 around seven and a half minutes after launch, completing another recovery operation.The booster, identified as B1097, completed its 14th flight. Its previous assignments included NASA's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 and eight Starlink missions.Separately, SpaceX is pursuing another major development in reusable launch technology through its Starship program. Ship 42, the first Starship upper stage successfully caught by the launch tower's mechanical arms, will not return to flight despite being considered technically capable of flying again.Speaking at the TomorrowX Summit on November 18, SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk explained that the company intends to preserve the vehicle because of its historical significance."In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said.Ship 42 completed Starship's 15th test flight, launched November 13, and returned to the company's Starbase facility in South Texas the following day. Musk said the vehicle had performed well enough that it could potentially fly again after several weeks of refurbishment.The recovery marked a significant step toward SpaceX's ambition of developing a fully reusable orbital transportation system. Before that mission, the company had successfully caught its Super Heavy first-stage booster three times and reflown a booster twice, but had never caught a Starship upper stage."Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," Musk said.SpaceX also plans to use Starship to deploy much larger satellite networks. The next-generation Starlink constellation is planned to contain approximately 100,000 satellites, while the proposed Starmind AI data-center constellation is expected to be 10 times larger.The company has already begun deploying next-generation Starlink hardware. Ship carried 26 of the new internet satellites during Flight 14, launched September 28, and repeated the deployment during Flight 15.

records.title: AnthropicとSpaceX、IPO主幹事に競合他社との取引禁止を要求…ウォール街で「横暴」論争
records.excerpt: Anthropicが813億ドル（約12.9兆円）規模のIPOを推進するにあたり、主幹事証券会社の核心人材に対し、上場後6カ月間OpenAIなど競合他社の業務を禁じる条件を要求していたことが明らかになった。人員を4人に制限し、午前2時の緊急書類承認を求め、グリーンシュー（追加割当）手数料を未払いとするなどの条件も併せて課した。SpaceXも同様の一方的な条件を提示しており、ウォール街では大型発行体と投資銀行の間の力関係が変わったとの分析が出ている。 米国の人工知能（AI）企業Anthropicが史上最大規模の新規株式公開（IPO）を推進するなか、主幹事証券会社に前例のない水準の制約条件を課していた事実が明らかになった。競合他社との業務を一定期間禁じる条項から、人員投入の制限、未明の時間帯における緊急書類承認の要求まで含まれており、ウォール街の内外で反発が起きている。 22日（現地時間）の外信報道によると、Anthropicは19日のナスダック上場を控え、IPOを担当した投資銀行（IB）チームの核心人材に対し、上場後6カ月間、OpenAI、Cursor、DeepSeek、Hugging Faceなど競合企業に関連する業務を担当しないとする内容の法的文書への署名を求めた。一部の銀行の高位役員がこれへの署名を拒否したとの話も伝わっている。 金融機関は通常、顧客の機密保護と利益相反管理のための内部規程を設けているが、個々の職員に対し特定の競合他社との業務を6カ月間全面禁止する条件を求めるのは極めて異例だ。あるIB関係者は、AI関連の大型上場が相次ぐと予想される状況で、6カ月間競合他社に関与しないと約束する人材を確保するのは容易ではなかったと語った。 人員構成にも制限が付いた。Anthropicは22の引受金融機関のうち一部について、案件に投入する人数を4人以内に減らし、必ず高位職でなければならないとする条件を提示した。会社情報の流出を防ぐための措置と解釈されるが、一部の銀行は業務過程で人員制限を迂回する形で対応したとされる。 情報アクセスの統制も強化された。Anthropicは通常のPDFファイルではなく、文書の閲覧履歴がすべて記録され、複製保存が不可能な「NetRoadshow」プラットフォームを通じて大半の証券会社と情報を共有した。文書には担当銀行員の個人名が透かしとして刻まれた。 切迫した日程も混乱を助長した。10日の販売活動開始を前に、証券会社には誤った公募価格帯と株式数が記載された書類が先に送付され、訂正されたS-1A書類はニューヨーク時間の午前2時ごろにようやく届いた。銀行は米国証券取引委員会（SEC）への提出期限に間に合わせるため、わずか数時間で検討と承認を終えなければならなかった。 先に6月に上場を果たしたSpaceXの条件はさらに一方的だったとの評価もある。ゴールドマン・サックスやMorgan Stanleyなど主幹事に対し、手数料の規模すら知らせないまま契約書への署名を求め、銀行ごとに確保すべき投資家の類型と注文規模を指定して通知した。AnthropicとSpaceXはいずれも、追加割当オプション（グリーンシュー）で販売される追加株式については引受手数料を一切支払わない方針としたと伝えられている。 項目 Anthropic SpaceX 上場時期 2026年11月19日 2026年6月 調達規模 813億ドル（約12.9兆円） 史上最大記録更新前の基準 主幹事数 22社 複数 引受手数料 約5.5億ドル（約870億円） 非公開 競合他社業務の制限 6カ月、核心人材対象 別段の制限は確認されず グリーンシュー手数料 未払い 未払い 注：調達規模と手数料はAnthropic基準 Anthropicの今回の上場は813億ドル（約12.9兆円）を調達し、6月にSpaceXが打ち立てた最大IPO記録を上回った。22の引受金融機関が受け取る引受手数料は約5.5億ドル（約870億円）に達する。巨額の手数料にもかかわらず、一部の銀行関係者はAnthropicが上場過程の全体を過度に統制したと指摘する。 市場では技術企業とウォール街の間の力関係が変わったとの分析が出ている。フロリダ大学のJay Ritter名誉教授は、これらの企業が市場支配力を背景に、引受団に対して通常とは異なる条件を要求できる交渉力を確保したと評価した。ただ株価の動きは厳しい。SpaceXは6月16日に201.8ドル（約3.2万円）の高値をつけた後、7月中旬には135ドル（約2.1万円）の公募価格を下回った。Anthropicは上場初日に17%急騰したものの、その後AI関連株の調整に見舞われ、直近では8.5%下落して取引を終えた。 今回の件は、今後のAI企業の上場ラッシュにおいて、主幹事の選定や手数料交渉の慣行に影響を与え得るとの見方を生んでいる。大型発行体が有利な条件を貫徹する事例が繰り返されれば、引受団の収益性や人員配置戦略にも変化が避けられないとの指摘だ。Anthropicと主幹事のゴールドマン・サックス、Morgan Stanleyはコメント要請に応じず、SpaceXも回答しなかった。

records.title: Anthropicの記録的IPO：2兆ドル評価、OpenAI、SpaceX、そしてAIの未来｜Sourcery
records.excerpt: Anthropicの記録的IPO？OpenAI、SpaceX、そしてAIの未来｜Sourcery — BigGo ファイナンス リアルタイム ウォッチリスト 保有株 市場 決算説明会 イベントカレンダー Podcast 要人動向 Anthropicの記録的IPO？OpenAI、SpaceX、そしてAIの未来 Host Molly Guest Apoorv Agrawal 3 日前 00:51:34 en Sourcery 今回のポイント AltimeterのApoorv Agrawal氏は、Anthropicの資本効率の高い超成長（売上1ドルあたりの計算コストが88セントから15セントへ低下）が、噂される1.5〜2兆ドル規模のIPOを正当化すると主張する。背景には10〜15GWの計算資源不足が形作るAI構築の広がりがある。 要約 Altimeterのグロース投資家であるApoorv Agrawalは、AIへの設備投資はまだ「初回」の段階に過ぎないと主張する。そしてAnthropicを稀有なビジネスだと評する——年率10倍で成長し、黒字で、資本効率も高く、IPOを控えた先行売上高倍率は11〜14倍という妥当な水準にある、と。対談の大半はAI経済の形に費やされている。約8,600億ドルに上るビッグテックの設備投資がどこに向かっているのか、収益の積み上げ構造がクラウド時代とどう異なるのか、そしてAnthropic、OpenAI、SpaceX、Google、オープンソース推論がそれぞれ彼の言う「AIの四季」にどう当てはまるのか。タイトルが掲げるAnthropicのIPOについて語られるのは主に終盤の数分と、中盤のS-1分析の箇所であり、エピソードの大部分は市場地図の解説である。 Agrawalはスタンフォード大学でAIスタックの講座を教えており、議論は5層モデル（チップ、データセンター、インフラ、モデル、アプリケーション／エージェント）を軸に組み立てられる。ホストのMollyが彼を導きながら、設備投資、エージェント化への移行、オープンソースの経済性、SpaceXの計算資源レンタル事業、GoogleのTPUクラウド、スタートアップの成長ベンチマーク、サイバーセキュリティ分野のAIを掘り下げていく。読み手は、各層を裏付ける具体的な数字と、Agrawalが次に価値が蓄積すると見る領域についての明確な見解を持ち帰ることになるだろう。 ビッグテックのAI設備投資は、GDP比ですでに過去のあらゆる技術ブームを上回っている Agrawalは、ビッグテックのAI設備投資を今年約8,600億ドルと見積もる。2年間で3倍以上に増え、今や米国の国防費に匹敵する規模だという。過去1世紀のブーム——鉄道、石油・ガス、通信、シェール——とGDP比で比べても、AI支出はすでにそのすべてを超えている。彼が投げかける未解決の問いは、これが鉄道ブームの曲線の頂点なのか、それともまだ登っている途中なのか。彼自身の答えは「サイクルはまだ早い」だ。 より興味深いのは収益の積み上げ構造の比較だ。クラウド経済とAI経済は、ほぼ逆の形をしている。 層 クラウド経済（概算） AI経済（概算） モデル・アプリ（最上層） 約6,000億ドル（Salesforce、Adobe、ServiceNowの合計） 約1,400〜1,500億ドル インフラ 約3,000億ドル（クラウド各社） — 半導体（最下層） 年約800億ドル はるかに大きく、最上層を支える クラウド時代には、ソフトウェアの収益がその下のシリコンを圧倒していた。AIでは、シリコンの層が、それが支えるモデル・アプリの収益よりはるかに大きい——まさに鏡像だ。Agrawalはこれをモバイル時代のマネタイズのパターンに重ねて読み解く。第1回は半導体に蓄積し、第2回はインフラとそれを可能にするデバイスに、第3回以降はソフトウェアとアプリに蓄積する。AI経済は2〜3年で約6倍に成長した一方、アプリ・モデル層は同じ期間に約100倍に成長した、と彼は指摘する。 チャットボットからエージェント型AIへのフェーズシフトは、2025年末から2026年にかけて起きた ChatGPT時代のユースケース——知識の検索、旅行計画、「答えを見つける」こと——が利用の約80%を占めていた。2025年末から2026年初めのある時点で、市場はエージェント時代に入った、とAgrawalは言う。長時間稼働するエージェントやエージェントの群れ（スウォーム）であり、現在ではコーディングとエージェント型自動化がエージェント利用の約80%を占める。これは技術者だけの話ではないと彼は強調する。営業、マーケティング、サポート、投資チーム（Altimeter自身を含む）が大量のエージェントを動かしている。 彼は第3のフェーズを予想し、候補を挙げつつも断定はしない。プロアクティブ型エージェント（ニュース製品「instinct」と「dots」を例に挙げる）、超長時間稼働のエージェントとスウォーム、そしてより大きなモデルが小さなモデルに「手術」を施して改善する、といったものだ。 導入が加速しているのか頭打ちなのかについて、AgrawalはOpenAIのデータを引く。上位10%の顧客は直近約18か月で利用量が17倍になった一方、中央値の顧客は2倍にとどまった——「フロンティア企業」と中央値企業の差は広がっている。Cursorのデータでは、上位10%のユーザーが全トークンの3分の2を占める。彼は、パワーユーザーではない多数派こそが最大のギャップであり、サイクルがまだ早いと考える理由だと述べる。インターネットの普及（ほぼ完全に普及したと彼は言う）とは異なるというわけだ。 「Anthropicに10万ドル以上を支払うFortune 500の顧客は、それが総経費の0.1%未満だと話しています。導入はまだ早い。私たちはこのすべての第1回にいるのです。」 AnthropicのS-1が示すのは、急成長し、資本効率が高く、多角化したビジネス AgrawalはAnthropicを「驚異的なビジネス」と呼び、S-1は研究するのが楽しかったと語る。グロース投資家としての彼の基準はシンプルだ——優れたビジネスかどうか、そして優れた価格で手に入るかどうか。Anthropicはその両方を満たすと彼は主張する。主要な数字は以下の通り。 売上高は過去3年間、毎年10倍で成長。第3四半期の売上高は約170億ドルで、史上最速のスケールアップだと彼は言う。「しかも、他を大きく引き離している」 年間10万ドル以上を支払う顧客が約12,000社、100万ドル以上が約1,900社——特定顧客への依存がない多角化した基盤 純収益維持率（NRR）は900% 売上高1ドルあたりの提供コストは、計算資源88セントから15セントに低下し、粗利率は約85% 現在の規模に到達するまでに消費したキャッシュは100億ドル未満——この資本効率は打ち破るのが難しいだろうとAgrawalは言う 彼が強調するのはAnthropicの計算資源戦略だ。TPU、Trainium、Nvidia GPUにまたがる異種混在の計算資源をオーケストレーションし、希少な計算能力をマネタイズしている（ワットあたり約16ドルから約60ドルに上昇したと彼は言う）。価格については、噂される1.5〜2兆ドルのIPOレンジを、下限で先行GAAP売上高の11倍、上限で14倍と位置づける——「無謀な倍率ではなく」、現在の比較対象企業に対して妥当だと。短期的にも長期的にも非常に成功するIPOになると予想しつつ、目先は「荒波」もあり得ると留保する。 「一年には四季があります。私はそれをAnthropic、OpenAI、SpaceX、Googleと呼んでいます。」 フロンティアは2研究所の競争、オープンソースは常緑の季節 Agrawalはこの市場を「皇帝たちのゲーム」と表現し、これまでは最も大きな貸借対照表を持つ者が勝ってきたと述べる。彼が見るフロンティア研究所は2つ——「はるか先頭を走っている」と彼が言うAnthropicと、「信じられないほどの回復力と脆さ」を見せてきたと評するOpenAIだ。OpenAIについて：ChatGPTのユーザーは12億人超。2025年末から2026年初めにかけて「コードレッド」態勢に入った。モデル（Astra）と製品（Codex、ChatGPTのワーク製品）は第3四半期に好調だった。そして営業面のリーダーシップを強化し、Dolly Roick（Wiz元CRO）、Brian McCarthy（Coursera元CEO、SpaceX出身）、Chad Beatsを迎えた。OpenAIは9月末時点で年換算売上高約500億ドルと、自社の年末ガイダンスを上回った。 対照的に、オープンソースは「常緑の季節」だ。Agrawalのメンタルモデルはこうだ。AI支出全体の20〜30%がオープンソースに流れ、過半はクローズドに流れる。現在のフロンティアのオープンソースモデルは、およそ半年前のクローズドのフロンティアがいた位置にあり、その差は一貫して保たれている。レジが鳴るのは推論の層——Base 10、Fireworks、Modal——であり、彼はこれがクラウド市場に似た形になると予想する。強いプレイヤーが複数いて、支配的な1社はいない。Jonathan Ross（Groq CEO）が、全推論の99%を約35社が動かしていると語ったことを引き合いに出す。上位5社は研究所であり、続く30社はCursorや「instinct」のようなAIネイティブのスタートアップだ。 顧客がオープンソースを選ぶ理由は、コントロール、コスト、そして主権の合流だ。インテリジェンスを借りるのではなく所有すること、独自のインタラクションデータで小さなモデルをファインチューニングすること、推論コストを削減すること。彼は、OpenAIがBase 10と組んだ提携（エピソードの2週間ほど前に発表）を挙げる。大口顧客がOpenAIのクレジットをオープンソースモデルに充当できるようにするもので、OpenAIが「研究所という水準を超えてプラットフォームになろうとしている」証拠だと見る。 SpaceXとGoogleは、ハイパースケーラー的な姿に至る2つの異なる道を示す Agrawalは、ハイパースケーラーの形に至る道はいくつもあると主張する。Base 10とその同業各社はオープンソースの道を進み、ルーティング、サンドボックス、プラットフォームツールでスタックを上へと登っている（Base 10はエピソードの前日にプラットフォームに関する発表を行った）。SpaceXはインフラの道を進む。 SpaceXの直近の決算は、年換算売上高約600億ドルの企業を明らかにしたと彼は言う。およそ半分がAI部門、約3分の1がStarlink、残りが打ち上げ事業だ。AI部門は第3四半期に相対市場シェアを20%以上伸ばし、経営陣は今年末までに年換算1,000億ドル、来年末までに5,000億ドル以上へと自信を持ってガイダンスを示した。AgrawalはSpaceXの強みを「原子とビットの両方」をオーケストレーションする点に置く。大規模インフラを素早く構築し、その後ビジネスモデルを革新して最大限のレントを得る。計算資源は長期リースではなくスポット価格で貸し出す——長期のネオクラウドリースがワットあたり10〜20ドルなのに対し、約25〜50ドルで、CFOは上限寄りを示唆した。これが成り立つのは、Anthropicのような最先端モデルが計算資源をワットあたり50〜100ドルでマネタイズしているからで、双方にとって win-win となり、SpaceXはほとんどのネオクラウドが2〜3年かかる設備投資の回収を1年未満で済ませられる。SpaceXは今年末に約3ギガワットの計算資源で終え、来年は約13ギガワットへとガイダンスを示していると見られる。Agrawalは明らかなリスクを指摘する。スポット価格は年間リースに対するAirbnb的な貸し出しのようなもので、Anthropicのような顧客による更新は不確実だ。 Googleについては「二都物語」と彼は呼ぶ。年換算売上高約2,500億ドルで12%成長する検索事業と、その半分の規模ながら8倍速く成長するクラウド事業——年換算約1,200億ドル、前年比103%。このクラウド事業はTPUを組み込んでおり、Anthropicが顧客であり、OpenAIがTPUを検討しているとの噂があり、Oracleが初期の外部クラウドプロバイダーであり、AnthropicはBroadcomと組んでTPUをリースする契約を結んでいる。彼はGoogleを、1社の中で起きる世代交代と季節の移り変わりだと総括する。 成長ベンチマークはリセットされた——10億ドルで10倍、100億ドルで3倍、1,000億ドルで倍増 Agrawalは古い「トリプル・トリプル・ダブル・ダブル」の定石を更新する。数十億ドル規模では、今や10倍がベンチマークだ——Cursorは今年10億ドルから100億ドルへ向かうと噂され、Cognitionも同様にスケールし、Base 10は2年間10倍で成長してきた。数百億ドル規模では、3倍が最高水準——OpenAIは2025年を年換算約200〜210億ドルで終え、2026年は約780億ドルで終えると見込まれている。数千億ドル規模では、倍増が最高水準——Googleのクラウドが1,200億ドルで100%超の成長というのが彼の例だ。より優れたベンチマーク手法があれば教えてほしい、と彼は呼びかける。 スタートアップの評価について、彼は優れた創業チームが出発点であり先行指標、数字は遅行指標だと述べる。Michael Truell（Cursor）をこれまで会った中で最も優れた若手創業者の一人として挙げ、Bob McGrew（Altimeterのかつての同僚、PayPal初期、Palantirの2人目のエンジニア、OpenAIでエンジニアリングと研究を統括）を、野心的な新事業を率いる驚異的な創業者として挙げる。 サイバーセキュリティは最大の新興AIワークロードであり、フロンティア研究所がそれを取り込む ソフトウェアエンジニアリング（最大のAIワークロード）と集中したクオンツ金融の支出に加え、Agrawalはサイバーを最大の新興市場と見る。彼はこれをいたちごっこと位置づける。攻撃側は今や、あらゆるドアと窓を探り、最も重大な脆弱性を突く強力なツールキットを持っている。彼は、Google Chrome——毎日約10億人が利用する——で「demur」とExpoのチームが見つけた脆弱性を挙げる。攻撃者がボタン一つ、電話一本もなしに、ワンクリックでコンピューターを制御できるものだった。防御側のAI支出は攻撃側に対抗して（「火には火を」）急増すると彼は予想し、フロンティア能力が最も重要であるため、フロンティア研究所（OpenAI、Anthropic）がその需要を取り込むと考える。周囲のExpoのようなハーネスが、年1回ではなく継続的なテストを可能にするからだ。 注目すべき点 このエピソードが未解決のまま残す論点はタイミングだ。Agrawalの強気シナリオは、導入がまだ早いこと（Fortune 500の経費の0.1%）、計算資源のマネタイズが高い水準にとどまること（Anthropicでワットあたり50〜100ドル）、そして倍率が妥当な水準にとどまること（先行ベースで11〜14倍）に依拠している。弱気シナリオは彼自身の留保に埋め込まれている。スポット価格の計算資源は更新次第であり、直近の米国データセンターの結果は来年の予測から10〜15ギガワットを削る可能性があり（小規模なネオクラウドには存亡に関わる打撃となる一方、ハイパースケーラーは吸収する）、IPOは「荒波」に遭うかもしれない。彼が挙げる目先のカタリストはAnthropicのIPOそのものであり、研究する幸運に恵まれた中で最高のビジネスだと彼は言う。そして短期的な変動にかかわらず、1兆ドル企業になると予想している。 関連企業 ANT 3.96% SPCX 3.65% GOOGL 4.53% NVDA 8.27% AMZN 3.85% MSFT 3.2% META 3.95% 注目ポイント OpenAIはBase Tenと提携し、大口顧客がOpenAIのクレジットをオープンソースモデルに充当できるようにした。ラボからプラットフォームへの移行であり、オープンソース需要が無視できないほど大きいことを認めた動きだ。 OpenAIは上級営業リーダーを採用して市場開拓体制を再構築した。ゲストはモデルと製品のアップグレードと並んで、この点を第3四半期の好調な売上に寄与した要因として挙げている。 SpaceXは計算資源を長期リースではなくスポット価格で収益化し、設備投資を1年未満で回収する。典型的なネオクラウドの2〜3年と対照的であり、インフラ構築の速さに重ねたビジネスモデルの革新だ。 Anthropicのようなフロンティアラボは、ワットあたり50〜100ドルで収益化できるため、割高なスポット計算資源を利用できる。大手ラボが計算資源に制約されているとき、相互に有益な取り決めが生まれる。 注目の発言 AI支出全体のおよそ20〜30%はオープンソースに回る。大半はクローズドソースだが、より小さな部分がオープンソースになる。そしてそこも収益化される。 今日の最高のフロンティア・オープンソースモデルは、6か月前のクローズド・フロンティアがいた地点にある。つまり6か月前のフロンティアを買う気があれば、オープンソースがそれを与えてくれる。 その知能を借りるのではなく、所有するのだ。 SpaceXはこれをスポット価格で貸している。典型的なネオクラウドなら1〜3年の長期リースを買える……SpaceXの短期計算資源はそのおよそ2倍だ。 これはAnthropicにとっての勝利であり……SpaceXにとっても勝利だ。設備投資を1年未満で回収できるのは驚異的で、ほとんどのネオクラウドは設備投資の回収に2〜3年かかる。 この売上を達成すれば、先に話したフロンティアラボより大きくなる……それはビットの編成とアトムの編成の両方に極めて長けているという強みから来ている。 トピック AI設備投資とデータセンター構築 AnthropicのS-1とIPO AIの四季 エージェント型AI時代への移行 オープンソース推論の経済性 SpaceXのAI計算事業 GoogleのTPUとクラウド成長 AI導入のべき乗則 サイバーセキュリティにおけるAI スタートアップの成長ベンチマーク 関連ニュース アルティメーターのアプールブ・アグラワル氏：アンソロピックの15セントの計算コストが1.5兆ドルIPOを正当化する 3 日前 ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ 関連エピソード SemiAnalysis 第41回 - 緊急：AnthropicのS-1が公開（トークノミクス／市場） AnthropicのS-1は、すでに黒字で、売上が前年比13.7倍に伸びる一方で計算コスト

records.excerpt: PANews 11月22日付の情報：The Kobeissi Letterの投稿によると、Anthropicの現金および現金同等物は記録的な2370億ドルに達し、Alphabet（$GOOGL）、Amazon（$AMZN）、SpaceX（$SPCX）、Apple（$AAPL）の4社の現金準備の合計を上回った。この額はNVIDIAの現金残高の8倍、Microsoftの12倍、Metの22倍でもある。参考として、Berkshire Hathawayの現金準備は3770億ドル。Anthropicの資金源には、IPOで調達した810億ドルと、特定の投資家向け私募で得た260億ドルが含まれる。 PANews 11月22日付の情報：The Kobeissi Letterの投稿によると、Anthropicの現金および現金同等物は記録的な2370億ドルに達し、Alphabet（$GOOGL）、Amazon（$AMZN）、SpaceX（$SPCX）、Apple（$AAPL）の4社の現金準備の合計を上回った。この額はNVIDIAの現金残高の8倍、Microsoftの12倍、Metの22倍でもある。参考として、Berkshire Hathawayの現金準備は3770億ドル。Anthropicの資金源には、IPOで調達した810億ドルと、特定の投資家向け私募で得た260億ドルが含まれる。

records.excerpt: ビットコインがAnthropicやSpaceXの新規株式公開（IPO）を前に、過去と類似した急落パターンを見せている。Anthropicの公募・私募を合わせた調達規模は約1,195億ドルに達する中、市場では大型IPOへの資金移動後にビットコインやイーサリアムが底打ちするかどうかに注目が集まっている。 AnthropicやSpaceXのIPOを控えビットコインが急落、今回は反発なるか Jang Sun-hee 記者 입력 2026.11.21 13:35 ビットコインは、アントロピックとスペースXの新規株式公開（IPO）を控え、同様の急落パターンを見せた。アントロピックの公募と私募を合わせた調達額は約1,195億ドルに達しており、市場では大型IPOに資金が移動した後、ビットコインとイーサリアムが底を打つことができるかに注目が集まっている。 仮想通貨（写真：聯合ニュース） 2つの大型上場を控えて繰り返された下落 アントロピックは19日（現地時間）、ナスダック・グローバル・セレクト・マーケットで「ANT」という銘柄コードで取引を開始した。同社は20日に公募と同時私募のすべてを完了したと発表し、公募規模は1株あたり83ドルで11億2,700万株、公募総額は約935億ドルだった。私募を合わせた全体の調達規模は約1,195億ドルである。CNBCによると、ビットコイン価格はアントロピック上場前の30日間で22.7%下落し、スペースXが6月12日に上場する前の一ヶ月間も22.3%下落した。イーサリアムも同期間にそれぞれ25.3%と28%下落しており、2つの大型IPOを控えた暗号資産市場で同様の売りの流れが見られた。 IPOへ移動した流動性 大型IPOが実施されると、投資家が既存の資産を売却して新たに上場した株式を購入するため、資産市場全体の相関関係が急激に高まる可能性があるという分析が出ている。シャープリンクの最高投資責任者（CIO）マシュー・シェフィールド氏は、アントロピック上場後の最初の15分間、ハイテク株やバリュー株、原油、金、暗号資産が一斉に売られた現象を、このような資金移動の事例として説明した。同氏は、長期的に価値の保存手段として機能する資産も、短期的には現金流動性の影響を受けると述べた。最近の暗号資産の弱気相場には、上場投資信託（ETF）からの資金流出やレバレッジ取引の清算、マクロ経済の不確実性、リスク回避の心理も影響を与えた要因として挙げられる。 上場後の反発には時間がかかる可能性も アントロピックの上場が終了した後、市場の関心はビットコインが現在の価格帯で支持線を構築できるかに移っている。ストライブ・アセット・マネジメントのマット・コール最高経営責任者（CEO）は、スペースX上場当時、ビットコインは上場完了後も最終的な底をすぐには見つけられず、下落トレンドを転換するのに70日かかったと語った。同氏は現在、ビットコインが底を形成する初期段階にあり、市場が当分の間、騰落を繰り返す可能性が高いと見ている。IPOで割り当てられた株式のロックアップ（売却制限）が解除されるタイミングも、資金の流れに影響を与える可能性がある。スペースXのIPO資料には、既存株主ごとに異なる売却制限が適用され、一部の数量は今後の決算発表後に段階的に取引が可能になる構造が盛り込まれていた。 6万〜6万2千ドル区間が試金石 ビットコインは11月に入り、ドル高や機関投資家の売り、レバレッジポジションの清算の影響を受け、弱気相場が続いた。人工知能（AI）関連企業の高い評価や投資支出をめぐる懸念がハイテク株の売りにつながり、暗号資産市場にも重荷が続いた。ナンセンの調査アナリスト、ニコライ・ショーネガード氏は、ビットコインの次の重要な試金石となる区間として6万〜6万2千ドルを提示した。21日、ビットコインはこの区間の上限付近である約6万2千ドルで推移した。この支持線が維持されれば安定化を確認できるが、売りが続けば7月の安値である5万7,737.35ドルを再び試す可能性があるとの分析だ。コールCEOは、最近の市場を金融危機の始まりというよりは、変動性の高いリスク資産の買い場と評価した。ただし、同氏はビットコインの回復局面を真冬が終わった直後の「早春」に例え、反発の過程でも急激な寒波や雨が続く可能性があると説明した。 著作権者 © 財経日報 無断転載および再配布禁止 前の記事 Zscalerの株価が18%急騰…CrowdStrikeは8%下落 次の記事 小井里駅で貨物列車が脱線、光州・龍山行き列車に影響

3/Y](https://touchlab.jp/category/ev/model3_modely/) # 【衛星通信】テスラ、Model 3/YにStarlinkを搭載へ〜2027年末を目標 2026/11/23 イーロン・マスクが、Cybercab以外のテスラ車でもStarlinkを使えるようになる時期について、「来年の終わりごろ」との見通しをXに投稿しました。 > Hopefully available towards the end of next year. > > This will be important for unsupervised FSD, so passengers have high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment. > > — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) [November 23, 2026](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2124673053246312848?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) 用途は「監視なしのFSD」の車内。場所を問わず、乗員が仕事や娯楽に高速回線を使えるようにするためとしています。 現在でもテスラの車両にモバイル通信モジュールが搭載されていますが、SpaceXが携帯キャリヤ事業に乗り出すことを表明しており、ごく自然な流れといえるかもしれません。 [![Image 7](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=touchlab.jp) Touch Lab - タッチ ラボ ![Image 8](https://touchlab.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/starlink_mobile_career_0-150x100.jpg) [News](https://touchlab.jp/category/news/) 【ニュース】SpaceX、携帯キャリア事業進出へ〜米国で800MHz帯を取得 📅️2026-10-09 SpaceXが、米国全土で使える「800MHz帯」の周波数免許を取得することで合意し、Starlinkを米国の主要な携帯キャリアにする計画を発表しました。壁を通る800MHz帯800MHz帯は、日本でいうプラチナバンドにあたる帯域です。携帯電話の初期から使われてきた周波数で、遠くまで届き、建物の中にも電波が入りやすい性質があります。売り手は投資会社のGrain Managementで、同社が全米で持つ800MHz帯の免許をすべてSpaceXに譲ります。規模は最大14MHz幅、価格は非公表。取引の成立にはFCC(米連邦通信委員会)の承認が必要です。衛星からスマー...](https://touchlab.jp/2026/10/spacex_mobile_career) ## **Cybercabに搭載開始** ![Image 9](https://touchlab.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/cybercab_starlink_1-jpg.webp) Image:@JoeTegtmeyer 「**Cybercab**」へのStarlink搭載は、2026年7月にテスラが[予告](https://touchlab.jp/2026/07/cybercab_starlink_v5/)していたもので、アンテナはSpaceXの家庭用新型「**Starlink V5**」で、下りは最大375Mbps以上とされます。 続く8月には、車体後部のリアゲートにアンテナを収めた実車が公開され、9月には生産ラインの車両にも搭載が始まったと伝えられています。なお、自動運転の判断は車載コンピューターで完結するため、走行に回線は不要とテスラは説明しています。 ## **ガラスルーフという壁** ![Image 10](https://touchlab.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/model3_106-1024x576-jpg.webp) 「**Model 3**」「**Model Y**」で悩ましいのが、アンテナの置き場所。どちらも屋根の大部分をガラスが占めています。 ただ、ガラス越しなら車内に置けるかというと、そうとも限りません。Cybertruckの開発を率いるWes Morrill(ウェス・モリル)は3月、屋根のガラスにある遮熱用の金属層がStarlinkの接続を妨げると説明。さらに8月には、「**Model Y L**」の後部ガラスでも衛星の電波が通らないという報告がオーナーから出ています。技術的には可能だと思いますが。 また、日本では走行中の車でStarlinkを使えない点も、ひとつのハードルになりそうです。 records.excerpt: Mesa Council debates Falcon Field contract before OK | News | themesatribune.com Skip to main content You have permission to edit this article. Edit About | Contact | Employment | Pick Up A Copy |Advertise | Digital Editions Special_sections Legals Facebook Twitter Instagram Vimeo Councilwoman Dorean Taylor raised concerns at the Nov. 12 study session with Granite Construction, which was awarded a contract last week to do work at Falcon Field Airport. (YouTube) Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Save Top Story Mesa Council debates Falcon Field contract before OK By CECILIA CHAN, Tribune Managing Editor Nov 23, 2026 2 hrs ago Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Save Council last week awarded a $792,000 contract to a construction company to rehab a vehicle service road at Falcon Field Airport despite one councilwoman’s strong reservations. Councilwoman Dorean Taylor at the Nov. 12 study session asked if the city could delay the project and find another company because she wasn’t happy with Granite Construction’s job performance. “I’m very familiar with Granite,” Taylor said. “They’re doing Southern and Val Vista and it’s been atrocious. It’s probably been one of the worst managed projects I’ve ever seen. They’re gone. They leave the project, they come back, they sub out, they’re very slow. Councilwoman Dorean Taylor raised concerns at the Nov. 12 study session with Granite Construction, which was awarded a contract last week to do work at Falcon Field Airport. (YouTube) “My residents and I both notice there’s barely anybody there. They’ve pushed the project out two months now. “In my opinion completely untrustworthy and I would hate to see us give them essentially an award for a bid. If we can avoid that, that would be fantastic.” Handing the job to Granite Construction, the sole bidder for the project, highlighted the state of the industry. Arizona's construction industry needs 40,000-plus more workers, according to the Arizona Chapter of the Associated General Contractors of America. The skilled labor shortage in the state’s construction industry is driving up project costs, extending timelines and creating severe staffing challenges, the trade association said. Marc Ahlstrom, assistant city engineer, said delaying the project was difficult as federal funding was attached to the project. The project is funded largely by grants from the federal Aviation Administration and the Arizona Department of Transportation. “A delay or a rebid would potentially jeopardize the funding,” Ahlstrom said. Taylor pressed the issue, asking if the city still had time to see if anyone else would be willing to bid on it. Airport Projects and Operations Manager Mark Gibbs detailed the challenge in rebidding the project. “We would have to coordinate with those two granting agencies for permission,” Gibbs said. “They may find some exception if we can’t find a valid reason why Granite Construction is non-performing in terms of its bid on this specific project. I don’t know if other projects that the city has may be a reason for them not to award this particular bidder.” City Manager Scot Butler said the market for contractors was “very competitive.” “This is a challenge not just in Mesa but throughout the region,” he said. “There’s a lot of construction activity going on as you’re all aware around semiconductor infrastructure and other things. “I’ve heard this from other cities as well that it’s a very tough market right now on getting a lot of competitive bids for some of these projects.” Ahlstrom said that especially with projects where the limit is $4 million – the average job order contract across the Valley – there are generally fewer bids. “That’s been the case for the last six or seven years,” Ahlstrom said. “In fact, we’ve had cases where we’ve had no bids on a couple of them.” Taylor said, “I’ve experienced how bad the project has run in my district. “I want it to be very publicly, vocally known that they are causing a lot of strain on the city’s resources, on the district’s residents, and I would hate to see that happen at Falcon Field as well.” Councilwoman Alicia Goforth, whose northeast district encompasses Falcon Field, asked if the city engineer agreed with Taylor’s assessment. “We’re well aware of the issues that Granite has had on the Val Vista Southern project,” Ahlstrom said. “And we are going to have discussions with our legal staff and internally and look at best practices and see if there’s ways to qualify contractors. “But in the past as we’ve looked at that it’s very hard to do with the rules that we are governed by.” He said that Granite has not done any other work at Falcon. The firm also bid to build a new taxiway at Falcon but lost out Nov. 16 to low bidder Sunland Asphalt Construction Co. Butler said if Granite rebid and was the lowest bidder, the city would still need to award it the contract as federal funds are involved. Falcon Field Airport Director Corinne Nystrom pointed out that if the city rebid the project and the bids come in higher, “the FAA and the state will not pay any more than what they’ve already agreed to pay.” Ahlstrom said staff recommended the city proceed with the contract. “My recollection is they have done airport work in other jurisdictions and that they could perform this work,” she said. Mayor Mark Freeman said he also supported moving forward because “if we rebid it and it’s higher then we have to pay the difference. We don’t know what that difference might be but it could be hundreds of thousands of dollars.” The city anticipates the project to take no more than three months to complete. “What does that look like if we have the same experience there as we’re having at Val Vista and Southern?” Taylor asked. Nystrom said it might be a bit of an inconvenience but that another access road could be used. Butler noted that the quality of contractors used for city projects is part of an ongoing dialog. “When we are able to use other construction methods, it gives us more flexibility to partner with firms that have a track record of being able to deliver on time and on budget projects for the city,” Butler said. “Unfortunately, there will be instances where the low bid is mandated by state law or federal law in this case. And so our hands are somewhat tied on this one.” Freeman asked if a contractor doesn’t perform well on a city contract and then bids on another, can Mesa say, “Maybe you’re not the best contractor for future projects?” “Can that be put on our books?” he asked. Ahlstrom said that debarring someone from bidding is hard to do. “In my time at the city, we’ve never debarred anybody from bidding,” Ahlstrom said. “And so we would be working with our city attorney and his staff to see what our options are there.” Butler noted hurdles in that process. “One of the challenges is there is a very high bar in state law and state statute for a contractor to rise to that level that we would be allowed to do that,” Butler said. “The industry has worked very well to delineate a very high standard within state statute that prohibits us from a lot of the flexibility that we’d like to have on projects like this.” Vice Mayor Scott Somers said, “If we debar somebody who’s the only one bidder on certain projects, now we have nobody bidding on projects. “But it does raise the issue, did everybody know that this project was available to be bid on? And so I think what we ought to be looking at is pushing these projects out better.” He said that the city instead should “incentivize better performance.” Butler said he was in total agreement. “Finding ways to incentivize work to be done quicker ahead of schedule, those are all things that we’re looking into,” Butler said. records.excerpt: Harvey Jones decided to shun the rollercoaster ride that is big tech and focus on a stunning FTSE 100 income stock with a super-sized yield. The post Forget... Forget Anthropic and SpaceX shares! I’d rather buy this boring UK income stock for its stunning 6.7% yield Image source: Getty Images Harvey Jones Mon, 23 November 2026 at 12:37 am GMT-7 3 min read ANT SPCX MNG.L As investors fixate on the Anthropic IPO, why am I banging on about the delights of this old-school FTSE 100 income stock? I decided to sit out the Anthropic excitement, and I'm glad I did. Its shares behaved much as SpaceX did, soaring on the initial hype before becoming volatile as underlying worries about AI swept back with a vengeance. By contrast to Anthropic and SpaceX, this UK blue-chip hasn't flown to the stars and back and that's a key reason why I like it. Another's that it's been giving me a fantastic rate of income, with share price growth on top. I love my M&G shares I had high hopes when I added wealth manager M&G ( LSE: MNG ) to my Self-Invested Personal Pension (SIPP) in spring 2023, and it's exceeded all of them. The stock was actually yielding 10%. A sky-high yield like that can be a warning sign, but I felt the shares had been overlooked and the company was good for its dividends. Somebody who invested £10,000 lump into this stock five years ago would now have £20,992. The shares grew 63% but reinvested dividends lifted the total return to 110%. M&G had its own IPO in October 2019, when it was spun off from FTSE 100 insurer Prudential . Its early years were also bumpy, as investor uncertainty and concerns about its prospects hit the share price and drove up that yield. Lately, it's had a much better run, albeit with volatility along the way. Buying opportunity? The shares have dipped 12% in the last three months, but are still up 17% over one year. I think this may be creating a buying opportunity. Sadly, the dividend isn't in double digits any more, but it's still 6.7%, one of the highest on the FTSE 100. The board's targeting annual dividend growth of 2%. Unfortunately, that's now below inflation, currently 3.6% and expected to rise further. That's a blow, as it means the dividend will shrink slightly in real terms. But given its high starting point, that's not the end of the world. And with luck, inflation will fall at some point. We'll see. The shares have also become more expensive after their strong run, but the forward price-to-earnings ratio's a modest 10.4. A dividend machine There are risks to every stock, including this one. If we get a wider AI or stock market crash , that could hit the value of assets under management, reduce customer inflows, increase outflows and cut commission-based fee income. M&G also operates in a fiercely competitive market, facing pressure from cheaper passive investment providers and rivals chasing the same institutional and private-market clients. Yet with that valuation and high yield, I think it's worth considering for the long term. It's the type of stock to buy and hold for years, hoping its dividends compound steadily and the shares enjoy the odd growth spurt. The income should come in handy in retirement. I'll be looking to take advantage if the shares dip further, locking in an even higher yield. records.title: Tesla Starlink Beyond Cybercab: 1 Model, 0 Prices
records.excerpt: Musk says built-in Starlink could reach more Teslas toward the end of next year for unsupervised FSD. Only Cybercab has it today, and no price is set. Tesla Starlink Beyond Cybercab: 1 Model, 0 Prices Dr. Heinrich Vogel Updated Nov 23, 2026 · 15 min read Courtesy of Tesla, Inc. Elon Musk says built-in Starlink could reach more Tesla vehicles toward the end of next year , and he tied the plan directly to unsupervised Full Self-Driving. Today, only the Cybercab is reported to carry the hardware. Tesla has not published a price, a model list, or a firm launch date for anything else. That gap between a bold claim and a thin spec sheet defines this story. Musk gave the plan a purpose (high bandwidth for passengers who no longer drive) and a rough window, but the details owners care about remain blank. This analysis separates what the reports confirm from what the headlines imply, and it looks at what the move means for Tesla hardware, for SpaceX, and for rivals running driverless fleets. For background on the only car that already has the dish, see our earlier look at Cybercab V1.5 in Dallas and its Starlink roof hardware . The story ran across several outlets over the weekend, including Teslarati, Yahoo Autos, Automotive News, Yahoo Finance, EV Central and Driving. Their reports agree on the core quote and on the Cybercab detail. They do not agree on how far the rollout will go, which is why this piece treats “every model” as an open question rather than a settled fact. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Add now What Musk Actually Said About Built-In Starlink The facts fit in a few lines. Musk said built-in Starlink could become available in Tesla vehicles “towards the end of next year.” Because today is November 23, 2026, that points to late 2027, and Tesla North used that framing in its headline. Musk framed the purpose in one sentence: “This will be important for unsupervised FSD, so passengers have high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment.” He added a caveat about geography. Musk said the plan applies “Except in China, as Starlink is illegal there.” Reports also say the Cybercab is the only Tesla vehicle currently equipped with Starlink. Nothing in the reports states a confirmed price for adding Starlink to any other Tesla. Note the word “hopefully” in the full reply, which appears in the exchange cited later in this article. Musk offered a target, not a commitment. Tesla has a long record of target dates that slid, so readers should treat “end of next year” as an aspiration until Tesla publishes a delivery schedule. Why Unsupervised FSD Needs a Better Connection The logic behind the announcement is easy to follow. In a supervised Tesla, the driver stays responsible and the cabin is a place where one person watches the road. In an unsupervised car, nobody watches the road, so passengers sit in the cabin with nothing to do but work, stream, or play. Their demand for bandwidth rises sharply, and a phone tether or a single cellular modem may not satisfy several people at once. Musk made that exact point when he said the feature matters for passengers who want bandwidth “everywhere” for work and entertainment. The word “everywhere” carries weight here. A satellite link does not depend on tower coverage, so it can keep a rear-seat video call alive on a rural highway where cellular signal drops. Whether Starlink in a moving car delivers that experience in practice is a separate question that Tesla has not answered with data. There is also a fleet angle. A driverless car that loses connectivity may need help from a remote operator, may need to download a map update, or may need to report a problem. Reports on the Starlink plan focus on passenger bandwidth and do not claim Starlink is required for vehicle safety. That distinction matters, and readers should not blur it. Our coverage of Cybercab ownership terms shows how much of the robotaxi pitch rests on passengers, not drivers. Confirmed vs Unconfirmed: The Fact Check Several outlets amplified the story, and the headlines ran ahead of the text. The table below sorts each claim by what the reports actually support. Claim Status What the reports say Musk said built-in Starlink could arrive toward the end of next year Confirmed as a statement Reported by Tesla North and other outlets Musk tied it to unsupervised FSD and passenger bandwidth Confirmed as a statement Same quote across multiple outlets Plan excludes China Confirmed as a statement Musk said Starlink is illegal there Cybercab is the only Tesla with Starlink today Reported Reports name the Cybercab as the sole equipped vehicle Price for non-Cybercab models Not stated Sources give no confirmed price Starlink in every Tesla model Unconfirmed No model list published Starlink as standard equipment rather than optional or subscription Unconfirmed No pricing structure published Rollout markets, hardware specs, bandwidth figures, firm date Unconfirmed Not given in any report Unsupervised FSD generally available by the Starlink rollout Unconfirmed No Tesla commitment found The pattern is clear. Musk’s words are solid, and every derived claim about scope, price or timing is not. When a headline says Starlink is “coming to every Tesla,” it stretches Musk’s statement past what he said. The Cybercab Is the Starting Point The Cybercab already carries Starlink, and that detail shapes everything else. Tesla built the two-seat robotaxi without a steering wheel or pedals, so passengers are the only occupants, and a satellite link fits that design from the start. Reports describe it as the only Tesla vehicle with the hardware today. Earlier on this site we tracked the Cybercab preview figures , including a reported $29,990 price and a $299 monthly fee mentioned in our five-year cost breakdown . Those numbers cover the Cybercab only. Nothing in the Starlink reports says whether the satellite hardware is included in the Cybercab price, and nothing says what it would cost to add the same hardware to a Model 3 or Model Y. Extending Starlink from a purpose-built robotaxi to cars designed years earlier is a bigger engineering step than the announcement suggests. The Cybercab was drawn around its roof and antenna. A Model Y was not. That explains why Musk used the careful word “hopefully.” Hardware Questions Tesla Has Not Answered Tesla has not released specifications for any non-Cybercab Starlink hardware. The reports contain no antenna size, no bandwidth figure, and no power draw. What follows is analysis of the engineering issues, not confirmed detail. Antenna placement and roof design A satellite terminal needs a clear view of the sky. Many Teslas have a large glass roof, which can pass some signals and block others, and the sheet metal around any antenna matters too. If Tesla wants Starlink in an existing model, engineers must either mount a terminal on the roof or redesign the roof assembly at the factory. The first path adds visible hardware. The second path ties the feature to new production, which fits Musk’s phrase about availability “in Tesla vehicles” without promising retrofits. Power, heat and cost A phased-array terminal draws power and sheds heat. In a car that sits in a Texas summer or an Alaskan winter, those loads have to stay manageable. Tesla has not said how much energy the system would use. Cost is also unknown. Because the reports give no price, any figure circulating online counts as speculation. Factory fit versus aftermarket The reports describe a factory-integrated feature, not a bolt-on accessory. That is a design choice with consequences. Factory integration gives Tesla control of quality and warranty, but it limits the benefit to cars built after the change. Owners of existing vehicles should not assume an upgrade path exists. records.title: Colombia Investigates Starlink and Telecommunications Operators Over Signal in Prisons
records.excerpt: Title: Colombia Investigates Starlink and Telecommunications Operators Over Signal in Prisons URL Source: http://colombiaone.com/2026/11/22/colombia-investigates-starlink-and-telecommunications-operators-over-signal-in-prisons/ Final URL: https://colombiaone.com/2026/11/22/colombia-investigates-starlink-and-telecommunications-operators-over-signal-in-prisons/ Published Time: 2026-11-22T17:32:06+00:00 Markdown Content: ![Image 1: Prisons](https://colombiaone.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Prisons-in-Colombia-Credit-X-@INPEC_Colombia-1024x683.jpg) During the operations carried out at La Picota, authorities found 582 cell phones, 3,754 SIM cards, six Starlink antennas, and 38 modems, among other electronic devices. Credit: X: [@INPEC_Colombia](https://x.com/INPEC_Colombia) The Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) has opened an administrative investigation and filed charges against [Starlink](https://colombiaone.com/?s=Starlink)[Colombia](https://colombiaone.com/colombia-news/ "Colombia news") S.A.S. for allegedly failing to comply with its legal obligation to attenuate telecommunications signals covering penitentiary and [prison](https://colombiaone.com/2026/09/29/first-mega-prison-set-to-be-completed-and-opened-by-abelardo-de-la-espriella-in-colombiafirst-mega-prison-set-to-open-under-abelardo-de-la-espriella/) facilities. The decision comes after six [Starlink antennas](https://colombiaone.com/2026/11/04/how-did-hundreds-of-phones-and-starlink-antennas-operate-inside-la-picota-without-being-detected/), along with hundreds of unauthorized communication devices, were found during an operation at La Picota prison in Bogota, the Office of the President of Colombia reported in a statement. Subsequently, technical inspections conducted by MinTIC’s Communications Services Monitoring and Inspection Center (CMIC) identified internet connections through WiFi networks provided by Starlink at four penitentiary facilities: [La Picota](https://colombiaone.com/?s=La+Picota), in Bogota; Bellavista, in Bello (Antioquia); Acacias, in Meta; and Las Heliconias, in Florencia (Caqueta). These findings prompted the opening of administrative proceedings to determine whether Starlink adopted the legally required measures to prevent its services from facilitating unauthorized communications from detention centers. ## Investigations against mobile operators Colombian law is clear: providers of telecommunications networks and services have a duty to attenuate signals covering penitentiary and prison facilities. This obligation is established in Article 16A of Law 65 of 1993, added by Law 1709 of 2014. MinTIC also opened administrative investigations and filed charges against Partners Telecom Colombia S.A.S., Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P., Comunicacion Celular S.A. (Comcel), and the Colombia Movil – Colombia Telecomunicaciones Joint Venture (Tigo), for allegedly failing to comply with their obligations to eliminate or restrict mobile signals at La Picota penitentiary facility. - Advertisement - The proceedings seek to establish whether these companies adopted the necessary measures to comply with the provisions requiring restrictions on the transmission, reception, and control signals of mobile telecommunications services within the facility. During the operations carried out at La Picota, authorities found 582 cell phones, 3,754 SIM cards, six Starlink antennas, and 38 modems, among other electronic devices, demonstrating the scale of the challenge facing the State in preventing unauthorized communications from prisons. ## Operators must answer for their legal obligations The National Government warned that penitentiary facilities can no longer continue to be used as communication centers to coordinate criminal activities, extortion, and other offenses. Telecommunications operators must comply with the obligations imposed on them by law and adopt the technical measures required of them to help control unauthorized communications in detention centers. If the violations are confirmed, the operators under investigation could face sanctioning proceedings that provide for fines of up to 15,000 current monthly legal minimum wages, in their applicable legal equivalent, temporary suspension of operations, and even cancellation of licenses, authorizations, or permits, as appropriate. The Office of the President stressed that the investigations will be conducted while guaranteeing due process and the right of defense of the companies involved. records.title: Anthropic, SpaceX Bar IPO Underwriters From Working With Rivals, Sparking Wall Street 'Bullying' Debate
records.excerpt: Anthropic, as it pursues an $81.3 billion IPO, required key personnel at its lead underwriters to sign agreements barring them from working on business involving rivals such as OpenAI for six months after listing. The company also capped deal staffing at four people per bank, demanded emergency document approvals at 2 a.m., and declined to pay greenshoe fees. SpaceX imposed similarly one-sided terms on its underwriters. Wall Street analysts say the power dynamic between mega-issuers and investment banks has shifted decisively in the issuers' favor. U.S. artificial intelligence company Anthropic has imposed unprecedented restrictions on its lead underwriters as it pursues the largest initial public offering on record, drawing pushback from across Wall Street. The conditions range from clauses barring work with competitors for a set period to caps on staffing and demands for emergency document approvals in the early morning hours. According to foreign media reports on the 22nd (local time), Anthropic required key personnel on the investment banking teams handling its IPO, ahead of its Nasdaq listing on the 19th, to sign legal documents pledging not to take on work related to competitors including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek and Hugging Face for six months after the listing. Some senior bank executives reportedly refused to sign. Financial firms typically maintain internal rules to protect client confidentiality and manage conflicts of interest, but requiring individual employees to swear off all work with specific competitors for six months is highly unusual. One investment banking source said that with a wave of large AI listings expected, it was not easy to find personnel willing to commit to staying away from competitors for six months. Staffing was also restricted. Anthropic told some of the 22 underwriting institutions to limit the number of people assigned to the deal to four or fewer, and required that they be senior staff. The move is seen as an effort to prevent leaks of company information, though some banks are said to have worked around the staffing caps during the process. Access to information was tightened as well. Instead of conventional PDF files, Anthropic shared information with most securities firms through the NetRoadshow platform, which logs all document-viewing history and blocks saving copies. Documents were watermarked with the individual names of the bankers handling them. A compressed timeline added to the confusion. Ahead of the start of sales activity on the 10th, securities firms were first sent documents containing an incorrect price range and share count, and the corrected S-1A filing did not arrive until around 2 a.m. New York time. Banks had only a few hours to complete their review and sign-off to meet the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing deadline. SpaceX, which completed its listing in June, is seen as having imposed even more one-sided terms. It had lead underwriters including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley sign contracts without even disclosing the size of their fees, and it specified and notified each bank of the types of investors and order volumes they were expected to secure. Both Anthropic and SpaceX reportedly decided not to pay any underwriting fees on additional shares sold through the over-allotment (greenshoe) option. Item Anthropic SpaceX Listing date November 19, 2026 June 2026 Amount raised $81.3 billion Before breaking the all-time record Number of lead underwriters 22 Multiple Underwriting fees About $550 million Not disclosed Competitor work restrictions 6 months, key personnel No separate restrictions identified Greenshoe fees Not paid Not paid Note: Amount raised and fees are for Anthropic. Anthropic's listing raised $81.3 billion, surpassing the record for the largest IPO set by SpaceX in June. The underwriting fees received by the 22 underwriting institutions total about $550 million. Despite the hefty fees, some bank officials say Anthropic exercised excessive control over the entire listing process. Market observers say the power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street has shifted. Jay Ritter, a professor emeritus at the University of Florida, said these companies have secured the negotiating leverage to demand terms from underwriting syndicates that differ from the norm, based on their market dominance. Still, share performance has been uneven. SpaceX hit a high of $201.80 on June 16 before falling below its $135 IPO price in mid-July, while Anthropic surged 17% on its first trading day but has since slid, closing down 8.5% recently amid a correction in AI-related stocks. The episode is expected to influence how lead underwriters are selected and how fees are negotiated in the coming rush of AI company listings. If large issuers repeatedly succeed in securing favorable terms, the profitability of underwriting syndicates and their staffing strategies will inevitably change, analysts say. Anthropic and its lead underwriters Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley did not respond to requests for comment, and SpaceX also did not reply.
