records.excerpt: Free Article Explore Premium Services The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Are Dangerously Close to Joining the Nasdaq in a Correction. Here’s the Level That Would Put the Nasdaq in a Bear Market, and What History Says Investors Should Do During a Stock Market Crash. Buying high-quality stocks and ETFs during periods of intense volatility can pay off for long-term investors. By Daniel Foelber – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:30PM EST Key Points The major indexes were hovering around all-time highs just a few weeks ago. If the sell-off worsens, it could be classified as a crash. The Nvidia sell-off is at least partly justified, as Jensen Huang is irreplaceable. 10 stocks we like better than NASDAQ Composite Index › The stock market sell-off has gone from bad to worse, with ripple effects extending to the major indexes. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC -5.28% ) is now firmly in a correction, which is a drop of at least 10% from this high. As of Nov. 19 market close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI -1.93% ) is down 9.7% from its high, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC -3.70% ) has proven more resilient but is still down 8.2% from its highs. It's worth mentioning that the Nasdaq and S&P 500 were both at all-time highs in early October -- showcasing the speed and severity of the sell-off. Here's the level that the Nasdaq would need to reach to be in bear market territory, the differences between a stock market crash and a bear market, and how to navigate further volatility. Image source: Getty Images. 22,178.20 in the Nasdaq Composite would mark a 20% decline The Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,879.20 on Nov. 19 -- putting it 13.5% off its all-time high. ^SPX data by YCharts If the Nasdaq fell to 22,178.20, that would put the index down 20% from its all-time high of 27,722.75, set on Oct. 6. A bear market is defined as a prolonged downturn of at least 20% from a high. So, for example, the rapid sell-off during the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020 and the tariff-induced sell-off in April 2025 both saw the Nasdaq down over 20% from its high, but those levels were very short-lived. In contrast, the broader sell-off in growth stocks during 2022, when the Nasdaq fell 33%, was a legitimate bear market. A stock market crash is typically defined as a sudden drop in a major index. Exact definitions vary based on speed and severity. For example, a 10% drop in a week can feel more crash-like than a 20% drop over six months, even if the 20% drop is more damaging to your portfolio. However, if the Nasdaq does fall to that 20% drawdown level over the next few weeks, I think it's fair to call it a crash, given that the all-time high occurred just six weeks ago. And the speed of the sell-off, especially over the last couple of weeks, has been rapid. Especially in certain sectors. ^IXIC & NVDA : Performance Comparison Key Financial Metrics ^IXIC – NASDAQ Composite Index 22,617.73 – 5.28 % ( - 1,261.47 ) NVDA – Nvidia $125.53 – 14.01 % ( - $20.45 ) 52wk Range 20,794.64 - 27,599.89 Dividend & Yield N/A Market Cap $3.0T 52wk Range $124.50 - $243.37 Gross Margin 74.93 % P/E Ratio 13.49 EPS (TTM) $9.31 Dividend & Yield $0.52 (0.41%) ^IXIC – NASDAQ Composite Index 22,617.73 – 5.28 % ( - 1,261.47 ) 52wk Range 20,794.64 - 27,599.89 Dividend & Yield N/A NVDA – Nvidia $125.53 – 14.01 % ( - $20.45 ) Market Cap $3.0T 52wk Range $124.50 - $243.37 Gross Margin 74.93 % P/E Ratio 13.49 EPS (TTM) $9.31 Dividend & Yield $0.52 (0.41%) Nvidia is down 32.3% in three weeks There are already pockets of the stock market that have undergone crash-like sell-offs. In just three weeks, the Nasdaq Composite is down 10.1%. Even gold and Bitcoin ( BTC +0.90% ) have undergone rapid declines. Nvidia ( NVDA -14.01% ) , which was the world's most valuable company for most of this year, has lost roughly a third of its value in three weeks -- accelerated by the sudden resignation of its founder and CEO of over 33 years, Jensen Huang. Gold Price in US Dollars data by YCharts For investors with outsize exposure to Nvidia and other artificial intelligence (AI) stocks , the sell-off feels like a crash -- even if the major indexes don't reflect as much damage. There are better stocks to buy on the dip than Nvidia History says that stock market sell-offs present excellent buying opportunities in hindsight. After all, the major indexes have still delivered excellent medium- and long-term returns, even when factoring in current drawdowns. But that doesn't mean investors should assume that every stock that is down is cheap just because the price is lower. I've been bullish on Nvidia for years. But even I think Jensen Huang's departure negatively impacts the long-term investment thesis on Nvidia. So much so that I shifted my stance from a buy to hold until we get more clarity on the extent of the national security risk, how Nvidia will be restructured without Huang, how the company will fare under new leadership, whether Nvidia can retain its top talent, if the fundamentals remain intact, and if Nvidia can continue operating with the financial muscle of a large company paired with the flexibility and innovation of a start-up. So while there's a fair argument that the Nvidia sell-off may have gone a bit too far, the business is definitely weaker without Huang, and earnings growth may slow under a more operations-oriented leader like Colette Kress . I think there are far more clear-cut buying opportunities in today's market than Nvidia. One example is ASML ( ASML -6.63% ) , which is a leader in the semiconductor equipment industry. Its machines are used by top chip fabs like those operated by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM -9.48% ) , Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF +0.00% ) , and Intel ( INTC -7.97% ) . These machines are needed to manufacture next-generation AI chips at commercial scale, making ASML an excellent long-term buy for investors who believe that AI sophistication and use cases will continue to evolve. Another approach is to buy a beaten-down growth stock exchange-traded fund (ETF) for a basket of top companies. For example, the Vanguard Growth ETF ( VUG -5.32% ) and Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF ( MGK -5.58% ) both have ultra-low fees and provide exposure to many top companies. Go with your highest-conviction ideas Stock market sell-offs are excellent times to update your watch list with new opportunities and buy stocks whose values have become more reasonable. However, investors should expect volatility to be swifter and more severe due to widespread access to information, the ability to act on it easily through high-frequency trading, and, at the retail level, mobile trading and zero-fee brokerage services . Index concentration is another factor driving volatility. At its peak, Nvidia alone made up around 8% of the S&P 500 (still 5.4%). But as the current sell-off proves, the impact of Nvidia on the broader market extends far beyond its own weighting, through the companies that directly or indirectly depend on, compete with, or transact with Nvidia. Therefore, it's best to only buy stocks you are OK with holding even if volatility continues to intensify. Technology stocks face pressure as AI valuations come under scrutiny S&P 500 historical returns favor long-term investment periods Nasdaq Composite outlook: earnings growth and valuations remain central The Nasdaq Composite reached multiple record highs in 2026 as artificial intelligence investment, corporate earnings and enthusiasm surrounding technology companies supported US equity markets. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 also established new peaks, extending a multiyear rally that has increasingly depended on expectations of AI-driven economic growth. The gains have been supported by expanding AI infrastructure spending, stronger-than-expected financial results, record S&P 500 share repurchases, major initial public offerings and investor interest in stock splits among established companies. Yet the valuations accompanying the rally have become a growing concern. By November, several historical measures of market risk had reached levels previously associated with major corrections, including the S&P 500’s cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio and record borrowing against investment portfolios. The Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average reached multiple record highs in 2026, supported by AI infrastructure investment, stronger corporate earnings and investor interest in major IPOs. The S&P 500 Shiller P/E ratio stood at 38.76 on November 17, 122% above its historical average, after reaching 42.84 in June. Previous periods of similarly elevated valuations preceded significant market declines. US margin debt reached a record $1.5 tn, increasing concerns about speculative exposure. Historical market data nevertheless show that bull markets have lasted substantially longer than bear markets. The central question for investors is whether corporate earnings can grow sufficiently to justify current stock prices, particularly among technology companies benefiting from expectations of substantial future AI revenue. Nasdaq Composite record highs in 2026 and the AI investment boom Artificial intelligence has been a major driver of the US equity rally, particularly for technology companies supplying computing infrastructure, semiconductor components and related services. Investment by hyperscale cloud providers and specialized cloud infrastructure companies has demonstrated substantial demand for AI computing capacity. Expectations that this spending will translate into higher corporate revenue and profitability have helped support technology valuations. According to IDC estimates cited in the source material, AI represents a potential $22.5 tn addressable market through 2031. Such projections have contributed to investor expectations for companies developing and supplying AI technology. The broader market has benefited from additional sources of support, including corporate earnings that exceeded expectations, substantial share buybacks and investor demand for high-profile public offerings. Under President Donald Trump, equity markets have also benefited from expectations surrounding corporate tax policy. During his first presidential term, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 57%, the S&P 500 advanced 70% and the Nasdaq Composite rose 142%. The current rally has nevertheless displayed considerable volatility. Technology shares remain particularly sensitive to changes in expected AI spending, earnings growth and valuation assumptions. S&P 500 Shiller P/E ratio reaches historically elevated levels One of the principal concerns surrounding US stocks is the level of equity valuations relative to historical earnings. The conventional price-to-earnings ratio compares a company’s share price with its earnings per share over the preceding 12 months. It provides a relatively straightforward valuation measure, but its usefulness can diminish during recessions when corporate earnings fall sharply or turn negative. The Shiller P/E ratio, also called the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio (CAPE), addresses this limitation by comparing stock prices with average inflation-adjusted earnings over the previous 10 years. Using a decade of earnings reduces the impact of short-term fluctuations in profitability and allows investors to assess valuations across different economic cycles. Although the measure was developed less than four decades ago, historical calculations extend to January 1871. Over that period, the S&P 500’s average Shiller P/E ratio has been approximately 17.45. As of November 17, 2026, the ratio stood at 38.76, approximately 122% above its long-term average. The measure had previously reached 42.84 in early June 2026, its second-highest recorded level, amid strong investor demand for AI-related equities. Only during the late-1990s technology boom did the ratio reach a substantially higher peak. In December 1999, it climbed to 44.19 before the dot-com bubble collapsed. The elevated reading does not establish that US stocks are about to decline. Valuations can remain historically expensive for extended periods, particularly when earnings growth and investor expectations continue supporting prices. It does, however, indicate that investors are paying considerably more for inflation-adjusted corporate earnings than the historical average. What previous market bubbles reveal about elevated valuations Since January 1871, the Shiller P/E ratio has exceeded 30 during six distinct periods, including five since the beginning of the 21st century. Each completed episode was followed by a substantial decline in at least one major US equity index, although the timing and causes differed. The first major period extended from June 1997 through August 2001, during the technology-driven expansion associated with widespread internet adoption. The Shiller P/E ratio peaked at 44.19 in December 1999. After the dot-com bubble burst, the S&P 500 eventually declined 49%, while the Nasdaq Composite lost approximately 78% of its value. Valuations remained elevated long enough that the Shiller P/E did not fall below 30 until the second half of 2001. The Nasdaq Composite plunged approximately 10%, marking its worst week since the March 20… Stock Market Crash: Nasdaq, S&P 500 Suffer Worst Weekly Losses in Years 2 min read IXIC SPX DJI The US stock market crash intensified this week as investors aggressively dumped technology and artificial intelligence stocks, pushing major Wall Street indexes toward their steepest weekly declines in years. The Nasdaq Composite plunged approximately 10%, marking its worst week since the March 2020 pandemic crash, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6%. Both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones entered correction territory, raising concerns that the AI-driven market rally may be facing a deeper repricing. By Alistair Sterling November 23, 2026 WIB · 2 min read Nasdaq Falls 13.5% From Peak as S&P 500 and Dow Near Correction The Nasdaq Composite is in a correction, and the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average are close behind. As of the November 19 close, the Dow was down 9.7% from its high and the S&P 500 was down 8.2%. A correction is a drop of at least 10% from a peak. The Nasdaq closed at 23,879.20 that day, 13.5% below its all-time high of 27,722.75, set on October 6. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 both hit records in early October. The Nasdaq has fallen 10.1% in just three weeks. The level that means a bear market A bear market is a prolonged decline of at least 20% from a high. For the Nasdaq, that line sits at 22,178.20. Advertisement Short, sharp drops do not always qualify. The Nasdaq fell more than 20% during the March 2020 COVID-19 sell-off and the April 2025 tariff-driven sell-off, but both were brief. The 2022 slide in growth stocks, when the Nasdaq dropped 33%, was a true bear market. A crash has no fixed definition. It usually means a sudden fall in a major index. Daniel Foelber, a Motley Fool analyst, wrote that a drop to the 20% level over the next few weeks would be fair to call a crash, given the peak came only six weeks earlier. Nvidia drags on the market Nvidia, the world's most valuable company for most of this year, has lost roughly a third of its value in three weeks. The fall accelerated after founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who led the company for more than 33 years, suddenly resigned. Advertisement At its peak, Nvidia made up around 8% of the S&P 500. It is now 5.4%. Foelber noted that its influence reaches further, through companies that supply, compete with or do business with it. Gold and Bitcoin have also fallen quickly, according to Foelber. What one analyst suggests Foelber, who holds Nvidia and ASML shares, moved his view on Nvidia from buy to hold. He cited open questions about a national security risk, how the company will be restructured and whether it can keep top talent. He said earnings growth may slow under a more operations-focused leader such as Colette Kress. He pointed instead to ASML, which makes chip-manufacturing equipment, and to two low-fee funds: the Vanguard Growth ETF and Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF. He also said investors should expect faster, more severe swings, and should only buy stocks they are comfortable holding if volatility worsens. records.excerpt: Wall Street is aiming for a rebound after the Dow Jones and the Nasdaq reported their worst weekly performance since March 2020, which was the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic. The Dow fell 8% last week, while the Nasdaq corrected 10%. Futures on Wall Street are looking to stage a rebound as trading resumed on Sunday evening US time following their worst week in years. This week happens to be a truncated one for the US markets as well.Futures on the Dow Jones are trading with gains between 650-700 points. The S&P 500 futures are up over 140 points, while the Nasdaq futures are up over 750 points at the start of trading in the futures market.Wall Street is aiming for a rebound after the Dow Jones and the Nasdaq reported their worst weekly performance since March 2020, which was the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic. The Dow fell 8% last week, while the Nasdaq corrected 10%. At its intraday low on Friday, the Nasdaq 100 index has slipped into "bear market territory", meaning a fall of 20% or more from the peak.S&P 500's 3.5% fall last week was also its worst weekly performance since April 2025, which marked US President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariff announcements. The S&P 500 closed below its 200-Day Moving Average on Friday, and Edward Yardeni, of Yardeni Research, cut his target on the index to 7,500 for the year-end from 7,900 earlier. However, he still believes that the index will end 2027 between 8,500 - 9,000 levels.A combination of multiple factors, profit booking due to the mega Anthropic IPO, issues surrounding Nvidia, breaking of key technical levels, worries of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates aggressively, are all contributing to the sell-off in the US markets.The sell-off has resulted in investors flocking to haven assets, with the US 10-year bond yield slumping back to 4.95% from 5.12% on Thursday. The US Dollar index also traded near the mark of 104, sparking a broader sell-off in metals.The Biggest Trigger For Wall Street This WeekAs this is a truncated week, most of the macroeconomic data will be reported during the first three days of the week itself.Before the macro data is reported, two key hardware companies, Hewlett Packard Enterprises, and Dell, will be reporting their quarterly results after market closing hours on Monday and Tuesday respectively. HPE shares are down 25% this month so far, while Dell shares have slumped 34%.The biggest trigger for the week though, will be the Personal Consumption Expenditure inflation data, which will be reported on Wednesday. This is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge and will be the final inflation print before the Fed rate decision on December 9.As of today, the probability of the Fed raising rates by 25 basis points on December 9, still stands at 89%.Second estimates of the Q3 GDP data, consumer spending print, jobless claims, wholesale and retail inventories data will also be reported during the course of the week.

records.excerpt: Indian markets ended last week at nine-month highs, with the Nifty and Sensex rising for a fourth consecutive week as strong earnings and banking stocks supported gains. Global technology shares sold off sharply, while inflation, upcoming RBI policy and GDP data may keep domestic markets cautious. Stock market prediction for Monday, 23 November, 2026: The Indian stock market benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty 50, are expected to have a gap-up today amid mixed global cues.Asian equities came under renewed pressure on Monday, 23 November, following last week's sharp technology-led sell-off on Wall Street. Although US equity futures staged a modest recovery in early Asian trade, regional chipmakers and technology-heavy indices remained under pressure, prompting governments across the region to roll out measures to stabilise financial markets.Market regulators in China, Taiwan and South Korea are stepping up efforts to contain the fallout from Wall Street’s AI-led sell-off, which has pushed the Nasdaq 100 into bear-market territory and sent the Dow Jones and S&P 500 into technical corrections.Equity markets across all three countries have retreated sharply from the highs reached in the first half of the year as the AI trade unwinds and concerns mount over the financial health of several companies. Sensex, Nifty: What happened on Friday?Indian equities bucked a broader selloff across Asian markets on Friday, 20 November, extending their winning streak to four consecutive weeks as a global rout in AI-linked stocks prompted a record surge in foreign portfolio inflows into domestic shares.The gains mark a notable turnaround for Indian markets, which had lagged their emerging-market peers over the past two years amid limited exposure to the global artificial intelligence boom and persistently high crude oil prices.The Nifty 50 climbed 2.6% over the week, while the BSE Sensex advanced 2.9%, with both benchmarks settling at nine-month highs of 25,800.60 and 83,919.71, respectively. On Friday alone, the two indices gained 1.1% each.Dhruv Joglekar, Assistant Fund Manager at Monarch PMS, said that strong corporate earnings continue to support the Indian market. Nifty 50 companies reported a 27% year-on-year increase in profit after tax in Q2 FY27, marking the fastest growth in 17 quarters and surpassing most analyst expectations.However, rising inflation remains a key concern. Retail inflation climbed to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance limit, while wholesale inflation rose to 12.29%. With the RBI having already raised interest rates in October, Joglekar expects another 25-basis-point hike at its 4 December policy meeting.He noted that historical trends offer some reassurance, pointing out that the PSU Bank index gained more than 40% during the 2022–23 monetary tightening cycle. However, overseas developments warrant caution, particularly the US Federal Reserve's hawkish stance and the US 10-year Treasury yield trading above 5%.On the domestic market outlook, Joglekar said the Nifty has already reached the 25,500 target projected by analysts, with its 52-week high of 26,328 emerging as the next major hurdle, around 3% higher. However, with the RBI's policy decision approaching and Q2 GDP data due later in November, growth is estimated at around 7.3%; he expects the market to consolidate rather than stage a sharp breakout. He identified 25,000 as a crucial downside level to watch.For investors, Joglekar recommended staying invested in quality large-cap stocks, particularly banking stocks, while maintaining a selective approach towards mid- and small-cap shares. Sensex, Nifty prediction for today: Sensex, Nifty outlookGIFT Nifty todayThe Gift Nifty Live Chart shows a weak start for the Indian stock market today. At 6:35 AM, the Gift Nifty was trading around the 25,930 level, a premium of 155 points from the Nifty futures’ previous close.SensexSachin Gupta, VP – Technical Research at Choice Equity Broking Private Limited, said the Sensex displayed strong bullish momentum, closing at 83,919.71, up 897.96 points or 1.08%. The index opened with a gap-down at 82,558.25 and slipped to an intraday low of 82,403.27. However, buying interest emerged soon after the opening, pushing the benchmark to a high of 84,037.96, close to its session peak.He said the sharp recovery from early losses and the close well above the opening level indicate strong buying demand at lower levels. Gupta identified 83,000–83,500 as the immediate support zone, where dips are likely to attract fresh buying. On the upside, resistance is placed at 84,200–84,500.Overall, he expects the Sensex to trade within a broad range of 83,000–84,500, with the near-term technical bias remaining bullish.Nifty 50Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, said the Nifty 50 resumed its next leg of the uptrend after consolidating for seven to eight sessions. The benchmark index surged 286 points on Friday, extending its gains despite weakness across global markets.He noted that the Nifty 50 witnessed a decisive breakout above the crucial 25,500 resistance level and is now advancing towards its previous all-time highs. records.title: Canada joins NATO Innovation Fund with more than $100 million commitment
records.excerpt: Defence Minister David McGuinty announced Canada is the 25th ally and the first in North America to join the venture fund. The Business Development Bank of Canada will hold and manage the stake. Adobe Stock Canada has formally joined the NATO Innovation Fund (NIF), committing more than $100 million that will let the fund invest in Canadian startups and funds, National Defence said. Defence Minister David McGuinty announced the move Nov. 21 in Halifax. Canada is the 25th NATO ally in the fund and the first in North America. Why it matters: Canadian defence and dual-use companies gain a new source of venture capital and a link to investors across the alliance. National Defence said the NIF is the world's first multi-sovereign venture capital fund, and that Canadian innovators now have access to more than €1 billion in deployable capital. The commitment The NIF release puts Canada's contribution at €64.59 million, or about $100 million Cdn. The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) will hold and manage the investment. Total commitments to the fund now top €1.1 billion. The NIF said membership also gives Canadian innovators a large network of co-investors and lessons from its work across 24 participating nations. The fund The NIF launched in 2022. Its first sub-fund was formally established in 2023 by 23 NATO allies. It invests in AI, autonomous systems, quantum technologies, biotech, space, hypersonics, novel materials, manufacturing, energy and propulsion, and next-generation communications. The NIF says it has more than 30 portfolio companies. Canadian ties National Defence said NIF portfolio companies have expanded into Canada over the past year. The NIF named two: Isar Aerospace, which was selected to develop a launch pad and provide launch services for Canadian satellites, and airship company Kelluu, which recently entered the Canadian market. What they said: "By joining the NATO Innovation Fund, Canada will help Canadian companies find the capital, partners and markets they need to grow," McGuinty said. BDC president and CEO Isabelle Hudon said the bank's Defence Platform "brings together capital, financing, expertise, partnerships and market connections to help defence and dual-use companies move from innovation to commercialization and scale." She said Canada's participation "extends that reach across the Alliance." NIF board chair Fiona Murray called Canada's decision "a landmark moment" for the alliance's approach to innovation. What's next: NIF president Ari Jónsson said the next step is "accelerating their adoption," with contracts and commercial opportunities for Canadian startups. Neither release gave a timeline for the first Canadian investments.

records.title: Remarks by UNICEF Executive Director, Catherine Russell at the roundtable conversation at Nasdaq Headquarters on World Children’s Day: Child-lens investing in capital markets
records.excerpt: Title: Remarks by UNICEF Executive Director, Catherine Russell at the roundtable conversation at Nasdaq Headquarters on World Children’s Day: Child-lens investing in capital markets URL Source: http://www.unicef.org/press-releases/remarks-unicef-executive-director-catherine-russell-roundtable-conversation-nasdaq Final URL: https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/remarks-unicef-executive-director-catherine-russell-roundtable-conversation-nasdaq Published Time: 2026-11-20T18:35:35+0000 Markdown Content: **NEW YORK, 20 November 2026 –** “Good morning, everyone. Thank you to Nasdaq for hosting us, and to all of you for joining us on World Children's Day. “Every year on November 20th, we celebrate the anniversary of the adoption of the Convention on the Rights of the Child — a landmark agreement that recognizes children's fundamental rights to survive, thrive, and reach their full potential. “And what better place to mark this occasion than here, at the heart of one of the world's leading financial markets? “This year's celebration is especially meaningful as UNICEF prepares to mark its 80th anniversary in December — eight decades of working to protect children and build a better future for every child. “Today, Nasdaq joins more than 20 stock exchanges around the world in a first-of-its-kind global effort to Ring the Bell for Children. “It is a powerful symbol of what we can achieve when the financial community comes together around a shared purpose. And I hope it marks the beginning of a lasting tradition — one that puts children's rights and wellbeing firmly on the agenda of capital markets everywhere. “Because the decisions made in financial markets today will help shape the world children inherit tomorrow. Children represent nearly one-third of the world's population. They are not simply future workers, consumers, or leaders. They are people with rights, needs, and aspirations today. And their wellbeing is closely connected to the long-term health of our economies and societies. “When children grow up healthy, safe, educated, and equipped with the skills they need, they contribute to stronger communities, more resilient economies, and a more prosperous future for everyone. “Yet children's rights and wellbeing remain often overlooked in investment decisions and corporate sustainability practices. This is a missed opportunity. “Investors have tremendous influence — through the capital they allocate, the companies they support, and the expectations they set. They can help shape business practices that affect millions of children and families every day — from working conditions for parents, to responsible supply chains, to the products and services children use. “That is why UNICEF is championing Child-Lens Investing. This approach encourages investors to consider children's rights and wellbeing in their decisions, and to use their influence to support businesses and solutions that create better outcomes for children. “And stock exchanges have a particularly important role to play. They are where companies and investors come together. They help establish expectations for transparency and responsible business conduct. And they influence what companies measure, what investors value, and ultimately where capital flows. “Stock exchanges do not simply reflect markets. They help shape them. “Through our partnership with the United Nations Sustainable Stock Exchanges Initiative, we are working to help exchanges, listed companies, and investors better understand their impact on children — and integrate children's rights into their practices. “I want to thank the Government of Finland for its leadership and support in advancing Child-Lens Investing, through UNICEF's Innovative Finance Hub and UNICEF USA's Impact Fund for Children. And my thanks to the Sustainable Stock Exchanges Initiative, Nasdaq, and all our partners who are helping bring this vision to life. “I also want to offer a special welcome to Aditya, from UNICEF USA's National Youth Council. Aditya, thank you for being here. Your voice — and the voices of children and young people everywhere — must help shape the decisions that affect your lives and futures. Because we cannot truly put children first without listening to them. “So today, I have three simple asks of stock exchanges and the wider financial community. “First, make children visible. Consider how financial decisions and business practices affect children and their rights. Second, recognize and reward leadership. Encourage companies that take meaningful steps to protect children and support their wellbeing. And third, help direct capital toward solutions that improve children's lives. From education and healthcare to safe environments and opportunities for young people. “Every morning, the opening bell signals a new day of possibility for markets around the world. “Today, let it signal something more. A commitment to a future where financial success and children's wellbeing go hand in hand. Where markets recognize not only the value of today's investments, but their impact on tomorrow's generations. And where every child has the opportunity to grow, thrive, and shape their own future. “The markets of tomorrow depend on the children of today. Let us invest in both. Thank you, and happy World Children's Day!” #####

records.excerpt: U.S. stock futures staged a sharp rebound and turned green late Sunday as they look to recover from one of Wall Street’s toughest weeks, which saw a sharp selloff in technology and AI-related stocks.As of 9:32 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 1.54%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 1.96% and Nasdaq-10… Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Jump Nearly 2% After Brutal Tech Selloff Last Week: GME, JNJ, ALNY, GAP In Focus 6 min read IXIC DJI SPX Key points: The Nasdaq Composite fell 10% last week, while the S&P 500 and Dow fell more than 8% each. Some market participants believe that the AI selloff is overblown and that the current dip represents a buying opportunity. JPMorgan analysts said in a note over the weekend that the firm remains confident in the durability of the AI supercycle, supported by lower leverage and improved positioning. U.S. stock futures staged a sharp rebound and turned green late Sunday as they look to recover from one of Wall Street’s toughest weeks, which saw a sharp selloff in technology and AI-related stocks. As of 9:32 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 1.54%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 1.96% and Nasdaq-100 futures increased 2.33%. On Friday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed significantly lower amid rising concerns about the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite led the decline, shedding more than 1,200 points to close 5.28% lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 1.93% lower and the S&P 500 fell 3.70%. Index Move Close Dow Jones Industrial Average -1.93% 48,147.33 S&P 500 -3.70% 6,910.39 Nasdaq Composite -5.28% 22,617.73 Markets were a bloodbath last week amid the tech-led selloff. The Nasdaq Composite fell 10%, while the S&P 500 and Dow fell more than 8% each. U.S. President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he “predicted” that if the Democrats win the midterm elections, the stock markets would go down substantially. Tech Rout Weighs Heavily On Markets, But Some See Opportunity In The Dip Last week, technology and AI-related stocks saw a massive drawdown amid rising concerns over artificial intelligence’s sustainability. Recent upheaval in Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) leadership, rising inflation concerns and the potential of a rate hike in the Federal Reserve’s upcoming December policy meeting pressured markets. Trump blamed Democrats for the sharp decline in markets, saying in a Truth Social post, “The Market is down more than 6 Trillion Dollars since the Democrats’ rather strange ‘win’ on November 3rd. NASDAQ, by itself, is down 20%. This is 100% due to the fact that the Democrats are ‘BAD’ due to their Anti Growth, and Retribution Only, Policies, and worse. If they don't change, FAST, it will only get worse.” Meanwhile, some market participants believe that the AI selloff is overblown and that the current dip represents a buying opportunity. Fundstrat's Tom Lee said in a recent CNBC interview that the recent sell-off is a healthy reset rather than a sign that the AI boom is at its end. While acknowledging that the past few weeks have been "tumultuous" for tech stocks and the market, with investors grappling with doubts about AI spending, financing structures and the sustainability of lofty valuations, he said that he sees this to be a "pretty healthy correction in tech and it's along the narratives to reset." He drew comparisons with how Cisco fell nearly 50% over three months in 1997, only to rebound the following year. "I think that we are at that moment where it feels like max pain, but for the patient investor, this is going to have a big payoff," Lee said. "I don't think that this means it's the end of the AI trade," he said, adding that AI would remain "one of the biggest stories" next year. Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster also noted that the latest sell-off in the market is more a fear-based move than deteriorating fundamentals. In a note last week, Munster said that while investors may be getting caught up in worries about what could go wrong, they are missing the picture on what AI could ultimately deliver. He cautioned against drawing a conclusion that the AI market is in a bubble from the price action alone, noting that the Nasdaq's roughly 16% decline since the start of October was not unprecedented. He compared it with the approximately 24% sell-off during the early-2025 DeepSeek shock and tariff uncertainty. "At its core, this sell-off is not about fundamentals, it's about psychology," he said, adding that, "The unfortunate answer is that the sell-off will end when [we] have more buyers than sellers." Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives called the AI sell-off one of the most "disconnected" downturns that he has seen in his career, saying that stocks are pricing in the possibility that the AI revolution simply goes away. "I believe we are less than 15% through" the AI opportunity, he said, calling it "a generational opportunity to buy the winners." JPMorgan analysts said in a note over the weekend that it is reiterating its view that the recent pullback in risk assets is mostly an AI de-leveraging event amidst weak sentiment, coupled with a more hawkish Fed reaction function being priced in. “We keep the faith in the durability of the AI supercycle, supported by lower leverage and improved positioning,” it said, according to Bloomberg. Markets will be watching for developments in the AI trade in the holiday-shortened week with Thanksgiving on Friday. Iran Uncertainty Lingers Amid Rising Tensions In The Strait Of Hormuz Meanwhile, on the geopolitical front, the uncertainty around the conflict between the U.S. and Iran sent long-term Treasury yields higher and exerted added pressure on market sentiment. Trump said over the weekend in an interview with Fox News that he may be inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if an agreement does not come to fruition. He also dismissed the ongoing diplomatic talks with Tehran as meaningless, and accused negotiators of the country of stalling. The president also said that while he wants a "permanent" deal with Iran, he added that Iran doesn’t “want to make a deal that's acceptable to me.” Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said as per a Reuters report that the country wants a diplomatic resolution to the ongoing war and confirmed that talks with the U.S. were ongoing through mediators. Araghchi added that Iran was seeking an agreement with the U.S. that would ensure that there would be “no further war,” according to the report. "I believe a fair solution can be reached ​on the issue of ​nuclear material, one ⁠that is based on our national interests while also meeting the country’s needs," he reportedly said. Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors said in a post on X, “Wanting something, and actually being able to accomplish it are two very different things, and this is greatest problem for the United States against Iran. President Trump and his ‘advisors’ may desperately WANT to change the outcome of this war, but they very simply do not have a course of action to do so. Sometimes you just have to take the L whether you like it or not.” However, oil prices continue to cool amid a supply increase. The International Energy Agency has forecast a roughly 2 million-barrel-a-day surplus this quarter. Brent crude futures were trading at $92.23 a barrel, down 0.37% at the time of writing, while WTI crude futures traded 0.24% lower at $83.21 per barrel. Trump said in a post on Truth Social, “Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!” Gold, Silver Extend Selloff Meanwhile, the precious metals trade continued to plunge sharply, with gold spot prices steadily declining. Spot gold closed down 8.71% this week at $3,543.60, down about 37% since its record high of $5,589.38 on Jan. 28. Silver also dropped sharply and is now about 65% below its January high, according to TradingView data. Risi

records.title: Canada auto plant the 'front line' in Trump's trade war | Gulf Times
records.excerpt: Nearly two years into President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada, specific battlefields have emerged. One is an idle auto plan... Nearly two years into President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada, specific battlefields have emerged. One is an idle auto plant northwest of Toronto. The Brampton Assembly Plant produced Dodge models until 2023, when global auto giant Stellantis said the facility needed to be retooled for the electric vehicle future -- pausing work for nearly 3,000 employees with a pledge to resume production in 2025, making the Jeep Compass. Then Trump imposed tariffs to force companies to make vehicles exclusively in the United States. Stellantis said the Jeep Compass would instead be made in Illinois and, on November 9, announced it was selling the Brampton plant to Canadian defense company Roshel. On a cold, windy afternoon outside the nearly empty plant this week, furious Canadian autoworkers demanded action from Prime Minister Mark Carney. "We've given our lives to this company. There's nothing we haven't done," said Jason Watson, a skilled tradesman and union leader. "The federal government needs to step in and do everything they can to reverse this sale," he said, flanked by dozens of autoworkers who, he said, had passed up other opportunities because they believed the plant would re-open. The fight over the Stellantis plant has exposed trade war's intractable challenges. Carney has earned acclaim for standing firm against Trump, but experts say he has few options to defend an auto industry that developed in southern Ontario because of its proximity to the United States. If tariffs continue restricting Canada's access to the US market, more job losses could be coming. Carney says reliance on the United States has made Canada vulnerable and the country needs to diversify. A similar battle at a Hamilton, Ontario steel plant -- where the US-owner Cleveland Cliffs has threatened hundreds of job losses citing tariffs -- has further highlighted Canada's vulnerability. Carney is trying to expand overseas trade relations and supercharge domestic manufacturing, in part through a defense industrial strategy that envisions more than CAD$500bn ($350bn) in spending over the coming decade. Roshel makes armored vehicles and could profit from government contracts. But Ardis Snow, Unifor union chairperson at the plant, said Roshel cannot replace the jobs or wages provided by an auto giant, suggesting it would pay roughly half of Stellantis's CAD$45 per hour. "Mortgage companies aren't going to say, 'Hey, we know you just had your salary cut in half, so we're going to cut your mortgage in half,'" Snow told AFP. Snow, who began working at the plant nearly 40 years ago, said colleagues moved to cheaper parts of Canada during the retooling shutdown. They were preparing to return when Stellantis announced Jeep Compass production was moving to Illinois. "It felt like a gut punch," he told AFP. But Stellantis kept assuring the union it would assign a new model to Brampton. In August, it confirmed the sale talks with Roshel. "Not that you can always believe everything that a corporation ever says to you, but we didn't have reasons not to believe it," he said. "They were not honest." Ottawa's rhetoric towards Stellantis has been tough. Carney called the sale "a betrayal." Stellantis global CEO Antonio Filosa is expected in Canada on Friday for talks with government and the union. But the company is giving no indication the sale could be reversed, suggesting it's focused on severance packages for workers through "a fair, negotiated resolution that supports affected employees and recognizes their years of service." Rallying with workers this week, the head of Canada's left-wing New Democratic Party, Avi Lewis, argued Carney should "compel" Stellantis to keep making cars in Brampton. "Once we lose this industrial capacity, it is gone," he said. Trump's "tariff war is an attack on Canada," Lewis added. "This is the front line in this fight." But University of Toronto industrial and labour policy expert Rafael Gomez stressed Ottawa's limited options. Stellantis was already struggling in a competitive global auto market. The Brampton plant's EV retooling was itself an uncertain gamble, and then Trump's tariffs upended the cost structure of North America's auto sector. The situation is "untenable on so many levels," Gomez told AFP. records.title: 欧州「クラウド主権」拡散も域内シェア15%で停滞…米国3社が70%を掌握
records.excerpt: 欧州の公共機関や規制産業を中心に、米国技術への依存を減らそうとする「クラウド主権」の動きが広がっている。欧州委員会は1億8,000万ユーロ（約310億円）規模のソブリンクラウド事業を欧州連合企業連合やStackIT、Scalewayなどに発注したほか、オランダ政府やデンマーク国鉄、スイス連邦機関なども調達要件を強化した。T-SystemsとNextcloudは需要がそれぞれ4倍、5倍に増えたと明らかにした。しかしEU域内事業者のシェアは2017年の29%から2022年に15%へ低下した後、停滞している。AWS、Microsoft Azure、Google Cloudの米国3社が70%以上を掌握している。既存システムへのロックインと移行コストの負担が足かせとなり、実際の大規模移行は遅れている。 欧州の公共機関や規制産業を中心に、中核デジタルサービスを域内で直接統制しようとするいわゆる「クラウド主権」の動きが鮮明になっている。米国技術への依存を減らし、データとインフラに対する統制権を確保しようとする試みだ。ただ、既存システムの移行障壁と米国ビッグテックの市場支配力が絡み合い、実際の移行実績はなかなか増えていない。 23日に業界関係者によると、ドナルド・トランプ米大統領の再登板以降、一部の技術アクセス制限やサービス障害が相次ぎ、欧州の政策当局や企業の警戒感が一段と高まった。国際刑事裁判所（ICC）がMicrosoft（MS）のサービスへのアクセス権を一時的に失った事件や、人工知能（AI）モデルの輸出規制などが、調達基準の変化を早めた契機として挙げられる。 最も象徴的な事例は欧州連合（EU）委員会の発注だ。欧州委員会は4月、最大1億8,000万ユーロ（約310億円）規模のソブリンクラウド契約4件を、ルクセンブルクのPost TelecomとベルギーのProximusが率いる企業連合、ドイツのStackIT、フランスのScalewayなどに割り当てた。オランダ政府もStackITと基本契約を締結し、非欧州サプライヤーへの依存度を下げる方針を打ち出した。デンマーク国鉄（DSB）、スイス連邦機関、ドイツ公共放送なども最近の調達で、特定サプライヤーや域外管轄権への依存を減らすためのデジタル主権要件を導入した。 需要指標も急ピッチで動いている。Deutsche Telekom子会社のT-Systemsは、2025年半ば以降、自社ソブリンクラウドの需要が4倍以上に増えたと明らかにした。MS 365の自社ホスティング代替を開発するNextcloudは、トランプ第2期発足以降、需要が約5倍に増えたと伝えた。ドイツ最大のホスティング・クラウド事業者IONOSのマルクス・ノガ最高技術責任者（CTO）は「真の価値は外部の『キルスイッチ』に左右されず、運用を無期限に継続できることにある」と述べた。 問題は、関心が実際の移行につながらない点だ。欧州委員会が6月に公表した「クラウド・AI開発法」草案によると、EU域内クラウド事業者の市場シェアは2017年の29%から2022年に15%へ落ちた後、停滞状態にある。一方、Amazon Web Services（AWS）、Microsoft Azure、Google Cloudの米国3社は依然として欧州クラウド市場の70%以上を占めている。 区分 2017年 2022年以降 EU域内クラウド事業者シェア 29% 15%（停滞） 米国3社（AWS・Azure・Google）シェア - 70%以上 注：欧州委員会「クラウド・AI開発法」草案（6月）基準 足かせは「ロックイン（囲い込み）」効果だ。IONOSのマーク・ノイフルト公共部門戦略担当は、公共部門の議論のうち実際の契約につながる割合は一桁にとどまるとし、移行懸念でプロジェクトが12～24カ月ずつ遅れることが頻繁にあると説明した。Nextcloudのフランク・カリチェク最高経営責任者（CEO）は「多くが変化を嫌い、移行プロジェクトを恐れている」と指摘した。相当数の組織がMS OfficeやMS 365、既存クラウドインフラに深く縛られているという意味だ。 米国ビッグテックも手をこまねいてはいない。AWSは10月、自社の「欧州ソブリンクラウド」がEU域外インフラと独立して運用できることを実証するテストを終えた。MSはフランスの「Blue」、ドイツの「Delos Cloud」など現地パートナーが運営する事業を前面に押し出した。Google CloudはThalesと設立した合弁会社「S3NS」がフランスのセキュリティ認証（SecNumCloud）を取得し、欧州委員会の1億8,000万ユーロ事業者に選定されたこともある。Googleは公共入札で、データ保存場所よりも運用の自律性、暗号鍵の統制、クラウドからの退出（エグジット）条項が評価項目として浮上していると説明した。 規制環境もこの流れを後押しする。金融会社の技術リスク基準を定めたEUデジタル運用強靭性法（DORA）とネットワーク・情報セキュリティ指令（NIS2）の施行により、顧客がデータやクラウド運用、中核技術インフラを誰が統制するかをより厳格に問うようになったというのがGoogleの分析だ。 ただ、業界内でも米国プラットフォームとの完全な決別は短期間では難しいとの見方が優勢だ。T-Systemsのクリスティーネ・クナックフスニコリッチ最高主権責任者は「大企業がすべての業務を移すのは現実的でなく、機密データだけを移すのが適切だ」と述べた。スイス金融ソフトウェア企業Temenosは、国際営業を行う大手銀行にはソブリンクラウドはまだ成熟していないと評価した。フィンランドのソフトウェア・機器企業Jollaのサミ・ピエニマキCEOは「欧州にはパズルのピースがほぼ揃っているが、一般の欧州人はもちろん政策担当者でさえ、それを一目で合わせて見るのは難しい」と皮肉った。 市場では、今回の流れがクラウドインフラの地図を短期間で覆すというより、機密データ中心の「二重構造」を強固にする可能性が大きいとの観測が出ている。公共・金融・国防など規制感度の高い領域では域内事業者と米国ビッグテックの現地化サービスが競合し、汎用業務ワークロードは既存ハイパースケーラーが引き続き担う構図だ。EUのクラウド・AI開発法がどのような調達基準として具体化されるかが、今後のシェア情勢を左右する変数として挙げられる。

records.title: Applied Digital (NASDAQ: APLD) Carries Debt At 159% Of Market Cap Despite $36 Billion In Contracted Revenue
records.excerpt: Buried inside one of the steepest stock slides of 2026 is a company sitting on tens of billions in signed tenant commitments. Buried inside one of the steepest stock slides of 2026 is a company sitting on tens of billions in signed tenant commitments. Applied Digital (NASDAQ: APLD), which constructs and operates AI data centers, has accumulated total debt equal to 159.1% of its current market value, compared with just 20.3% for the average S&P 500 constituent. The debt load is not the only pressure point: the company’s free cash flow ran to negative $4.5 billion over the twelve months ended August 31, 2026, as construction spending vastly outpaced what operations returned. Yet the business is growing at a pace that few companies of any size can match, with revenue expanding an average of 138.2% annually across the last three twelve-month periods, against 6.5% for the broader index. The clearest sign of commercial traction came on the October 7, 2026 earnings call, when management disclosed roughly $36 billion in contracted revenue spread across five campuses under signed leases. A single Tier 1 investment-grade hyperscaler has committed to all three of the company’s next campuses, Polaris Forge 3, Delta Forge 1, and Delta Forge 2, on 15-year take-or-pay terms that require payment whether or not the tenant uses the space. That contract structure gives Applied Digital years of visibility, but it has not stopped the stock from losing 70.9% between May 21 and November 19, 2026, while the S&P 500 declined just 3.1% over the same stretch. Part of the investor skepticism likely traces to the composition of reported revenue: in the quarter ended August 31, 2026, the company’s high-performance computing hosting segment generated $262.6 million in total revenue, but only $65.8 million of that came from base rent. The largest slice, $183.5 million, reflected tenant fit-out services, essentially the one-time work of equipping space for incoming customers, with the remaining $13.3 million drawn from tenant recoveries. The operating margin for the twelve months to August 31 sat at negative 28.6%, a stark contrast to the 18.9% margin the S&P 500 posted over the same period. At its November 19 closing price of $13.98, the stock traded at 4.8 times trailing sales versus 3.1 times for the index, suggesting the market is still pricing in future contracted rent rather than current profitability. Management offered one partial comfort on the debt timeline, noting that more than 80% of outstanding obligations do not mature until fiscal 2031 or beyond, giving the company a multi-year runway before principal repayments become acute. A potential near-term catalyst is the expected signing of approximately 250 megawatts of expansion leases before the end of calendar 2026, with management indicating those deals would be priced materially higher than earlier agreements. Applied Digital is also targeting more than 600 megawatts of new capacity entering service over the next twelve months, more than double the 250 megawatts it brought online in the preceding year. Investors waiting for confirmation of the expansion lease signings and a clearer split between base rent and fit-out revenue will likely look to the January 2027 earnings report as the next decisive data point. records.title: Le Plan pour un Canada plus fort : Répercussions de la nouvelle stratégie de sécurité nationale sur l’investissement étranger
records.excerpt: Title: Le Plan pour un Canada plus fort : Répercussions de la nouvelle stratégie de sécurité nationale sur l’investissement étranger | JD Supra URL Source: http://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/le-plan-pour-un-canada-plus-fort-9224985/ Final URL: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/le-plan-pour-un-canada-plus-fort-9224985/ Markdown Content: En octobre 2026, le gouvernement fédéral (le « gouvernement ») a publié le [_Plan pour un Canada plus fort – La sécurité nationale pour les Canadiens et les Canadiennes_](https://www.canada.ca/fr/conseil-prive/services/publications/plan-canada-plus-fort/securite-nationale-canadiens-canadiennes.html) (le « Plan »), soit la première politique fédérale en matière de sécurité nationale depuis plus de 20 ans. Fait à noter pour les entreprises et les investisseurs, le Plan « commence, délibérément, par la sécurité économique », qualifiant celle-ci de « facteur primordial » dans les décisions du gouvernement qui concernent l’investissement étranger. Le Plan renforce également le rôle croissant que joue la sécurité nationale dans l’examen des investissements étrangers au Canada et met en lumière les secteurs susceptibles de faire l’objet d’une surveillance accrue. ## **Principaux points à retenir** * **Pleins feux sur les secteurs essentiels.** Le Plan présente huit capacités stratégiques : les nouvelles technologies, les minéraux critiques, la défense, l’énergie, les transports, les produits pharmaceutiques et les biotechnologies, la sécurité alimentaire, ainsi que les paiements, le règlement et l’investissement (collectivement, les « capacités stratégiques »). La protection et le renforcement de ces capacités orienteront expressément la prise de décisions par le gouvernement. * **Importance accrue de la sécurité économique dans l’examen des investissements étrangers.** Le gouvernement envisage de moderniser sa trousse d’outils en matière de sécurité économique, notamment au moyen d’« outils d’application de la loi améliorés », afin de protéger le Canada contre les activités économiques étrangères hostiles. Des propositions visant à moderniser la législation relative à la sécurité nationale seront également présentées au cours de la première année du Plan. * **Ouverture du Canada à l’investissement étranger.** Le Plan met l’accent sur l’investissement, la croissance économique et les partenariats avec des alliés fiables, ce qui comprend une « relation avec les États-Unis axée sur la collaboration et la lucidité », tout en cherchant à renforcer la sécurité économique du Canada et sa résilience dans les secteurs stratégiques. * **Évaluation du risque relatif à la sécurité nationale tôt dans la planification d’une opération.**Les investisseurs étrangers, notamment ceux qui investissent dans les capacités stratégiques, devraient évaluer le risque relatif à la sécurité nationale que présentent leurs opérations envisagées au Canada, et ce, bien avant la clôture de l’opération, et envisager la possibilité de communiquer de manière proactive avec le gouvernement, ou encore de mettre en place des mesures d’atténuation. ## **Au-devant de la scène : la sécurité nationale** Le Plan officialise une transition déjà bien en cours sous le régime de la _Loi sur Investissement Canada_ (la « LIC »). Depuis l’exercice 2020-2021, 76 examens complets relatifs à la sécurité nationale en vertu de la LIC ont été effectués, soit plus que le double du nombre d’examens relatifs à l’avantage net (34). Les investissements dans les minéraux critiques, les technologies, les télécommunications et les infrastructures essentielles ont suscité une attention particulière. Le Plan indique que ces domaines continueront d’être visés par le régime d’examen relatif à la sécurité nationale et que ce dernier pourrait s’étendre à des domaines qui, par le passé, faisaient l’objet d’une attention moindre dans le cadre de tels examens, comme la sécurité alimentaire, les produits pharmaceutiques et les systèmes financiers. Cette attention davantage focalisée sur la sécurité nationale est particulièrement pertinente compte tenu des modifications à la LIC à venir qui, une fois entrées en vigueur, imposeront une obligation de dépôt préalable à la clôture pour certains investissements dans des secteurs sensibles visés, quelle que soit la taille de l’opération. Bien que la liste des secteurs sensibles n’ait pas encore été publiée, les capacités stratégiques précisées dans le Plan, ainsi que la[Liste de technologies sensibles](https://www.canada.ca/fr/services/defense/securitenationale/liste-technologies-sensibles.html), la[liste des minéraux critiques](https://www.canada.ca/fr/campagne/mineraux-critiques-au-canada/les-mineraux-critiques-une-occasion-pour-le-canada.html) et la[Stratégie nationale sur les infrastructures essentielles](https://www.securitepublique.gc.ca/cnt/rsrcs/pblctns/srtg-crtcl-nfrstrctr/index-fr.aspx), pourraient servir d’indicateurs quant à sa portée. ## **Ouverture à l’investissement, sous l’angle de la sécurité nationale** Une surveillance accrue ne signifie pas que le Canada ferme la porte à l’investissement étranger. Récemment, le gouvernement a déployé des efforts en vue d’attirer et de diversifier les investissements étrangers, notamment en tenant la première édition du Sommet canadien de l’investissement, ainsi qu’en élargissant ses relations économiques avec la Chine, les Émirats arabes unis et d’autres pays. Pour en savoir davantage, consultez nos _Bulletins Blake_ s intitulés[_Le Sommet canadien de l’investissement signale de nouvelles occasions pour les entreprises_](https://www.blakes.com/fr-ca/perspectives/le-sommet-canadien-de-l-investissement-signale-de-nouvelles-occasions-pour-les-entreprises/) et[_Le Canada ouvre la porte à de plus grands investissements en provenance de la Chine et d’autres pays_](https://www.blakes.com/fr-ca/perspectives/le-canada-ouvre-la-porte-a-de-plus-grands-investissements-en-provenance-de-la-chine-et-d-autres-pays/). Le Plan prévoit des partenariats visant à renforcer la position du Canada dans des secteurs stratégiques, ainsi qu’à agrandir sa participation dans ces derniers, mais les investissements touchant les technologies sensibles, les infrastructures, les chaînes d’approvisionnement et les données seront susceptibles de faire l’objet d’une surveillance accrue. Or, une telle surveillance accrue ne se traduit pas nécessairement par une interdiction : des engagements ont été utilisés pour répondre à des préoccupations en matière de sécurité nationale dans six des 16 examens relatifs à la sécurité nationale menés en 2024-2025, même si le pouvoir exprès d’accepter ces engagements n’est entré en vigueur qu’au cours de la même année. ## **Enjeux plus vastes en matière de concurrence** Le Plan n’aborde pas directement le régime de la _Loi sur la concurrence_. Cependant, l’importance qu’il accorde aux capacités et à la résilience du pays, ainsi qu’à la participation canadienne aux opérations, vient s’ajouter aux débats sur l’harmonisation de la mise en application des lois relatives à la concurrence avec les objectifs du Canada en matière de productivité et de sécurité économique, notamment dans les secteurs stratégiques. Par exemple, le Plan prévoit de renforcer la sécurité alimentaire au moyen de la[Stratégie nationale de sécurité alimentaire](https://agriculture.canada.ca/fr/ministere/initiatives/strategie-nationale-securite-alimentaire), ce qui coïncide avec l’[examen](https://bureau-concurrence.canada.ca/fr/comment-nous-favorisons-concurrence/avis-derriere-letiquette-prix-examen-chaine-dapprovisionnement-alimentaire) en cours de la chaîne d’approvisionnement alimentaire canadienne, mené par le Bureau de la concurrence. Par conséquent, les parties à des acquisitions, à des coentreprises et à des collaborations stratégiques, devraient continuer à évaluer les risques liés à la concurrence tout en tenant compte des considérations en matière de sécurité nationale. ## **Répercussions pour les entreprises** Le risque relat

records.title: México tiene dos océanos, pero su economía azul representa menos del 0.5% del PIB: UNAM
records.excerpt: Especialistas advierten que el país desaprovecha sus recursos marítimos y proponen impulsar la industria naval, la biotecnología y las energías oceánicas para generar empleos. México cuenta con una posición geográfica privilegiada entre los océanos Atlántico y Pacífico, además de una amplia diversidad de ecosistemas costeros. Sin embargo, esta riqueza natural no se ha traducido en un desarrollo económico proporcional a su potencial, advirtieron especialistas de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM). De acuerdo con Clemente Ruiz Durán, profesor de posgrado e investigador de la Facultad de Economía de la UNAM, la llamada economía azul representa menos del 0.5% de la economía nacional, pese a las oportunidades que ofrecen los recursos marítimos para diversificar la producción, desarrollar nuevas industrias y generar empleos. Durante el Seminario Internacional "Hacia un nuevo paradigma productivo para la Economía Azul en México", el académico planteó la necesidad de incorporar estas actividades a la política industrial del país, mediante inversiones en infraestructura, innovación tecnológica y aprovechamiento sustentable de los recursos oceánicos. Lorena Rodríguez León, directora de la Facultad de Economía de la UNAM, señaló que las ventajas geográficas y la diversidad de ecosistemas costeros de México no se han aprovechado suficientemente para impulsar el crecimiento económico. "La transición hacia una economía más sustentable debe representar también una oportunidad para fortificar nuestra estructura productiva, desarrollar nuevas capacidades tecnológicas y generar mejores condiciones de bienestar para la población", afirmó. La especialista consideró necesario fortalecer las capacidades productivas locales, incrementar la innovación tecnológica y vincular las cadenas de valor, sin descuidar la conservación de los ecosistemas. Asimismo, destacó que la colaboración entre instituciones académicas, autoridades e industrias puede contribuir al diseño de políticas industriales que permitan aprovechar los recursos marítimos y generar nuevas oportunidades económicas. Para revertir la limitada participación de la economía azul, Ruiz Durán propuso diversificar las actividades productivas relacionadas con los mares, particularmente mediante el fortalecimiento de sectores industriales y tecnológicos. Entre las oportunidades identificadas por el investigador destacan la construcción de astilleros, la fabricación de embarcaciones de grandes dimensiones y el desarrollo de componentes electrónicos y tecnologías marinas. También planteó incentivar la pesca, la acuicultura, la biotecnología marina y las energías oceánicas, actividades que podrían contribuir a ampliar la estructura productiva nacional. En particular, destacó las posibilidades de la biotecnología marina para desarrollar medicamentos, tratamientos y nuevos alimentos, mediante el aprovechamiento de los recursos oceánicos y el fortalecimiento de la investigación científica. El académico señaló que estas actividades representan una oportunidad para generar nuevas cadenas productivas y aprovechar recursos que actualmente tienen una participación reducida dentro de la política industrial mexicana. El desarrollo de nuevas industrias marítimas también podría tener efectos positivos en las economías de los estados costeros, especialmente en regiones donde existen necesidades de generación de empleo. Ruiz Durán identificó a Oaxaca y Chiapas como entidades que podrían beneficiarse del fortalecimiento de la economía azul, mediante la creación de fuentes laborales y nuevas actividades productivas. De acuerdo con el especialista, estas oportunidades permitirían incorporar a sectores de la población que actualmente trabajan en la informalidad, al tiempo que contribuirían a diversificar las economías regionales. En ese sentido, consideró que el aprovechamiento de los recursos marítimos debe acompañarse de estrategias que fortalezcan las capacidades productivas y tecnológicas de las comunidades costeras. El investigador de la UNAM señaló que México puede tomar como referencia las experiencias de países que han desarrollado industrias vinculadas con el aprovechamiento de los océanos. Entre ellos mencionó a Corea del Sur, China y Japón, naciones que han consolidado sectores de construcción naval, infraestructura portuaria y tecnologías relacionadas con las actividades marítimas. También destacó el caso de Noruega, que ha ampliado su participación en el sector energético mediante el desarrollo de energía eólica marina y servicios técnicos especializados. Estas experiencias, explicó, muestran las posibilidades de incorporar los recursos marítimos a las estrategias de desarrollo industrial y tecnológico. Por su parte, Luis Godoy Rueda, representante de Open Society Foundations, destacó la importancia de analizar el potencial de la economía azul en el contexto del regreso de la política industrial a la agenda nacional, particularmente a partir del Plan México. Consideró que las estrategias para desarrollar estas actividades deben vincularse con la política comercial, las cadenas regionales de valor y los objetivos de transición verde. Los especialistas coincidieron en la necesidad de fortalecer las capacidades productivas y tecnológicas del país para que el aprovechamiento de los recursos marítimos contribuya tanto al crecimiento económico como a la conservación ambiental. De esta manera, la economía azul se presenta como una oportunidad para diversificar la industria mexicana, impulsar nuevas actividades económicas y generar empleos en las regiones costeras, mediante un modelo que combine desarrollo productivo y sustentabilidad.

records.title: Vivienda representa 5.5% del PIB en México, pero 27.5% de los hogares depende de pagar renta o tener prestada una propiedad
records.excerpt: La Alianza por la Justicia Fiscal plantea tasas a la acumulación inmobiliaria y cobros coactivos para financiar infraestructura y vivienda El sector de la vivienda en México genera el 5.5% del PIB nacional mientras el 27.5% de los hogares carece de inmueble propio, según registros del Instituto Nacional de Estadísitca y Geografía (INEGI) y la organización Alianza por la Justicia Fiscal ante un rezago habitacional de 8.2 millones de propiedades. En contraste con la actividad económica del ramo, los municipios del país recaudan más de 84 mil millones de pesos por gravámenes inmobiliarios como predial y traslación de dominio, monto que quintuplica los 16 mil 855 millones de pesos ejercidos por el Gobierno federal en vivienda social durante 2025. La Alianza por la Justicia Fiscal documenta que los fondos federales para vivienda social apenas alcanzaron una ejecución del 52% frente a los 32 mil millones de pesos aprobados originalmente, concentrando el 42.3% del gasto en el Estado de México, Hidalgo y Chiapas. El PIB habitacional crece 4.4% impulsado por la autoconstrucción La Cuenta Satélite de Vivienda de México 2025 del INEGI reporta que el sector habitacional generó 1 billón 859 mil 806 millones de pesos corrientes. Esta cifra representó un crecimiento real de 4.4% respecto a 2024, un avance superior al 0.6% registrado por la economía nacional. La autoproducción de los hogares aportó el 56.8% del producto interno bruto del sector de la vivienda, seguida del alquiler efectivo con 22.7% y la producción de unidades económicas con 7.2%, de acuerdo con el clasificador funcional del instituto estadístico. El rubro de la construcción representó el 68.5% del valor sectorial bajo la clasificación industrial, mientras los servicios inmobiliarios y de alquiler abarcaron el 25.8%. Las actividades financieras y de seguros vinculadas a los inmuebles completaron el 4.3% restante. El instituto de estadística contabilizó 2, 368,290 puestos de trabajo en el ramo durante 2025, equivalentes al 5.8% del empleo nacional. El personal ocupado en actividades de vivienda creció 3.3% anual, a pesar de que el empleo total del país retrocedió 0.6%. Al sumar el alquiler imputado de 2 billones 011 mil 623 millones de pesos —el costo teórico que pagarían los propietarios por rentar sus casas—, el valor total de la vivienda alcanzó 3,871,429 millones de pesos corrientes. Ese monto equivale al 11.5% de toda la economía mexicana. México enfrenta déficit de 8.2 millones de casas y renta absorbe ingresos Frente a las cifras del INEGI, el informe de la Alianza por la Justicia Fiscal advierte que México enfrenta un déficit de 8.2 millones de viviendas, según la Encuesta Nacional de Vivienda. El 27.5% de las familias mexicanas reside en inmuebles rentados o prestados. La Secretaría de Desarrollo Agrario, Territorial y Urbano (SEDATU) estima que el 80% del déficit habitacional responde a necesidades de mejoramiento y ampliación, mientras el 20% restante demanda construcciones nuevas. Además, 10.3 millones de personas padecen carencias por espacios y materiales en sus domicilios. El informe documenta que 5.8 millones de hogares alquilaban su residencia en 2020, con apenas 54% respaldado por un contrato formal. En 18 estados, más de la mitad de los inquilinos renta debido a la falta de créditos o recursos económicos para adquirir una vivienda. Las rentas presentan una alta concentración patrimonial. El decil con mayores ingresos acapara el 53% de las rentas del país, mientras que en la Ciudad de México los hogares del 10% más pobre destinan hasta el 60% de sus ingresos al pago de alquiler. La brecha de tenencia afecta a las mujeres jóvenes. En la capital del país, 79% de los hogares dirigidos por mujeres de 30 años o menos paga renta, frente al 65% de los hogares encabezados por varones del mismo rango de edad. La producción de vivienda económica cae por debajo del 1% Entre 2020 y abril de 2026 el país edificó 888 mil 503 viviendas, pero únicamente el 0.41% correspondió a vivienda económica con precio menor a 420 mil pesos. Si se añade la vivienda popular, la cifra alcanza apenas el 10.2% de la producción total. El reporte subraya que los precios de las casas se triplicaron mientras los salarios permanecen estancados. La salida del Infonavit de la construcción directa para operar exclusivamente créditos redujo la oferta asequible y marginó a los trabajadores sin empleo formal. El 90.5% de la riqueza de las familias en México reside en bienes raíces. La concentración inmobiliaria y el auge del alojamiento temporal restringen la oferta habitacional permanente y aceleran el encarecimiento de los alquileres en áreas urbanas centrales. Los municipios captan 0.3% del PIB en gravámenes inmobiliarios Los impuestos a la propiedad representan 0.3% del PIB en México, por debajo del 1.6% en Colombia y 1.3% en Chile. El impuesto predial recaudó 0.11% del PIB en 2022, el nivel más bajo registrado entre 13 países de América Latina. records.title: Banco de México bajó la tasa de interés a 6.25%: cómo puede afectar los créditos, las tarjetas y los ahorros
records.excerpt: El recorte de 25 puntos base entró en vigor el 6 de noviembre y puede influir en el costo del financiamiento y el rendimiento de los ahorros. El Banco de México (Banxico) redujo su tasa de interés de referencia de 6.50% a 6.25%, una decisión que entró en vigor el 6 de noviembre de 2026. El ajuste fue de 25 puntos base y se aprobó por mayoría de la Junta de Gobierno del banco central, según el comunicado de política monetaria publicado el 5 de noviembre. La medida puede tener efectos en distintos productos financieros que utilizan las familias mexicanas, como los créditos, las tarjetas de crédito y las cuentas de ahorro. La tasa de referencia de Banxico funciona como un indicador para el costo del dinero en la economía. Cuando disminuye, puede favorecer una reducción de las tasas de algunos financiamientos, aunque el efecto depende de las condiciones de cada producto y de las decisiones de los bancos. En los créditos con tasa variable, una disminución de las tasas de referencia puede reflejarse en un menor costo financiero cuando las condiciones contractuales contemplan ese ajuste. En cambio, los préstamos con tasa fija mantienen las condiciones pactadas durante el periodo establecido. Por eso, quienes tienen un crédito vigente deben revisar su contrato antes de asumir que pagarán menos. La reducción de la tasa de referencia también puede influir en los rendimientos que ofrecen los bancos y otros instrumentos de ahorro e inversión. Cuando las tasas bajan, ahorrar en productos vinculados a ellas puede resultar menos atractivo, ya que los rendimientos ofrecidos pueden disminuir. Esto no significa que todas las cuentas bancarias vayan a pagar menos intereses de inmediato. El efecto dependerá del tipo de producto contratado, sus condiciones y la institución financiera. Para entender cómo puede repercutir el movimiento de Banxico en las finanzas personales, estos son los principales puntos: La decisión de Banxico se tomó después de evaluar el comportamiento de la inflación y la actividad económica. En su comunicado, el banco central señaló que la inflación general pasó de 3.42% a 3.62% entre la primera quincena de septiembre y la primera de octubre, mientras que la inflación subyacente bajó ligeramente de 3.79% a 3.78%. Además, anticipó que la inflación general convergería a su meta en el cuarto trimestre de 2027.

records.label: mvsnoticias.com
records.title: Cultura aporta 2.7% del PIB de México y genera 1.3 millones de empleos
records.excerpt: Los conciertos y espectáculos musicales encabezan el crecimiento de las industrias culturales, mientras que las actividades digitales ganan terreno. La cultura mexicana no solo es una expresión de identidad, tradición y creatividad. También representa una actividad económica de gran relevancia. En México, las industrias culturales aportan el 2.7% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) y generan alrededor de 1.3 millones de empleos, una dimensión comparable con la del sector minero-metalúrgico. Así lo explicó el periodista y analista económico Luis Miguel González, durante una conversación con Ana Francisca Vega en MVS Noticias, en la que examinó las cifras del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (Inegi) sobre el comportamiento de la economía cultural. “Cuando decimos 2.7% del PIB, solo como contexto, es lo mismo que aporta el sector minero-metalúrgico. De ese tamaño es”, señaló. La comparación permite dimensionar una actividad que suele quedar relegada en las discusiones económicas, pese a que comprende desde las bellas artes y las artesanías hasta los medios de comunicación, el diseño y los servicios digitales. Los conciertos impulsan el crecimiento cultural Uno de los datos más llamativos es el dinamismo de los espectáculos musicales. De acuerdo con las cifras comentadas por González, los conciertos y las presentaciones de música registraron un crecimiento del 12%, convirtiéndose en una de las actividades de mayor expansión dentro del sector. El fenómeno refleja la creciente oferta de espectáculos en el país y la actividad económica que generan a su alrededor: producción, contratación de personal, servicios técnicos y organización de eventos. “Cuando uno ve la oferta cultural, la cantidad de conciertos que hay, entiende que aparezca como tan dinámico”, explicó el periodista. El segundo ámbito de mayor crecimiento corresponde a los servicios relacionados con internet, el desarrollo de software y otras actividades digitales. Esta transformación ha ampliado los límites tradicionales de lo que se entiende por cultura. Un diseñador gráfico que desarrolla contenidos para una plataforma digital, participa en la creación de software o elabora la imagen de un concierto forma parte de una misma economía creativa. Las artesanías, el sector que más empleo genera Aunque la tecnología y los espectáculos concentran buena parte del crecimiento, las artesanías continúan siendo la actividad que más personas emplea dentro del sector cultural. Sin embargo, González advirtió que también se trata de una de sus áreas más vulnerables. “Es un sector muy vulnerable al cambio tecnológico, sigue empleando mucha gente, pero yo diría que es la parte más precaria del PIB cultural”, sostuvo. La diferencia entre las actividades tradicionales y las digitales plantea uno de los principales desafíos para la economía creativa mexicana: cómo aprovechar el crecimiento tecnológico sin dejar atrás a quienes dependen de oficios y expresiones culturales tradicionales. El analista destacó que las herramientas digitales pueden alcanzar mercados masivos y generar una riqueza difícilmente comparable con la producción artesanal individual. Ciudad de México lidera; Quintana Roo sorprende La distribución territorial de la economía cultural también ofrece resultados inesperados. La Ciudad de México ocupa el primer lugar en la producción cultural del país, una posición que refleja su concentración de actividades artísticas, medios de comunicación, espectáculos y servicios creativos. La sorpresa aparece en el segundo puesto: Quintana Roo, por delante de entidades que suelen asociarse con industrias culturales y tecnológicas, como Jalisco. González explicó que la posición del estado caribeño está estrechamente relacionada con el turismo. Los visitantes que llegan a destinos como Cancún y la Riviera Maya no solo consumen servicios de hospedaje y entretenimiento, sino también espectáculos, música y otras experiencias culturales. Esta demanda convierte a la cultura en una actividad complementaria de gran importancia para la economía turística. México, una potencia cultural con margen para crecer A pesar de su riqueza histórica, artística y gastronómica, México no destaca especialmente por el peso de la cultura dentro de su economía cuando se compara con otros países. Según González, la aportación mexicana se encuentra cerca del promedio internacional y no supera de manera significativa la proporción que representan estas actividades en economías como Estados Unidos, España o Brasil. El periodista mencionó el caso del Reino Unido, donde las industrias creativas representan una proporción cercana al 6% del PIB, impulsadas en buena medida por las actividades digitales. La comparación sugiere que México todavía tiene oportunidades para ampliar el valor económico de su creatividad, especialmente mediante el desarrollo tecnológico. Una oportunidad laboral para las nuevas generaciones Más allá de su aportación al PIB, el crecimiento de las industrias culturales plantea una oportunidad para los jóvenes que buscan incorporarse al mercado laboral.

records.excerpt: 【公式】B.革新 | 2026年からの新制度について | B.LEAGUE（Bリーグ）公式サイト Loading.. B.LEAGUE B.LEAGUE B.革新とは 審査基準・結果 参入決定クラブ 選手契約・ドラフト サラリーキャップ制度 ロスター・オンザコート 選手登録制度 ドラフト制度 シーズンの変更点 レギュラーシーズン ポストシーズン よくある質問 B.革新 | B.Innovation | 2026 TIP OFF 5分でわかる B.革新 B.LEAGUEはどう変わる？ 審査基準・結果 のページを更新しました。 2025.11.19[WED] B.LEAGUE ONE / B.LEAGUE NEXTの参入クラブ を公開しました。 2025.10.30[THU] ドラフト制度 のページを更新しました。 2025.3.12[WED] 全てのニュースを見る B.INNOVATION 世界一型破りな ライブスポーツエンタメを目指し B.LEAGUEが変わります 2016年にB.LEAGUEが開幕して以来、リーグとクラブの事業規模は大きく成長しました。 しかし、B.LEAGUEが「バスケで日本を元気に」を実現するため、また、クラブがステークホルダーや地域の皆さまを幸せにできる存在となるためには、クラブが今以上に経営力をつけ、長期的視野で成長のための投資を行うことができる環境を作ることが不可欠です。 そこで、B.LEAGUEは、「強化」「経営」「社会性」の3つの軸に沿って、2026年からリーグ構造の変更を伴う、大きな変革を行います。 B.革新とは OVERVIEW 5分でわかる「B.革新」 B.LEAGUEはどう変わる？ 2026-27シーズンから新たなリーグ構造に生まれ変わります。 2026-27シーズンから新たなリーグ構造となり、競技成績に基づいた昇格・降格が廃止されます。 各ディビジョンに参入するためには厳正なる審査をクリアしなければなりません。 審査には「平均入場者数」「売上高」「ホームアリーナ」等の条件が設けられており、2026-27シーズンに向けて続々と参入クラブが決定しています。 CRITERIA 審査 クラブ・アリーナを軸に地域が発展するための審査基準を設定。財務健全性や経営基盤の安定性を審査基準として強化。クラブごとに運営指針の達成度や将来ビジョンを審査し透明性を確保。B.LEAGUE PREMIERだけではなく、B.LEAGUE ONE、B.LEAGUE NEXTの審査基準を引き上げ。 審査 CLUBS 参入クラブ 参入決定のクラブ一覧。リーグの発展と地域バスケの拡大を目指す。新規参入後の戦力均衡を図り、長期的な競争力を確保。地域振興やファンコミュニティ形成に積極的な取り組みを推奨。 参入クラブ SCHEDULE B.LEAGUE PREMIERでは、これまでのB.LEAGUEのレギュラーシーズンの形式から大きく変わり、ポストシーズンについてもFINALSがHOME/AWAY方式になるなど、大きな変更点が設けられていきます。 レギュラーシーズン B.LEAGUE PREMIERは露出拡大・アリーナ運営・選手コンディション・AWAY観戦のしやすさを鑑み、週末試合と平日試合をバランスよく開催。B.LEAGUE ONE、B.LEAGUE NEXTは現在のB1、B2と同様の形式を採用予定。 レギュラーシーズン ポストシーズン B.LEAGUE PREMIERは現在中央開催されているFINALSを出場クラブのホーム＆アウェーでの開催に変更。 試合数も3戦先勝方式(最大5試合)に変更されます。B.LEAGUE ONEは「広さ」の全国リーグとしてより多くの地区代表クラブが優勝争いを行うことでリーグ全体の盛り上げを狙い、ポストシーズンへの進出クラブ数を16クラブへ拡大。 ポストシーズン PLAYER SYSTEM 新しいB.LEAGUEには、これまでに無かったたくさんの制度が設けられ、よりクラブ同士の実力が均衡するような仕組みが採用されます。 サラリーキャップ制度 クラブ間の財政バランスを保ち、リーグの競争力維持が目的。選手の報酬上限と下限を設け、クラブの健全な財政を推進。最低年俸制度により、安定した選手生活を支援。 サラリーキャップ制度 ロスター・オンザコート 試合出場や登録可能枠の調整で、競技力の強化を目指す。外国籍選手は登録3名、出場はB.PREMIERでオンザコートフリーを実現。帰化/アジア特別枠の出場機会は継続維持しつつも、U22枠やユース育成特別枠といったユース選手、ユース出身選手の活躍機会を拡大。 ロスター・オンザコート 選手登録制度 選手流動性制度の再設計として、B.LEAGUE PREMIER内の移籍を柔軟に行えるルールを導入。また、クラブの意思で当該選手を期限付き移籍させることが可能な「育成契約選手制度」を設けます。 選手登録制度 ドラフト制度 未来のスター選手発掘に向けたドラフト制度を新設。クラブが公平に新人選手を獲得できる仕組みを確立し、指名順位や契約期間、報酬基準についてのルールをまとめました。 ドラフト制度 TOP B.革新とは 審査基準・結果 参入決定クラブ
